en: The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll One, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter One: Turning the Wheel of Dharma. Chapter One: Turning the Wheel of Dharma.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of sixty-two thousand bhikṣus. All were arhats whose outflows were exhausted, who were free from further afflictions, possessed of complete mastery, liberated in mind and liberated by wisdom;

they were like well-trained mahānāgas who had accomplished what was to be done, laid down the heavy burden, attained their own benefit, destroyed the fetters of existence, gained liberation through right knowledge, attained mastery over their minds, and had crossed to the other shore of all mental states—with the sole exception of Ānanda.

There were four million four hundred thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with Maitreya Bodhisattva as their foremost leader; all had attained dhāraṇīs, patience, and meditative concentration, and deeply understood that all phenomena are empty and devoid of fixed conceptions—all such great beings were non-retrogressive.
At that time, furthermore, the Great Brahmā King was accompanied by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Brahmā sons;
the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations was accompanied by his retinue of four million people;

the King of the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations was also accompanied by his retinue of three million five hundred thousand people; and the King of the Tuṣita Heaven was likewise accompanied by his retinue...
Three million beings were present together; likewise, the King of the Yāma Heaven was accompanied by his retinue of three million five hundred thousand beings;
Śakra-devānām-indra, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, was also accompanied by his retinue of four million beings;
Vaiśravaṇa, the King of the Heaven, was also accompanied by a retinue of ten thousand spirits and deities; and Virūḍhaka...
The King [Vaiśravaṇa] was also accompanied by a thousand followers of Kumbhāṇḍas; the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka was also accompanied by a thousand followers of nāgas;
the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra was accompanied by a thousand followers of gandharvas;
and the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda were each also accompanied by a thousand followers.
Together with such a multitude as these, all have already resolved their minds toward the Mahāyāna and have practiced the six *pāramitās*.

At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded by his retinue, expounded the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly: to eliminate the four inversions, to give rise to the light of wholesome dharmas, to obtain the radiance of wisdom, and to comprehend the Four Noble Truths; desiring that the bodhisattvas of future ages may enter samādhi, and having entered samādhi, surpass the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, never regressing from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva, Avidyādṛṣṭi Bodhisattva, Varuṇadeva Bodhisattva, Siṃhamati Bodhisattva, Sūryaprabha Bodhisattva, and ten thousand other such chief Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence toward the southeast, looked up with single-minded joy and veneration, saying:
"Homage to the Lotus-Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!"
Homage to the Lotus Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha! How rare it is, World-Honored One,

that not long after attaining anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, you have been able to manifest various and immeasurable transformations of supernatural power, enabling immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings to plant roots of goodness and become non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Ratnasūryaprabha, who rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O Maitreya Bodhisattva!"
O Bodhisattva Vigatamoha-darśana!
O Bodhisattva Varuṇadeva! O Bodhisattva Siṃhamati!
“Sūryaprabha Bodhisattva!
For what reason did these ten thousand leading bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and their retinue abandon listening to the Dharma,

rise from their seats, bare their right shoulders, place their right knees upon the ground, join their palms in reverence toward the southeastern direction, and with single-minded joy speak these words?”
"Namo to the Lotus Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
Namo to the Lotus Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!"
"How rare, World-Honored One!

Having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you have not long been able to manifest various and immeasurable transformations of supernatural power (*ṛddhi-vidhi*), causing immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of sentient beings to plant roots of goodness."
"World-Honored One!
How far is that Buddha Padmottara from here?
How much time has passed since that Buddha attained enlightenment?"
What is the name of that land,
and by what means is it adorned?
For what reason does the Buddha Padmottara manifest such various transformations?
In the worlds of the ten directions, all Buddhas manifest various and immeasurable transformations; while some bodhisattvas are able to behold them, why am I alone unable to see them?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Jewel Sun Radiance:
"Excellent, son of good family! Well said!"
Excellent! That which you have asked is itself a treasure, it is itself noble and good, it is itself eloquent, and it is itself a skillful question, O son of good family!

You are able to inquire of the Tathāgata about such a profound and wondrous meaning because you wish to teach and transform immeasurable billions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to plant roots of goodness, and because you wish to manifest the various adornments of the Lotus Honored One’s realm.
"Good son! I shall now speak; listen attentively!
Listen attentively!"
"Reflect upon this well; receive and uphold it well.
The Bodhisattva Ratnārcis, with a single-minded joy, accepted the instruction and listened.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ratnārcis:
“Good son! One hundred million times ten thousand Buddha-lands away from here toward the southeast, there is a Buddha-world named Lotus.

It is adorned with various kinds of ornaments, strewn with all manner of famous flowers, and its fragrance permeates everywhere. Adorned with jewel-trees and various precious mountains, its ground is made of deep blue lapis lazuli. Immeasurable bodhisattvas fill that land, and the sublime sounds of the Good Dharma are heard everywhere.”

The ground is as soft as celestial raiment; when one walks, the feet sink into it four inches, and upon lifting them, it returns to its natural state, whereupon various lotus flowers spontaneously arise.
The trees made of the seven treasures were seven yojanas in height, and their branches naturally suspended celestial *kāṣāya* robes.

In that Buddha-world, the sounds of various celestial musical instruments were constantly heard; from the voices of those birds, there constantly issued forth the sublime Dharma-sounds of the faculties (*indriya*), powers (*bala*), and factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*).
When the branches and leaves of the trees brushed against one another, they produced sounds that surpassed the five kinds of music of the devas and humans.
The fragrance emanating from the roots of each tree surpasses all celestial perfumes, and its scent pervades more than a thousand yojanas.
Between the trees hang celestial garlands.
There was a seven-jeweled tower, five hundred yojanas in height, one hundred yojanas in length and breadth, with railings all around made of the seven jewels.

On the four sides of that tower there are great pools of water, eighty yojanas long and fifty yojanas wide. On the four sides of these pools are exquisite stairways made entirely of the seven precious gems. Within the waters of these pools are blue utpala flowers, red kumuda flowers, pink padma flowers, and white puṇḍarīka flowers; each individual lotus flower is exactly one yojana in length and breadth.
During the first watch of the night, there were bodhisattvas who, having arisen upon the flower pedestals, sat cross-legged and experienced the blissful joy of liberation.

When the night had passed, winds arose from the four directions—soft, fragrant, and pure—which touched the bodies of the bodhisattvas; these winds caused the closed flowers to bloom and blew them, scattering them across the ground.

At that time, the Bodhisattva arose from samādhi and again experienced the joy and bliss of liberation; descending from the lotus pedestal, he ascended a high tower and sat cross-legged upon a seat made of the seven precious gems to listen to and receive the sublime Dharma.

Surrounding the perimeter of that garden on all four sides were mountains of Jambūnada and purple-golden *kāñcana*, twenty *yojanas* in height and exactly three *yojanas* in length and breadth. These mountains were interspersed with countless hundreds of thousands of precious gems, deep-blue lapis lazuli beads, and the brilliance of fire-pearls.

At that time, the Buddha Padmottara, through a great radiance combined with the brilliance of various jewels, illuminated his buddha-world in unison. The light of that land was subtle and supreme, being the foremost; there were neither sun nor moon, nor day nor night, and the passage of seasons was known by the closing of flowers and the roosting of birds.
Upon that mountain of jewels is a magnificent terrace of deep blue lapis lazuli, sixty yojanas in height and twenty yojanas in length and breadth.

The terrace is surrounded on all four sides by railings made of the seven precious substances. In the center of the terrace is a bed made of the seven precious substances, upon which sits a bodhisattva in his final birth to listen to and receive the Dharma.

“Good son! In that Buddha-world there is a bodhi tree named Indrā, three thousand yojanas in height; its trunk is five hundred yojanas in circumference and breadth, and its branches and foliage are one thousand yojanas in circumference and breadth.”
Below there are lotus flowers with stems of lapis lazuli five hundred yojanas in height.

Each flower has one billion, one hundred thousand golden petals five yojanas in height; the calyxes are made of agate and the filaments of the seven precious gems, ten yojanas in height, and they are exactly seven yojanas in length and breadth.
At that time, the Buddha Padmottama sat upon this flower and attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* during the previous night.
Surrounding his bodhi-flower seat were various kinds of lotus flowers, upon which various bodhisattvas each sat, beholding the manifold transformations of the Buddha Padmottama.
At that time, after the World-Honored One Śākyamuni had spoken these matters, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jewel-Sun Radiance addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
“By what marks and characteristics does the Buddha Padmottara manifest his various transformations?
We pray that you will explain this.
The Buddha told Ratnārcisprabha:

“Good son! Last night, the Buddha Padmottara attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*). Having passed the night, that Buddha manifested various transformations of supernatural power (*ṛddhi-vidhi*)."

His body manifested transformations as far as the Brahma Heaven; from the mark of the fleshly protuberance on his crown, he emitted sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of rays of light, illuminating Buddha-worlds in the zenith as numerous as the atoms of dust.

At that time, the bodhisattvas from the upper direction did not observe the forms perceived by the eyes in the lower direction—namely, the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains and the various small mountains—but observed only the worlds reached by the Buddha’s light.

In various worlds, there are bodhisattvas who receive the prediction of enlightenment (vyākaraṇa), whether they have attained dhāraṇīs, the samādhi of patience (kṣānti), or have reached the high station of being in their final birth before buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha).
All the radiance belonging to these bodhisattvas and others was completely eclipsed by the light of the Buddha.
Thus, this multitude joined their palms toward the Honored Buddha Padmottara and gazed up at his venerable countenance.

At that time, he saw only his body adorned with the thirty-two marks and the eighty minor characteristics arranged in succession; he saw the Buddha Padmottara and the various adornments of his world. Having seen this, his heart was filled with joy.

At that time, within as many Buddha-worlds as there are motes of dust, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, having beheld the light-transformations and the world of the Buddha Padmottara, each abandoned their own lands and, by means of their supernatural powers, all set out together to go to where that Buddha was, to prostrate, circumambulate, make offerings, pay respect, honor, and praise him.

“Good son! At that time, those Buddhas saw the various bodhisattvas manifest their tongue-phenomena, which completely covered all sentient beings—whether walking, standing, sitting, or otherwise—in the four continents. Some bodhisattvas entered meditative concentration, and emerging from that concentration, they stood amidst the great assembly to prostrate, circumambulate, make offerings, revere, honor, and praise the Buddha Padmottama.”
"Good son! At that time, that Buddha manifested such a mark of the broad and long tongue; having performed this transformation, he immediately withdrew it. Good son!"

The Buddha Padmottara again emitted light from the pores of his body; from each and every pore issued sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of rays of light. These lights were subtle and wondrous, pervading the ten directions, reaching across as many Buddha-worlds in each direction as there are atoms of dust.

In every place throughout that world, all those bodhisattvas who have received their predictions of enlightenment have attained dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and patience, or have reached the high stage of being in their final birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha).

Having seen this light, each of them left their own buddha-world and, by means of their supernormal powers, all set out together to arrive at that buddha’s abode, where they prostrated, circumambulated, made offerings, paid homage, revered, honored, and praised him.

"Good son! At that time, after the Buddha had manifested these transformations, he withdrew them once more and preached the True Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas and the great assembly, turning the wheel of non-retrogression, desiring to bring great benefit and great happiness to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings."
Out of compassion for the world, for the sake of humans and devas, he desires to cause them to be fully endowed with the unsurpassed Mahāyāna.
Chapter Two: The Dhāraṇī Chapter of the Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra. At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnārcis addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How can one know the distinction between day and night in that Buddha-world?
What are the characteristics of the sounds heard there?
And how do those bodhisattvas achieve their accomplishments?
"What other practices does one who practices with a single mind differ from?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Jewel-Sun Radiance: "Good son!

In that Buddha-world, the constant radiance of the Buddha’s light serves as illumination; with flowers closing and birds nesting, the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas enter various meditative concentrations and sport like lions, their minds filled with joy as they experience the bliss of liberation.
At that time, he knew it was already nightfall.

When the wind blew, scattering various flowers upon the ground, the birds sang together in harmonious and exquisite melodies, and various kinds of flowers rained down as winds arose from the four quarters; the fragrance was subtle, exquisite, soft, and smooth, and the Buddha and the bodhisattvas arose from their meditative concentration.

At that time, that Buddha was preaching the Dharma-treasury for Bodhisattvas to the great assembly, desiring to cause them to transcend the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; therefore, it was known that this was the daytime.

“Good son! In that Buddha-world, the assembly of bodhisattvas constantly hears the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṅgha, the sound of cessation, the sound of non-existence, the sound of the six pāramitās, the sound of the powers and fearlessnesses, the sound of the six supernormal knowledges, the sound of non-action, the sound of neither arising nor ceasing, the sound of subtle and tranquil stillness, the sound of the tranquility of causes, the sound of the tranquility of conditions, the sound of great kindness and great compassion, the sound of the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas and of prophecy, and the pure, wondrous sounds of exclusively bodhisattvas; they are never separated from hearing such sounds.”
"Good son! Such are the characteristics of the sounds you have heard. Good son!"

The bodhisattvas in that realm, whether already born there or yet to be born, all fully achieve the thirty-two marks; their bodies constantly emit light that illuminates one yojana, and until they attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they never fall into the three evil realms.

All those bodhisattvas have fully accomplished a mind of great loving-kindness, a mind of great compassion, a supple mind, a mind free from the turbidity of attachment, a tamed mind, a tranquil mind, a patient mind, a meditative mind, a pure mind, an unobstructed mind, an unstained mind, an undefiled mind, a true mind, a mind that delights in the Dharma, a mind that desires to cause sentient beings to sever their afflictions, a mind like the earth, a mind free from all worldly speech, a mind that loves and delights in the noble Dharma, a mind that seeks wholesome dharmas, a mind free from the notion of self, a mind of cessation free from birth, old age, sickness, and death, a mind that burns away all afflictions, a mind of cessation that releases one from all bonds, and a mind that attains immovability regarding all phenomena.

“Good son! Those bodhisattvas have attained the power of single-minded concentration, the power of initiation, the power of conditions, the power of vows, the power of non-contention, the power of observing all dharmas, the power of all roots of goodness, the power of all samādhis, the power of extensive learning, the power of upholding the precepts, the power of great relinquishment, the power of patience, the power of diligence, the power of meditative concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of tranquility, the power of reflection, the power of all supernatural faculties, the power of mindfulness, the power of bodhi, the power to destroy all Māras, the power to subdue all heterodox teachers, and the power to destroy all afflictions.”

Thus, those bodhisattvas who have already been born or will be born in that buddha-field are truly bodhisattvas; they have already made offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and have planted roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas.

Those bodhisattvas take the savor of dhyāna as their food; their sustenance is the Dharma-food and fragrance-food, just like that of the Brahmā heavens. There is no solid food, nor even the name for it;

there is no unwholesomeness, nor are there women. Suffering sensations, love and hatred, all other afflictions, as well as the physical and mental distress of "self" and "mine," the three evil realms, and so forth—all such names are entirely absent.

Furthermore, there is no darkness or foul-smelling places, no impurities, thorns, or filth; no mountains, hills, mounds, or ridges; no earth, sand, gravel, or stones; nor is there the light of the sun, moon, stars, or burning fires. There is no Mount Sumeru or the great oceans, nor the dark and obscure regions between the two Iron Ring Mountains, large and small. There is no rain, turbidity, or chaotic, evil winds, nor any of the eight difficult conditions (*aṣṭāvakṣaṇa*); indeed, none of these names even exist there.

“Good son! That Buddha-world is constantly illuminated by the light of the Buddhas and the precious light of the Bodhisattvas; that light is subtle, wondrous, pure, and supreme, pervading the entirety of that land.”

Within it there is a bird named Good Fruit (*Sukalaviṅka*), whose voice constantly utters the subtle and wondrous sounds of the faculties (*indriya*), powers (*bala*), factors of awakening (*bodhyaṅga*), and the path (*mārga*).
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jewel-Sun Radiance (*Ratnādityaprabha*) again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
How great in length and breadth is that Buddha-world?
For how long will he remain in the world, live his life-span, and preach the Dharma?
Last night he first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; after his parinirvāṇa, for how long will the Dharma remain?
For how long will the assembly of bodhisattvas remain in this world?
Among those bodhisattvas born in that world, will there be any who are far removed from seeing the Buddha, hearing the Dharma, and making offerings to the Sangha?
What was the name [of the Buddha] before the Buddha appeared in the Lotus World?
How much time has elapsed since the previous Buddha, the World-Honored One Sun, passed into parinirvāṇa in that realm?
After his parinirvāṇa, how much time will elapse before the Buddha Padmottara attains the Way?

By what causes and conditions do all the Buddhas throughout every place in the worlds of the ten directions enter the Lion’s Play Samādhi and manifest various miraculous transformations, such that some bodhisattvas see them while others do not?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Jewel Sun Radiance:
"Good son! It is like Sumeru, the King of Mountains, which is sixteen thousand eight hundred yojanas in height and eighty-four thousand yojanas in length and breadth."

Suppose there were someone who, through diligent application of effort, the power of illusion, or the power of meditative concentration, could shatter Mount Sumeru into pieces as small as mustard seeds—beyond all calculation, such that no one except the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the All-Knowing One, would be able to comprehend it.
Suppose one mustard seed represents one set of four continents; let all the sets of four continents within this Lotus World be counted by exhausting these mustard seeds.
May bodhisattvas fill them completely, just like the bodhisattvas in the Western Land of Peace and Bliss.
“Good son! That Buddha Padmottama lived for thirty intermediate kalpas teaching the Dharma, and after his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma remained in the world for a full ten intermediate kalpas.”
“Good son! Those bodhisattvas who have already been born or will be born there shall have a lifespan of forty intermediate kalpas. Good son!...”
That Buddha-world was originally named Candana; it was pure, exquisite, and wonderful, yet not as it is now.
At that time, there were likewise no such pure bodhisattvas in that world.

“Good son! In the past, when the world was called Candana, a former Buddha appeared in the world named Sūryacandraprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. His lifespan lasted thirty intermediate kalpas as he preached the Dharma.”
At the time of his parinirvāṇa, some bodhisattvas, by the power of their vows, departed for other buddha-fields; those who remained there thought to themselves:
"In the middle watch of this very night, the Tathāgata, the Honored One of Sun and Moon, shall enter parinirvāṇa."

"After this Buddha has passed into extinction, we shall protect and uphold the True Dharma during ten intermediate kalpas. Who will be able to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi in succession after this True Dharma has been extinguished?"
At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Gaganamudrā; because of his original vow, the Tathāgata Candrasūryaprabha immediately bestowed upon him this prediction:
"O son of good family!..."
After my parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full ten intermediate kalpas.

At the end of those ten intermediate kalpas, during the first watch of the night, the True Dharma will be extinguished; at that time, you shall immediately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your name shall be Padmottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣa-damya-sārathi, Śāstā deva-manuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.

At that time, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas went to the place where the Buddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa was; having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, those bodhisattvas made offerings to the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa through various forms of mastery and lion-like play by means of their power of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*).
Having made these offerings, they circumambulated him three times to the right and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
We wish to enter the meditative absorption of cessation during these ten intermediate kalpas."
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā: ‘Good son!...’”
This *dhāraṇī* gate of comprehending all things has been taught by the many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past to those bodhisattvas who have received the office of Buddhahood;
likewise, it is being taught now by the Buddhas of the ten directions to those bodhisattvas who have received the office of Buddhahood.
The Buddhas, World-Honored Ones of the future, shall likewise preach this to those bodhisattvas who have received the office of Buddhahood—namely, the "Comprehension of All Dharani Gates."
Then he spoke these verses: "Jali jalinī"
Mahā-jaṭī-vikiri-viki-sapati mahā-sapati.
Tidatāṭahita caṭa kaṭa dhara troka asmagaka sihele.
Mili tile liuliu qi mahaliuliuqi shayi tou shayi.
jāmi macchamandi śatani gadani amule mulapavaḥ
Leshani-maloshi-ni-viravade-nimite-nimite-parishuti-apiti.
*Pāyā-viḍṇe pāro-ughāre ḍaṇḍa-viśa-biśa-pāru-ut-taṇḍe.* "By these phrases,

one destroys all the discourses of the non-Buddhists, gathers the True Wheel of Dharma, and is further able to protect those who preach the True Dharma, revealing and analyzing the Dharma-gate of liberation consisting of the four foundations of mindfulness."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:
*Buddho bhagavān āma-maṇe mamaha śrī-pṛthivī-ante nite loka-dhātu-saṃtita-vamane.* "These verses reveal and distinguish the four kinds of noble gates of liberation."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

*Posati posani dale dharapati | Juti sujivi supapati niṭi sumavati kṣanti-kṣiti-karuṇodīkṣayi | Bhiṭi upabhiṣa sabhane arakṣi-bharadi | Khaki khaki-kṣayi amule muru-śuddhani ||* "These verses reveal, explain, and distinguish the Dharma-gate of liberation through the four fearlessnesses."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

“Cupphara, agapphara, anephara, nepphara, sumudāyanta, ibhidhi vibhidhi, udumbaradūlana akhaṃsamakhaṃ, itipada, addhataddha, sarvaloka, ataga, lepidha, abhusale, dhadhamani visagavati apphalaphalaṇa. “These verses reveal, analyze, and protect the Dharma-gate of the Three Vehicles.”
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

*Mentada | Anidhihara | Babata-piao | Itam-phale-niyen-phale | Samodananyen | Vibhuśa | Badasuma-dou | Amianmo-wu-ajiuma-dou-tuotobadi-dashabala-vibata-ta | Sishatida | Haniyinmadizhanmadi | Alujiu | Adidou-nasa-zhimodi* "These verses are what all Buddhas of the present have originally practiced; they reveal and analyze the Dharma-gate of the Four Right Efforts."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

“Anide | Mānide | Mānide | Māmānide | Chale | Jile | Tīle | Liśe | Li-ta-pi | Śvade | Mudde | Utpali | Samli-ni | Samli-samā-samli | Kṣaye | Akṣaye | Aja-dhi-śvade | Śamiti | Dhāraṇī | Abhagapavas-rena-bhati | Renamabati-jñanabhati | Merubhati-kṣayini-taśani | Lokabhati-pade-taśani. “These verses reveal, elucidate, and distinguish the Dharma-gate of the four kinds of unimpeded eloquence and liberation.”
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

*Kaṃsāpāpāde dhaśani | dhyānalokadhātūpapāśani | sarvānti bumati cindi | sarva-sarva | vama sarva-pāyapākṣayakare | kugare vaśani | lokānudarsanapivā* "These verses reveal, explain, and distinguish the Dharma-gate of liberation through the four bases of power (*catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ*)."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

"Acarai | Budhitadadhāpacarai | Nanani | Gandanasitigambhiti | Nisiti Sampichi | Parigasarai Sumijantiti | Jantiti Acarai | Acaccharai | Apalai | Bimbavari | Nepavarivacaracali | Pavalai | Anaya | Anaya | Abisi | Hūṃ hūṃ Svabhividekade | Nidesi | Gagami | Nayudhi" "These verses reveal, elucidate, and distinguish all the gateways of the faculties (*indriya*), powers (*bala*), and liberations (*vimokṣa*)."
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

*Purbā, cūrbā, dharmapare, hehe, apayicire, cikalekṣe, ayamatudde.* *Didele mamale śucā śuśele, lokasāni jñānaye kṣakṣi, dindanacakṣaye sāntidina.* These verses reveal, demonstrate, and analyze the Dharma-gate of liberation through the seven factors of enlightenment (*saptabodhyaṅga*).
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:
"Cakravarti-pate cakrale..."
Cchāgadhare dhara cchāgale dhare mule he he le le dhare ārupavati.
Hū hū rātriṇi he he bhaṭṭe kṣudhite piṅgale yathādhikṛte yathāpratikṛte yathāpalañje.
Vītilasaya-ta-bhaye-li-vīti-sacche-ni-le-hara-ja-lu-ca-vīli-vili-ni-le-hara.
Amuktaniṣkāraṇi, akāraṇi, akārasamādhi-niṣkāraṇi, akāraprajñā-niṣkāraṇi, bimbodgata-niṣkāraṇi.
Bhimadeva Janadhareśanani reharanākṣate nirehara candhani reharasūlini.
Līhārapādāśaye ṣaṇḍatā arhatā agata abudhani rabuda sambuddha buddha ita abuda.
Cūḍā-puṭaniha-amo-mau-le-arā-pratā-dhara-prabhaṃ-tale.
Mandale cūḍale dharoma gaga lāni maujuṇa samaujuṇa.
Gaṅgā-bhaṅga-maṇu-nirvāṇa-śānti-śānti-pāraṃ-niṣṭhite.
Cic-cit-tu-ma-yu-pa-he-dīpaka-ma-bale-male-akṣaṇi-bale-male-bindhi-viri-viri-uṣari-śaraṇi.
Dhāraṇī babādhi bala nārāyaṇi.
Vidhuma, Brahmo-ma, Brahmā-cela, Indiva, Śititiya, Rāṇi, Maheśvara-rāṇi,
Samasumi, Aramanemi, Ikakalasa, Risica, Nica-ra, Acchanda, Sūri.
Sarva-śūra-āpala-puṇya-gati-dambha-dhita-ayana-kṣatriya-vāsikā-gāthāre-aradāhani.
Makāravilohani-siddhamantrī-vilokamantrī.
“This gateway of dhāraṇīs is upheld by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones; it reveals and distinguishes the Dharma-gateway of liberation consisting of the ten powers of the Tathāgata.”
At that time, when the World-Honored One Śākyamuni spoke this Dharma-gate of the Dhāraṇī for Understanding All, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, surging and subsiding.
At that time, a great, subtle, and wondrous light pervaded the ten directions, extending beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Within them, all the Kings of Mountains, Sumeru, and the large and small Iron Ring Mountains were no longer visible to the eye; one saw only the earth of the worlds as level as the palm of a hand.

In every location throughout the worlds of the ten directions, there were bodhisattvas, infinite in number, who had attained various meditative concentrations, dharanis, and patiences; by the Buddha’s spiritual power, this assembly vanished from their own lands and suddenly arrived at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the Sahā world.

Arriving at the place where the Tathāgata was, they prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet and offered to the Buddha the various kinds of sovereign supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) attained by the bodhisattvas.
Having made these offerings, they each sat down in order on one side, desiring to hear the explanation of all the gateways of *dhāraṇī*.

Innumerable devas of the desire and form realms came to where the Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and each sat in order to one side to listen to and receive the teaching on the comprehension of all dharani-doors.
In this way, the entire great assembly was able to see the Lotus Buddha-field, as well as that Buddha surrounded by a gathering of great Bodhisattvas.

At that time, when the World-Honored One Śākyamuni preached this "Dhāraṇī Gate for the Comprehension of All," seventy-two Ganges-sands of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attained this Dhāraṇī Gate. Immediately, they were able to see the innumerable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the worlds in the ten directions, and they also saw the pure and wondrous worlds of those Buddhas; the Bodhisattvas marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence.
Because these bodhisattvas have attained mastery through the lion’s play of meditative concentration, they fashioned various kinds of offering implements to worship the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bodhisattvas: "Good sons!..."

If a bodhisattva cultivates this dharani-door of comprehending all, they will immediately attain eighty-four thousand dharani-doors, seventy-two thousand samadhi-doors, and sixty thousand dharma-aggregate doors; they will immediately attain great loving-kindness and great compassion, understand the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and attain all-knowledge without any obstruction.

This dharani gateway encompasses all Buddha-dharmas; having realized this dharani, the Buddhas preach the unsurpassed Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings and remain in the world for a long time, not entering nirvana.

“Good son! You should know that what you have now seen is due to the majestic spiritual power of the *dhāraṇī* gates that bring about complete understanding; it causes this great earth to quake in six ways and produces subtle, pure, and radiant light that shines throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.”

Wherever the light reached, bodhisattvas from immeasurable worlds came to this assembly to hear, receive, and fully comprehend all dharani gates; they were joined by all the immeasurable devas of the desire and form realms from this world, who gathered together in harmony.

Furthermore, there were various nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, humans, non-humans, and others, all of whom came desiring to hear the exposition of the gateways to the dhāraṇīs for the thorough understanding of all things.
If a bodhisattva, having heard and understood all the gateways of dhāraṇī, then becomes non-retrogressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If there is anyone who transcribes this, that person shall, until reaching unsurpassed *nirvāṇa*, never be separated from seeing the Buddha, hearing the Dharma, and making offerings to the Saṃgha.

If one can read and recite it, all evil karmas and the like will be exhausted without remainder; upon receiving birth in a subsequent body, one will immediately transcend the first stage (*bhūmi*) and attain the second dwelling (*vihāra*).

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva can practice and fully comprehend all dharanī-doors, all the grave sins of the five heinous acts committed will be entirely extinguished; in their second rebirth, they shall transcend the first stage and attain the second dwelling.

If one has not committed the five heinous crimes, all heavy karmic obstructions of this present body will be forever exhausted without remainder; upon changing bodies, one shall immediately transcend the first stage and attain the second dwelling.
If one is unable to recite or practice [the teachings], yet at the time of hearing the Dharma offers various silken fabrics to the Dharma Master,
then all the Buddhas currently residing in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges will each praise and extol them,
saying: "Excellent!"
"Excellent!
he said, and immediately bestowed upon him the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
By virtue of these causes and conditions of making offerings, this bodhisattva shall before long receive the rank of a Buddha and achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in a single lifetime.
If one makes an offering of incense, before long one shall attain the fragrance of unsurpassed concentration;
if one makes an offering of flowers, before long one shall attain the flower of unsurpassed wisdom;
if one makes an offering of rare jewels to the Dharma Master, before long one shall attain the jewels of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.
“Good son! If there are bodhisattvas who can understand and master this dhāraṇī, they will obtain great benefit. Why is this?

This dharani gateway can reveal and distinguish all the treasuries of the dharmas of all bodhisattvas; by upholding it, it causes all bodhisattvas to attain the four pleasing dharmas of unimpeded eloquence.

“Good son! When the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa had finished teaching the dharanī-gate to the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā, at that time the great earth shook in six ways, and there were immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous lights that shone everywhere throughout the infinite and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions; one could see all those Buddha-fields, their grounds as level as the palm of a hand.”
"At that time, there were also immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within the assembly, all of whom beheld the innumerable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions.

At that moment, immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas from the ten directions each vanished from their own worlds and suddenly arrived in the Candana world. There they saw the Buddha Candrasūryaprabhāsa, prostrated before him, circumambulated him, and made offerings with reverence, respect, honor, and praise, all desiring to hear and receive this dharanī gateway."
“Good son! At that time, that Buddha addressed the bodhisattvas, saying: ‘Good sons!’”

I have now granted you, who are all in your final birth before Buddhahood, permission to enter the meditative absorption of cessation for ten intermediate kalpas; as for the remaining bodhisattvas, they should, during those ten intermediate kalpas, receive this dharani-gate, the Dharma-treasury of bodhisattvas, from the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Gaganamudra.

In accordance with the Dharma they uphold, they shall behold all the Buddhas existing throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions; by virtue of seeing these Buddhas, their hearts will give rise to joy, and they shall plant roots of goodness.

At that time, there were among those in the assembly various bodhisattvas who had attained manifold masteries and the lion’s play; they made offerings to that Buddha with all kinds of ritual implements.
Having made these offerings, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśamudrā shall, after ten intermediate kalpas have passed, attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and shall turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma."
At that time, the Buddha told them:
"O sons of good family!
It is as you have said."
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā, after ten intermediate kalpas have passed, shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; and immediately following that night, he shall turn the wheel of Dharma.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā had attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he passed that very night and turned the wheel of the True Dharma, the non-retrogressive wheel, and the unsurpassed wheel.

At that time, there were immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas in the assembly who, having previously received this dharani gateway from the Bodhisattva Gaganamudra during ten intermediate kalpas, had attained non-retrogression; some were in their final birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha), and they were destined to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

“Good son! If there is a bodhisattva who does not extensively practice and study this dhāraṇī, yet in a future life attains a stage beyond the first bhūmi and enters the second vihāra, they shall not regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and will certainly attain this gateway of the dhāraṇī.”
Having spoken thus, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsa manifested various supernatural transformations for the sake of the bodhisattvas.
Having manifested these, he revealed the Nārāyaṇa-samādhi to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā, saying:
"Once you have attained this samādhi, you shall then receive a vajra-body."
Furthermore, he manifested for him the light of the Samādhi of All Adornments, saying: "Good son!
Although you have not yet turned this wheel of the true Dharma, in a dream you have expounded this gateway of dhāraṇī for the sake of all bodhisattvas."

At that time, you shall have already attained the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of a Tathāgata’s body; you shall also emit this light of the Samādhi of All Adornments, which will universally illumine all immeasurable worlds, and within that light, you shall behold immeasurable and boundless Buddhas.

He further manifested for them the Vajra-throne Samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, although he had not yet sat beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment nor turned the wheel of Dharma, he was already able to expound the subtle and wondrous Dharma for all the bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, he manifested for them the Wheel-Hair Samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, he immediately turned the wheel of Dharma. At the time of turning the wheel of Dharma, immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas attained definitive certainty.

At that time, having heard this teaching, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā immediately realized for himself that he was to turn the wheel of Dharma. Overjoyed and leaping with delight, he, together with immeasurable bodhisattvas, made offerings to the Buddha.
Having made these offerings, they each entered their respective multi-storied pavilions.
At that time, that Buddha entered *nirvāṇa* without remainder during that very night.
When the night had passed, the bodhisattvas made offerings to his relics.
Having made these offerings, they each returned to their respective precious towers and palaces.
The bodhisattvas from other directions each returned to their own original Buddha-worlds.

Bodhisattvas who had been born for only one more life entered the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*) during ten intermediate kalpas (*antarakalpa*), while the remaining bodhisattvas, by virtue of the sublime Dharma preached through the Seal of Space (*ākāśamudrā*), planted roots of goodness throughout ten intermediate kalpas.

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā attained unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment last night; this very day he has turned the wheel of the true Dharma and manifested various miraculous transformations, causing hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable sentient beings to become non-retrogressive in their pursuit of unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment.

As I now speak this gateway of dhāraṇīs, eighty nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas attained the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharmakṣānti); seventy-two billion sentient beings became non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; seventy-two nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas attained this gateway of dhāraṇīs for the thorough understanding of all things; and immeasurable, boundless devas and humans resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Vigatarāga who addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
How many dharmas must a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplish in order to be able to cultivate and collect this *dhāraṇī* gate of understanding all things?"
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vigatarāgapratigha, saying: "Good son,
if a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they will be able to cultivate this dharanī-gate."
What are these four?
Abiding in these four noble lineages, a bodhisattva always attains contentment with coarse clothing, food, bedding, and medicinal requisites.
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these four dharmas, they are able to cultivate this dharanī gateway.
Furthermore, son of good family,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes five dharmas, they are able to cultivate this dharanī gateway.

What are these five? First, one personally upholds the prohibitive precepts, which means cherishing and protecting the *vimukti-śīla* (liberation precepts) and accomplishing the conduct of dignified demeanor;
guarding the dharma of the precepts with a sense of dread as if toward a small vajra.
They uphold and study all the precepts;

seeing those who break the precepts, they exhort them to maintain them; seeing those with wrong views, they exhort them to right view; seeing those who violate dignified conduct, they exhort them to abide in it; seeing those with distracted minds, they exhort them to single-mindedness;
and seeing those who take pleasure in the two vehicles, they exhort them to settle securely in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these five dharmas, they are able to cultivate this dharani-gate.
Furthermore, son of good family,
when a bodhisattva accomplishes six dharmas, they are able to cultivate this dharani-gate.
What are the six? First, one personally cultivates extensive learning with unhindered mastery; seeing those of little learning, one encourages them to become extensively learned.
Second, one is personally free from stinginess; seeing those who are stingy, one encourages them to abide in the dharma of non-stinginess.
They themselves are free from envy; seeing those who are envious, they exhort them to abide securely in the dharma of non-envy.

They themselves do not fear others and bestow fearlessness upon them; seeing those who are terrified, they provide protection for them, using skillful words to guide and console them so that they may attain peace and security.
Their minds are free from flattery and devoid of guile or deceit.
They practice the samādhi of emptiness.
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these six dharmas, they are able to cultivate this dharanī gateway.

Once a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has accomplished these characteristic dharmas, for seven years they condense all the *tāpī* verses and phrases; during the six periods of day and night, with head bowed in reverence and single-minded contemplation, they attend to the foundation of mindfulness regarding the body, practice the samādhi of emptiness, and recite these *tāpī* verses and phrases.
At the very moment of arising, he universally brings to mind all the immeasurable Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions.
After seven years have passed, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva immediately attains this *dhāraṇī* gateway of comprehending all things.
“Once a bodhisattva has attained this gateway of dhāraṇīs, they immediately obtain such a noble, pure eye.

Having obtained this eye, they see, in every location throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who do not enter parinirvāṇa, and they also see them manifesting various and immeasurable transformations of supernatural power.”

At that time, this bodhisattva beholds all immeasurable Buddhas without exception; by seeing these Buddhas, he immediately attains eighty-four thousand dharani-doors, seventy-two thousand samadhi-doors, and sixty thousand dharma-doors.
Once Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have attained this *dhāraṇī* gate of comprehending all things, they further develop great compassion toward sentient beings.

Moreover, once Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have attained this Dharma-gate, all their grave offenses, such as the five heinous crimes (*pañcānantarya*), shall be forever exhausted without remainder upon changing their current bodies.
In the third birth, having exhausted all karma, one attains the tenth stage (*bhūmi*).

If one has not committed the five heinous crimes (*ānantarya*), all other karmas will be forever exhausted without remainder in this very body; after passing through one more life, one attains the tenth stage, and before long, one shall attain the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*saptatriṃśad-bodhipākṣika-dharma*) and omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
“Good son! This gateway of dhāraṇīs that understands all things can bring great benefit to all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Because a bodhisattva constantly contemplates the Dharma-body of all Buddhas, they are able to see various miraculous transformations of supernatural power (*ṛddhi-vikurvaṇa*). Having seen these transformations, they immediately attain such untainted joy (*anāsrava-prāmodya*); because of this joy, they then accomplish such miraculous transformations. By the power of these supernatural abilities, they are able to make offerings to the Buddhas in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Having made these offerings, they also listen to and receive the sublime Dharma from those Buddhas. Because they listen to and receive the Dharma, they immediately attain dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and patience (*kṣānti*), and then return once more to this Buddha-world.”
“Good son! This dharani gateway is able to perform such great beneficial deeds as destroying evil karma and increasing all roots of goodness.
At that time, various bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In the past, at the abodes of as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, we heard this dharani-gate; having heard it, we immediately attained it.”
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in two Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in three Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke these words:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in four Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"We have already heard this dharani-gate from as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in five Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke these words:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of six Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we have immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are grains of sand in seven Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke thus:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas as there are sands in eight Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
Furthermore, another bodhisattva spoke these words:
"We have already heard this dharani gateway from as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in nine Ganges Rivers; having heard it, we immediately attained it."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In a past age, ten *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a great kalpa named ‘Excellently Pervasive.’”
During this kalpa, this Sahā world was exquisitely pure and adorned with every kind of ornament.

At that time, a Buddha appeared in the world, named Śālarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
There were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bhikṣu-saṃghas, and furthermore, incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas respectfully surrounded him.

At that time, the Buddha Śālarāja expounded for the great assembly this "Dhāraṇī Door of Understanding All. I, at that time, heard this Dharma from that Buddha; having heard it, I practiced and studied it, and having studied it, I immediately attained it, expanding and perfecting it.

Throughout such immeasurable and boundless kalpas, there were incalculable asaṃkhyeya Buddhas; during that time, according to their respective lifespans, I made offerings to these immeasurable Buddhas by means of the various lion’s-play sovereign samādhis attained by bodhisattvas.

At that time, I was able to plant immeasurable, boundless, incalculable, and asankhyeya roots of goodness at each and every one of these Buddhas. Having planted those roots of goodness, I immediately attained a vast accumulation of great merit; by virtue of these roots of goodness, immeasurable Buddhas bestowed predictions of enlightenment upon me.
"By virtue of my original vow, I have remained long in saṃsāra; because I was awaiting the proper time, I did not attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
World-Honored One!
I only pray that the Tathāgata will now confer upon me the rank of a Buddha, enabling me to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya:
"So it is, so it is! It is just as you have said."
When the Buddha Śālarāja was present in the world, you had already attained this Dharma-gate of the *Sarvārthaprativedha-dhāraṇī*. Maitreya!

If, throughout ten great eons in the past, you had desired to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you would have immediately and fully accomplished that *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and entered *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa* at that very time.
"Maitreya! You have long dwelt in saṃsāra; because of your original vow, you have not attained [enlightenment], for you are awaiting the proper time. Maitreya!"
"I now confer upon you the office of a Buddha.

At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the great assembly—including bodhisattvas, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, rākṣasas, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans—and having made this observation, he spoke these verses:
*Daita pūmi* (Dhiti-pūmi)
Dantabhu mi dambhadabhu migadibhu mi.
Meditibhūmi prajñābhūmi viśāradabhūmi.
Bhate svabhāvamye anucchambhe apacaramye.
Samata bhasma bhasma bhūme jati khara bhūme saca ja vicaja.
Parākṣa viśagada śavati viśadeti rāṇa.
Rāgaga-saṭṭha-sabba-dā "Vimati-uyha-pheṇa-rāga-ma-aṭṭha-khara.
Vaśa-saṃgama-īti-jūra-śiti-mi-mandra-dhāra-vati-prajñā-buddha-adhigami-tas-tuṣa-pānta.
Ilāyane lāye āhuṣaṭha amukta mukta athavate garuḍavate.
Dīhīnādeva-ākānamati-bhagavanmati-samiti-viśvabhūti.
Vidhāvara vidhāvara aradara kuruṣa dūruṣa raimara ruta-taru-ta.
"Sarvatha sarvathā caṇi lutha tihā dādā he phalava hu phala sarva phala setthapati.
When these verses on the liberation of the various twelve links of dependent origination were spoken, sixty nayutas of devas perceived the Four Noble Truths.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

“Dāphala | Agadaphala | Raraphala | Araphala Nīlahula | Bhavadabhāta | Itaphala | Nikṣepha | Namo dhyāne | Vibhūte | Prajñācakra | Anupradīpacaka | Janicaka. When these verses of liberation were spoken, one hundred million devas conceived the aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and all attained the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

“Padma sumadhu amomadhu akumadhu citrapakva madhātadhāśara vipapatha ihāśveta suṇema sutejana tīrthe arukū ābhāsa atīrṇa mahāmaunam. When these verses of liberation were spoken, sixty-four thousand nāgas gave rise to the mind of anuttarasamyaksambodhi and all attained the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:

"Akṣobhya-kṣa | Śubha-śāpa-mandana | Arasthu-bhagala-cu | Karada-kṣa | Siddhamati-samanta | Dākṣapale | Heṭhakaluma-hāpale | Ujjatara | Dhāraṇī | Hegarakṣa | Kūṭakṣa | Kūpakṣa | Virobhu | Vilupa | Mukha | Śrītekhada | Śrītepalai-aśurubhiṇa | Surupamati" When these verses of liberation were spoken, twelve billion yakṣas gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and all attained the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke these verses:
"Aṭibhīlī."
Niti ṭi-saṃti-ṭiga-tini.
Nāgamī ālamī pāramī
Adame madame made miśani āḥ.
The *dhāraṇī-avaśyāyana* for guarding [the mind] through meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
Sattvasatīva-sa-nāgaḥ
Sā yakṣā sā asurā devanāganī ṣaṭ tīre brāhmaṇi.
Nī ṣaṭi rāvi miṭe prajñāpanī bhadra mate pālirā vigate tiṭi pālipāragate tiṭi rāvi phuve khivi jaṇe visaccale paṃta.
Abhidhāna-pañca-śūra-paṇḍita-vīrya-vitta-vitta-vitti-viśva-nide.
Makā-vinda-viśa-pat-li-kṣama-de-ṣka-paro-hu-u-hara-lu-ti-ra-pa-du.
Asura Vindana, Yakṣa Vindaya, Yakṣa Vindarali.

Uṇḍanāmevakhadīdhāraṇy-āviśatīśeṣudhāni.
Pakṣi-stuti, Jīva-stuti, Pakṣi-parikarma.
"Di-mo-di-ji-di-du-di-ji-na-po-di-bo-luo-na-fu-di-sha-ye-zhe-jia-shu-ruo-tuo-zhe-jia-bei-ye.
Having spoken these verses on liberation, fifty-six thousand asuras gave rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and all attained the stage of non-retrogression.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Fearless Ground of Equanimity, saying:
“Good son! The appearance of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the world is extremely rare; to expound and disseminate this Dharma is even more difficult.”
This Dharma is that which is cultivated through morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. Good son!
Such passages as these can cause a bodhisattva to achieve majestic virtue.

“Good son! When the Tathāgata was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, he gathered these chapters and phrases through giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom, making offerings and paying respect to immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.”

In the presence of the Buddhas, they may practice giving, or cultivate pure conduct through the observance of the precepts, or exert themselves with diligence, or practice patience, or enter into samādhi, or cultivate wisdom.
I have cultivated and accumulated various kinds of purely wholesome and pure karma; therefore, I have now attained supreme wisdom. "Good son!

In the past, throughout immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* billions of *nayuta* kalpas while practicing the bodhisattva path, my body was always far removed from false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, and frivolous speech; therefore, I have now attained this mark of the tongue."
"Good son! For these reasons, that which is spoken by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, is true and without falsehood.
At that time, the World-Honored One manifested various transformations of supernatural powers.
Having performed these transformations, he entered the Samādhi of Pervasive All-Virtues.

Having entered this samādhi, he extended his broad and long tongue until it completely covered his face; from the root of that tongue, he emitted sixty billion rays of light. These lights were subtle and wondrous, illuminating the entire trichiliocosm, so that those in the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, the devas, and humans all received their radiance.
As for the sentient beings in the hells whose bodies were ablaze, by receiving this light, they attained cool and refreshing bliss in an instant.
Before each of these sentient beings, there appeared a manifested Buddha, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics.
At that time, because they had seen the Buddha, all sentient beings attained happiness and each thought:
"It is by the grace of this person that we have obtained joy.
Toward the emanated Buddha, their hearts were filled with gladness, and they joined their palms in reverent salutation.
At that time, the Buddha addressed those sentient beings:
"If you now invoke 'Namo Buddha, Namo Dharma, Namo Sangha,' by virtue of these conditions, you shall always obtain happiness."
These beings knelt for a long time with palms joined, receiving the Buddha's teaching, and spoke these words:
"Homage to the Buddha!
Homage to the Dharma!"
"Namo to the Saṃgha!
By virtue of these roots of goodness as a causal condition, these sentient beings, upon the end of their lives here, will either be reborn in the heavens or among human beings.
If there are sentient beings in the cold hells, at that moment a soft and warm wind will immediately arise and touch their bodies; this is likewise true for those born among devas and humans.
The sentient beings among the hungry ghosts, being oppressed by hunger and thirst, were relieved of their afflictions of hunger and thirst and experienced happiness through the light of the Buddha.

Furthermore, before each of them appeared a manifested Buddha, adorned with a body of the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics; because they beheld the Buddha, they all attained happiness and each thought:
"By the grace of this person, I have been granted this joy."
At the presence of the transformation buddhas, their hearts were filled with joy, and they joined their palms in reverent worship.

At that time, the World-Honored One enabled those sentient beings to perceive the causes and conditions of their past-life karmic offenses; they immediately repented and reproached themselves. By virtue of these roots of goodness, at the end of their lives therein, they were reborn among devas or human beings;
the same was true for sentient beings in the realm of animals.

At that time, because the World-Honored One was demonstrating the causes and conditions of past lives to the devas and humans, immeasurable and boundless sentient beings came to where the Buddha was; they prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and listened to and received the sublime Dharma.
At that time, there were incalculable devas and humans who resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and countless bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attained *dhāraṇī*, *samādhi*, and *kṣānti*.
The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll One;
The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Two.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Three: On Great Giving (Mahādāna), Part One.
At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Śāntamati. Having beheld the various miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

For what reason are the worlds of all other Buddhas pure, subtle, and adorned with various ornaments; free from the five turbidities and devoid of all impurities; wherein there dwell only great Bodhisattvas who have accomplished various immeasurable merits and enjoy every happiness; and in whose lands even the names of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas do not exist, let alone the reality of the two vehicles?

For what cause and by what condition does our World-Honored One dwell in this defiled, impure world—amidst the turbidity of lifespan, the turbidity of the kalpa, the turbidity of sentient beings, the turbidity of views, and the turbidity of afflictions—and within this world of five turbidities, attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
Why do you preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles among the fourfold assembly?
For what reason do you not take up such a pure world, yet instead remain far removed from the five turbidities of this evil world?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Silent Mind:
"Good son! Because of their original vows, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas take up pure and wondrous lands; likewise, because of their vows, they take up impure lands."
Why is this? Son of good family!
Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished great compassion, they take up this wretched, evil, and impure earth.
Therefore, by virtue of my original vow, I abide in this impure and defiled world to realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O son of good family!
"Listen now with close attention; reflect upon it well and receive it properly, and I shall now speak.
At that time, the bodhisattvas received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Silent Intent: "Good son!

In the past, beyond incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, this buddha-world was named Sandhārana, and at that time, the great kalpa was called Sustaining Virtue (*Sudhāra*)."
In that kalpa, there was a wheel-turning sage king named Araṇemin, who ruled over the four continents.
He had a great minister named Ratnasāgara, who was of the brahmin caste and well-versed in the interpretation of signs and omens.

At that time, he gave birth to a son whose body was adorned with the thirty-two marks, further embellished in succession by the eighty secondary characteristics; each mark was accomplished through a hundred merits. His constant radiance extended one fathom, and his body was perfectly proportioned like a nyagrodha tree; gazing intently upon even a single mark, one could never be satiated.
At the time of his birth, hundreds of thousands of devas came together to make offerings, and for this reason he was given the name Ratnagarbha.

Later, when he had grown up, he shaved off his hair and beard, donned the dharma robes, and left the household life; he attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and was again titled the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, and Bhagavat.
He immediately turned the wheel of Dharma, causing hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of sentient beings to be born among humans and devas, or to attain liberation.

Having thus benefited the devas and humans, he was respectfully surrounded by a great assembly of hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of śrāvakas as he traveled in succession through cities and villages, gradually arriving at a city named Anzhoula, which was the seat of governance for the Holy King.
Not far from the city, there was a grove named Jambū.
At that time, the Tathāgata, together with a great assembly of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of śrāvakas, stayed in this grove.

At that time, the Wheel-Turning King heard that the Buddha Ratnagarbha, together with a multitude of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great śrāvakas, was traveling by stages and had arrived at the Jambū Forest.
At that time, the holy king thought to himself:
"I shall now go to where the Buddha is, to pay homage, circumambulate him, and offer worship, reverence, respect, and praise."

Having formed this thought, he immediately used his own power as a holy king (*cakravartin*) to emerge from the city of Anucakra, surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable multitude, and proceeded toward the Jambūvana grove.
Having reached the outskirts of the grove, he alighted from his carriage in accordance with the Dharma and proceeded on foot to where the Buddha was.
Upon reaching the Buddha’s presence, he prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to sit to one side.

“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha immediately preached the True Dharma for the noble king, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening him through various skillful means.”
Having spoken this Dharma, he remained silent.
Then the Wheel-Turning King rose from his seat, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I only pray that the Tathāgata and the assembly of noble ones will accept my offerings of robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicinal requisites for the duration of three months."
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata granted his consent by remaining silent.
The king, knowing then that the Buddha had already granted permission, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times, and departed with joy.”
At that time, the Wheel-Turning King addressed the minor kings, ministers, people, and their retinues, saying: "Do you know this?"
"I have now invited the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and his great assembly for the duration of three months, to provide them with all that they require for their comfort.
Whatever I hold dear and precious—my various articles of worship, as well as my servants and attendants—I now relinquish them all to offer as a gift to the Buddha and the assembly of noble ones."

You all should now likewise relinquish your most cherished possessions, including all articles of offering and your male and female servants and attendants, to present as offerings to the Buddha and the assembly of noble ones.
Having heard this, the people immediately accepted the instruction and joyfully practiced it.
At that time, the Minister of Treasures, within the Jambū Grove, made the ground out of pure gold and constructed a seven-jeweled pavilion upon that ground.

The four gates of that tower were composed of the seven treasures, and there were rows of trees made of the seven treasures; upon all these trees hung precious garments and necklaces, adorned with various kinds of pearls, exquisite jeweled canopies, and diverse precious vessels.

Furthermore, there were various fragrances, exquisite jewels, and flowers and fruits adorning the trees; diverse flowers were scattered about, and silken hangings and cotton wool served as bedding, while silk banners were suspended from them.

The noble golden wheel hovered in the air before the pavilion, seven feet above the ground; the white elephant treasure stood behind the Tathāgata holding a tree made of the seven treasures, which was further adorned with pearls, silks, and various kinds of necklaces, and atop it was a wonderful canopy made of the seven treasures.

He caused the Jewel Woman to stand before the Tathāgata, grind ox-head sandalwood and black aloeswood to scatter over the Buddha, and place a maṇi jewel before the Buddha; the subtle and wondrous radiance of both the jewel and the golden wheel was constantly bright, pervading the Jambūnada forest day and night without distinction.
The constant body-light of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha is subtle, wondrous, and pure, pervading the trichiliocosm.
He provides couches for each and every śrāvaka made of gośīrṣa-candana, with side-tables made of gośīrṣa-candana placed beside each bed.
Behind each seat was a white elephant treasure, holding a tree made of the seven precious gems; its various adornments were likewise like those of the Tathāgata.
Before each seat was a jade-woman treasure, who ground ox-head sandalwood and black aloeswood to scatter as offerings.
Before the seat of each and every śrāvaka, a maṇi jewel was placed.
Within that grove, various kinds of music were performed, and on the perimeter of the grove, the fourfold army of treasures stood encircling it.

“Good son! At dawn, the wheel-turning king departed the city for the place where the Buddha was. Having reached the outskirts of the grove, he descended from his carriage in accordance with the Dharma and proceeded on foot to where the Buddha was.”

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and personally provided water for washing, while serving exquisite delicacies with his own hands to the Buddha and the great assembly.
When the meal was finished, they set aside their bowls and rinsed their mouths.
Then the Wheel-Turning King took up a precious fan in his hand and fanned the Tathāgata and each of the śrāvakas.
At that time, the king’s thousand sons and the eighty-four thousand minor kings all made offerings to each of the śrāvakas, just as the Wheel-Turning King had made offerings to the World-Honored One.
Shortly after the meal, hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of sentient beings entered the Jambūvana forest to listen to and receive the true Dharma from the Tathāgata.

"At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of devas in the sky, scattering celestial flowers and performing celestial music as offerings to the Buddha; at that moment, celestial robes, necklaces, and various jeweled parasols revolved spontaneously in the sky."

Furthermore, there were forty thousand blue-clad yakṣas who gathered ox-head sandalwood from the sandalwood grove to kindle fires for the Buddha and the great assembly so that they might cook their food.
At that time, during the night, the Wheel-Turning King lit hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of lamps before the Buddha and the great assembly.

“Good son! At that time, the wheel-turning king bore one lamp upon his head, carried two lamps upon his shoulders, held four lamps in his left and right hands, placed one lamp upon each of his two knees, and likewise placed one lamp upon each of his two ankles; in this manner, he made offerings to the Tathāgata throughout the entire night.”

By the Buddha's spiritual power, his body and mind were filled with bliss and free from any exhaustion; it was just as when a bhikṣu enters the third dhyāna, and the joy experienced by a Cakravartin Wheel-turning King was likewise the same. He made such offerings for the full duration of three months.

At that time, the king’s thousand sons, along with eighty-four thousand minor kings and an immeasurable multitude of hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas, also made offerings of exquisite food to each of the śrāvakas; the delicacies they provided were identical to those consumed by the noble king, and this continued for three full months.
The Jewel Woman also made offerings of various flowers and incense, just as the Wheel-Turning King makes offerings to the Buddha, without any distinction between them.
As for the other sentient beings who offered flowers and incense, their offerings were no different from those of the Jewel Woman’s offerings to the Śrāvakas.
“Good son! After three months had passed, the Wheel-Turning King presented to the Tathāgata a dragon-head necklace made of Jāmbūnada gold by the Treasurer-General,
as well as eighty-four thousand precious golden wheels, white elephants, and dark-blue horses.”
...maṇi jewels, exquisite fire-jewels, the treasure of the minister of the treasury, the treasure of the commander of the fourfold army,
and various minor kings [residing] in the city of Anucakra and its various small towns; seven-jeweled clothing-trees,
clusters of exquisite jewel-flowers, various jeweled canopies, and the exquisite garments worn by the wheel-turning sage kings— various [such things].
Flower garlands and exquisite necklaces; magnificent chariots made of the seven treasures and various jeweled couches;
jeweled nets interlaced with the heads and eyes of the seven treasures; golden locks of Jambū-river gold and strings of precious pearls;
exquisite sandals, carpets, and cushions; subtle and wonderful footstools, vessels and implements of the seven treasures, and musical instruments such as bells and drums.
There were musical instruments, jeweled bells, conchs, and drums; groves, gardens, banners, and streamers; precious vases, lamps, and candles;

birds and beasts made of the seven treasures; various exquisite fans; and all kinds of medicinal herbs—each of these items numbering eighty-four thousand—were offered as gifts to the Buddha and the assembly of noble ones.
Having made this offering, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
My kingdom has many affairs, and there were various shortcomings; I now repent for my transgressions."
I only pray that the Tathāgata will dwell long in this garden, and that I may frequently come and go to pay homage, circumambulate you, and respectfully offer worship, honor, and praise.

"The sons of that king were seated before the Buddha; each prince individually invited the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus to accept their offerings for the entire three-month period, providing all necessities and only requesting his consent."
At that time, the Tathāgata silently granted his consent.

Knowing then that the Tathāgata had accepted the request of his sons, the Wheel-turning King prostrated with his head at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, circumambulated them three times to the right, and departed with joy.

“Good son! At that time, the king’s eldest son among his thousand sons was named Animiṣa (Unblinking). For the duration of three months, he made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, providing all necessities of comfort just as a noble cakravartin king would.”
At that time, the Wheel-Turning King went daily to the Buddha’s abode to behold the Honored One’s countenance and the community of bhikṣus, and to listen to and receive the sublime Dharma. "Good son!
At that time, the great minister, the brahmin Ratnasāgara, traveled throughout Jambudvīpa to every man, woman, boy, and girl, begging for whatever was required."
At that time, the brahmin first made a request to the donor:
"If you can now take refuge in the Triple Gem and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, only then shall I accept what you offer."

At that time, among all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa, there was not even a single person who did not receive the three refuges from the brahmin and resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having caused all those people to receive his instructions, he then accepted the offerings they bestowed.
At that time, the brahmin established hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable sentient beings in the three bases of merit and inspired them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Crown Prince Animiṣa made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus for a full three months.
At the conclusion, as his act of giving (dakṣiṇā), he presented eighty-four thousand golden dragon-head necklaces;
however, with the exception of the noble King’s golden wheel, white elephant, dark-blue horse, jade maiden, treasurer, minister of war, and mani-jewel, he offered all other possessions he had.
Golden wheels, elephants, horses, and exquisite fire-jewels; young boys and girls, trees of the seven precious gems, clusters of seven-precious flowers, and various jeweled canopies;
sublime garments, diverse flower garlands, superior necklaces, and wonderful chariots of the seven precious gems; various jeweled couches, and heads and eyes made of the seven precious gems.
Intertwined jewel nets and Jambu-river gold chains; strings of precious pearls and exquisite sandals;
embroidered rugs and cushions, as well as subtle and wonderful footstools; vessels and implements made of the seven treasures, bells, drums, and musical performances;
jeweled bells, conchs, and gongs; gardens, groves, banners, and streamers; jewel-filled vases, lamps, and candles; and birds and beasts made of the seven treasures.
He offered eighty-four thousand exquisite fans, various medicinal herbs,
and other such items to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.
