Having made this offering, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Whatever was deficient, I now repent for it today.”

“At that time, the second prince, named Nima, for the duration of three months, made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, providing gifts just as those offered by Prince Animiṣa, as described above.”
The third prince was named Rājavṛnda; the fourth prince was named Upacāra; the fifth prince was named Abhaya;
the sixth prince was named Gaganapriya; the seventh prince was named Subāhu; the eighth prince was named Mṛdu; the ninth prince was named...
Madhusū; the tenth prince was named Mṛdumati; the eleventh prince was named Maṅgānu;
the twelfth prince was named Madhupūrṇa; the thirteenth prince was named Manumata;
the fourteenth prince was named Macakrapūrṇa; the fifteenth prince was named Maśānu; the sixteenth—
The prince was named Vimala; the seventeenth prince was named Ajama; the eighteenth prince was named Anūna;
the nineteenth prince was named Arthamegha; the twentieth prince was named Indraka;
the twenty-first was named Nepālu; and the twenty-second was named Nikāju.
Twenty-third is named Moon-Mindfulness; twenty-fourth is named Sun-Mindfulness; twenty-fifth is named King-Mindfulness;
twenty-sixth is named Vajra-Mindfulness; twenty-seventh is named Patience-Mindfulness;
twenty-eighth is named Abiding-Mindfulness; twenty-ninth is named Remote-Mindfulness; thirtieth is named...
Ratnasmṛti; thirty-first, Rāhu; thirty-second, Rāhuvīrya; thirty-third, Rāhudatta; thirty-fourth, Ramadatta;
thirty-fifth, Deśadhana; thirty-sixth, Icchāvarta; thirty-seventh, Laṇḍa.
Forty-sixth, Pūrṇa; thirty-eighth, Rākṣasa-lūṣa; thirty-ninth, Rāyaśu; fortieth, Yama; forty-first, Jayapūrṇa;
forty-second, Jaya-lu; forty-third, Yamaku; forty-fourth, Jayatu; forty-fifth.
The first was named Ya-p'o-nu; the forty-sixth was named Ya-sa-nu; the forty-seventh was named Nam-mo-chu-ti;

the forty-eighth was named A-lan-ch'a-nu. These and others among the thousand sons of the noble king each, for three months, made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, providing all necessities such as clothing, food, bedding, medicine, and other requisites.
Their food, drink, bedding, and medicine were likewise all provided in the same manner as for the first prince;
furthermore, the various items offered as alms were each given in the number of eighty-four thousand.

According to their respective acts of giving, each of them conceived a resolve: some vowed to become the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, some sought to become a Brahmā King, some sought to become a Māra King, some sought to become a Wheel-Turning Sage King, some vowed to attain great wealth, and some sought the state of a Śrāvaka. Among these princes, there was not even a single one who sought the vehicle of a Pratyekabuddha, much less the Mahāyāna.
At that time, because of his acts of giving, the Wheel-Turning King again sought the rank of a Wheel-Turning King.

Then, for a full two hundred and fifty years, the Holy King and his thousand sons made offerings in this manner; at the end, each of them turned toward the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus to repent for all their shortcomings.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara went immediately to where the Buddha was and addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘I pray only that the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus will accept my offerings of robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicinal requisites for a full seven years.’”
At that time, the Tathāgata silently gave his consent, accepting the brahmin’s invitation.
Son of good family!
At that time, the brahmin provided all the necessities for the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, just as a noble cakravartin king would provide them.
"Good son! At a later time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again had this thought:

'I have now caused hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; however, I do not know what the aspiration of the Cakravartin King is—does he aspire to be a king of men?'"
Is it a heavenly king?
A śrāvaka? Or a pratyekabuddha?
Is it for the sake of seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
If I shall certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a future life, I will deliver those who have not yet been delivered;
I will liberate those who have not yet been liberated.
"Those who have not yet escaped birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, and affliction, may they all be made to escape them;
those who have not yet attained parinirvāṇa, may they be made to attain it.

If this is certain, then while I lie down at night, there shall appear to me in dreams the various devas, Māras, Brahmās, nāgas, yakṣas, and so forth, as well as the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, śrāvakas, śramaṇas, and brahmins, to explain for my sake the aspirations of this noble king—whether he seeks to become a human king or [something else]."
"Is it for the sake of seeking the heavenly kings?
Or is it for the sake of seeking the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the pratyekabuddhas, or anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi? "Good son!"

At that time, while the brahmin Ratnasāgara was asleep, he saw a radiance; by means of this light, he immediately beheld the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in every place throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Each of those World-Honored Ones, from afar, bestowed exquisite and beautiful flowers upon this brahmin.

Within the calyxes of these flowers, images of sun discs were visible; atop each sun disc was a magnificent canopy made of the seven precious gems. From each individual sun disc, sixty billion rays of light issued forth, and all these radiance beams entered the mouth of the brahmin.
He saw his own body extending for a full thousand yojanas, pure and free from defilement, like a clear mirror.
Within his abdomen, he saw sixty billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, sitting cross-legged in meditative absorption upon lotus flowers.
Furthermore, he saw a garland of suns encircling his body, and from within the various flowers issued forth musical instruments whose sounds surpassed those of the celestial musicians. "Good son!

At that time, the brahmin further saw the king with his body smeared with blood, running hither and thither in the four directions, his face and head resembling a pig as he devoured all kinds of insects."
Having devoured the insects, he sat beneath an eranda tree; then immeasurable sentient beings came to devour his body until only a skeleton remained.
Having cast off that skeleton, he repeatedly took on new bodies, and it was likewise so each time.

Thereupon, he again saw various princes who had assumed the faces of pigs, elephants, water buffaloes, lions, foxes, wolves, leopards, or monkeys; their bodies were smeared with blood, and they likewise each devoured immeasurable sentient beings while sitting beneath *eranda* trees. Furthermore, immeasurable sentient beings came to devour their own bodies until only skeletons remained; once the skeletons were gone, they repeatedly took on new bodies in this very same manner.
Or he may see the prince wearing a garland made of sumana flowers, riding in a small, dilapidated cart drawn by water buffaloes, galloping southward along an improper path.
Furthermore, he saw the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra Devānām Indra, and Mahābrahmā arrive at his location and address the brahmin, saying:
"Of all the lotuses surrounding you on every side, you should first take one flower and give it to the Wheel-turning King."
"Give one flower each to the princes; give the remaining flowers to the minor kings; then give them to your sons and the rest of the people.
Having heard these words, the brahmin immediately followed his instructions and distributed them all accordingly.

Having had such a dream, he suddenly awoke; rising from his reclining position and sitting up, he recalled all that he had seen in the dream and immediately understood that the Wheel-Turning Sage King’s aspirations were base, that he delighted in birth and death, and was greedily attached to worldly pleasures.
I now further know this:

"Among the princes, some may have aspirations that are lowly and inferior, because there are those among the princes who have resolved to seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas; therefore, I saw in my dream a *sumanā* flower used as a garland, and one riding a water-buffalo cart on an uneven path, galloping southward."

"For what reason did I see such great radiance in my dream last night, as well as the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, and the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in every place? It is because I have previously taught immeasurable sentient beings within Jambudvīpa and caused them all to dwell securely in the three bases of merit."

Therefore, in my dreams I have beheld radiant light and seen, in every direction, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, throughout immeasurable worlds; in each and every place, they have commanded all sentient beings within Jambudvīpa to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

I invited the Buddha Ratnagarbha and the community of bhikṣus, and for a full seven years I provided them with all that was necessary for their well-being; it is because of this that I saw the Buddhas of the ten directions bestow lotus flowers upon me in my dream.
Because I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I have thus seen in a dream the Buddhas of the ten directions bestowing precious canopies upon me.

Just as I saw the image of a sun disc within a lotus pedestal, immeasurable light entered my mouth; and I saw a great body filling a thousand *yojanas*, with a canopy of the seven treasures adorned by the sun; and I saw within my own belly sixty billion hundred thousand bodhisattvas sitting cross-legged upon lotuses, absorbed in the correct reception of *samādhi*.

"The lotus flowers that the Brahma King has commanded me to distribute—dreams such as these are beyond my understanding; only the Tathāgata can interpret them. I shall now go to the World-Honored One to inquire about their significance."
"For what cause and condition do you see these various things? "Good son!

At that time, the Brahmachārin Ratnasāgara, having passed the night, went to the Buddha's dwelling at the break of dawn. When the food and drink were prepared, he personally provided the water for washing and served the exquisite delicacies with his own hands."
Having finished eating and performed the ritual washing of the hands, and having completed the collection of the bowls, he sat upon a low seat to one side, desiring to hear the sublime Dharma.

At that time, the Holy King and his thousand sons, along with an immeasurable and boundless assembly of hundreds of thousands, departed from the city of Anzhoula, respectfully surrounding him as they proceeded toward the Jambūvana Garden. Upon reaching the outskirts of the garden, they descended from their vehicles according to the prescribed rites and walked on foot to where the Buddha was. They prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, and sat before the Buddha, desiring to hear the Dharma.
At that time, the brahmin related in detail to the Buddha everything he had seen in his dream.
The Buddha told the brahmin:

"Regarding the great radiance you saw in your dream, throughout the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions—equal in number to the sands of the Ganges—in every place where the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, were present, they gave you lotus flowers. Within the calyxes of these flowers were images of sun discs; their great light entered your mouth. This was because, during the previous two hundred and fifty years, you had taught immeasurable sentient beings within Jambudvīpa, causing them to abide in the three bases of merit, and further caused immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

Now, having again performed such a great act of giving to make offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, for this reason the Buddhas of the ten directions have bestowed upon you the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. The World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who are currently preaching the Dharma, have given you a lotus flower with silver stems and golden petals, lapis lazuli filaments, and agate anthers; within the calyx of the lotus is an image of a solar disc. Such matters as these are all the signs of your receiving the prediction.

"Brāhmaṇa! Regarding what you saw in your dream—the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently preaching the Dharma in every place throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and those wonderful canopies of the seven treasures which those World-Honored Ones have given to you, adorned as far up as the Brahma Heaven: in a future age, during the night, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. On that very night, a great fame shall pervade the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, reaching up to the Brahma Heaven. You shall obtain the mark of the invisible crown of the head (anavalokitamūrdha-lakṣaṇa), such that no one can surpass it; this is the first sign of your attainment of the Way."

"As for your dream in which you saw a great body surrounded by a garland of suns: in a future age, when you have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, those immeasurable sentient beings whom you previously taught within Jambudvīpa and caused to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* shall, at that very same time, also attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* throughout worlds in the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust.

Each of them shall likewise utter these words of praise: 'In the past, we were exhorted and transformed by the brahmin Ratnasāgara, whereby we resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; therefore, today we have all attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.'"
"Such-and-such World-Honored One is my true spiritual friend.
At that time, each of those Buddhas dispatched their own great Bodhisattvas for the purpose of making offerings to you.

The various bodhisattvas, by means of the manifold sovereign powers of their own buddha-fields previously attained—the lion’s play and the miraculous transformations of their supernormal knowledges—thereby made offerings.
At that time, after the bodhisattvas had made various kinds of offerings, they listened to the Dharma there and attained dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and patience.
Having heard and received the Dharma, these bodhisattvas each returned to their own lands and recounted to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, all the matters concerning your country.
"O Brahmin!
These dream events are all the signs of your attainment of the Way.
O Brahmin!"

As for your dream-vision of immeasurable billions of great bodhisattvas within your womb, sitting cross-legged in meditative absorption (samādhi-samāpatti) upon lotus flowers: once you have attained unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) in a future life, you shall further exhort and transform immeasurable billions of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, causing them not to regress from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

After you have entered unsurpassed parinirvāṇa, in a future age, there will be immeasurable Dharma-kings, World-Honored Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who shall likewise proclaim your name, saying:

"In the past, during eons as numerous as the atoms of the great earth, there was a certain Buddha; that Buddha, the World-Honored One, exhorted and transformed us, establishing us in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* so that we did not fall back. Therefore, we have now attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and become Kings of the True Dharma."
"O Brahmin! Such dreams as these are all the signs of your attainment of the Way.
"O Brahmin! [he continued.]

The human forms with the faces of pigs, up to those with the faces of monkeys, that you saw in your dream—whose bodies were stained with blood and who had devoured various kinds of insects, then sat beneath an eranda tree while immeasurable sentient beings pecked at and ate their bodies down to the skeletal remains, and after leaving the skeletal remains repeatedly took on new bodies—these are the foolish people who dwell in the three bases of merit, namely: generosity, self-discipline, and the virtuous restraint of body and speech.
Such persons as these shall be born in the heavens of Māra, where they will experience the suffering of decline and fall;

or if born among humans, they will undergo the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, pain, and despair, as well as the suffering of separation from the beloved, the suffering of encountering the hated, and the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks;
or if born among the hungry ghosts, they will experience the suffering of hunger and thirst.
If one is born among animals, there is the suffering of having one's head cut off amidst the darkness of ignorance;
if one is born in the hells, one undergoes various kinds of suffering.
Desiring not to be separated from such sufferings, one therefore dwells securely in the cultivation of the three bases of merit.

If such a deluded person aspires to become a celestial king or a wheel-turning sage king, or desires to rule over one set of four continents, or even to rule over all four sets of four continents, and thus devours all sentient beings, those very sentient beings will in turn devour such a deluded person.
In this manner, transmigrating through birth and death, one's journey is immeasurable.
O Brahmin! Such a dream is the very manifestation of having long endured birth and death.

"Brahmin! As for those people you saw in your dream, who were wearing garlands made of sumana flowers, riding in small, dilapidated carts yoked with water buffaloes, and galloping southward along an improper path—"

"Brāhmaṇa! This is the mark of one who abides in the three bases of meritorious action, who is able to discipline himself and attain tranquility, and who is oriented toward the vehicle of the śrāvaka."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin Ratnasāgara said to the wheel-turning king:
‘Great King, you should know that a human body is difficult to obtain.’”

Your Majesty has now attained this accomplishment without hindrance; for the appearance of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in the world is extremely rare, rarer even than the udumbara flower. To have a mind of desire well-tamed and to form virtuous vows is likewise exceedingly difficult.
"Great King!
If you now wish for the state of a deva or a human, this is the root of suffering.
If you desire to rule over one, two, three, or four of the four continents, this too is the root of suffering, leading to the cycle of birth and death."
"Great King!

Whether born as humans or devas, all are impermanent and lack any fixed nature, being like a swift wind. Such persons greedily cling to the pleasures of the five desires, their minds never finding satiety, just like a small child gazing at the moon reflected in water."
If there are those who aspire to receive the pleasures of negligence among gods and humans, they will repeatedly fall into hell and undergo immeasurable suffering;
if born among humans, they will experience the suffering of separation from loved ones and the suffering of encountering those one hates;

if born in the heavens, they will experience the suffering of decline and death, and shall again repeatedly undergo the suffering of entering a womb, as well as various sufferings of devouring one another and being deprived of life.
Their ignorance is like that of an infant, whose mind knows no weariness. Why is this?

Because they have been separated from spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), because they do not form virtuous vows, because they do not practice with diligence, because they fail to attain what should be attained, fail to understand what should be understood, and fail to realize what should be realized; thus, their ignorance is like that of an infant, lacking the capacity for discernment.
Only the bodhicitta can bring about the complete abandonment of all suffering without exception, yet instead one gives rise to weariness;
though one repeatedly undergoes suffering within the cycle of birth and death in the world, one instead finds it sweet and pleasurable, thereby causing all sufferings to increase even further.
"O Great King!
You should now contemplate that within birth and death there are such various kinds of suffering as these.
O Great King!"
Having now made offerings to the Buddha and planted roots of goodness, you should therefore give rise to deep faith within the Triple Gem.
Great King, you should know that the offerings previously made to the World-Honored Buddhas are the cause for great wealth in future lives;
the protection of the prohibitive precepts is the cause for rebirth among humans and devas in future lives.
Listening to the Dharma now is the very cause for wisdom in future lives.
Great King!
Since you have now accomplished such matters as these, you ought to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Then the king replied to the brahmin:
"I do not now seek such bodhi; my heart currently delights in birth and death.
For this reason, I practice giving, maintain the precepts, and listen to the sublime Dharma."
“Brahmin! Unsurpassed Bodhi is profoundly deep and difficult to attain.
At that time, the Brahmin spoke again to the Great King:
"This path is pure; one should single-mindedly fulfill its aspirations and seekings.
This path is free from turbidity because the mind is pure.
This path is upright because it is devoid of flattery and crookedness."
This path is pure white, for it is free from afflictions.
This path is vast, for it is without obstruction.
This path is receptive, for it involves much reflection.
This path is fearless, for it does not engage in any evils.
This path is great wealth, for it practices the perfection of generosity (dāna-pāramitā).
This path is pure, for it practices the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā).
This path is selfless, because it practices the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).
This path is non-abiding, because it practices the perfection of vigor (*vīrya-pāramitā*).
This path is undisturbed, because it practices the perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*).
This path is well-discriminated because it practices the *prajñāpāramitā*.
This path is the destination of true wisdom because it practices great compassion (*mahāmaitrī*).
This path is non-retrogressive because it practices great compassion;
this path is joyful because it practices great sympathetic joy;
this path is steadfast because it practices great equanimity.
This path is without thorns and brambles, for it is always far removed from thoughts of desire, ill-will, and affliction.
This path is peaceful and secure, for the mind is free from obstructions.
This path is without thieves, for it discerns forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles.
This path destroys Māra, because it skillfully discerns the aggregates, sense bases, and elements.
This path is free from Māra, because it severs all fetters.
This path is sublime and supreme, because it is beyond the contemplations of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
This path is all-pervasive, for it is that which is upheld by all Buddhas.
This path is a precious treasure, for it is all-encompassing wisdom.
This path is luminously pure, for the radiance of its wisdom is free from all obstructions.
This path is well-expounded, for it is protected by spiritual friends.
This path is impartial, for it severs both love and hatred.
This path is free from dust, for it is devoid of malice, defilement, and anger.
This path leads to a good destination, for it is free from all that is unwholesome.
Great King!
This path is such that it can lead to the place of peace and happiness, even unto Nirvana; therefore, you should resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Wheel-Turning Sage King replied to the great minister, saying:
"Brahmin! Now a Tathāgata has appeared in the world, with a lifespan of eighty thousand years."
Their lifespan is limited, and they are unable to completely cause all sentient beings to sever all evil karma and plant roots of goodness.

Having planted these roots of goodness, they establish them in the fruits of the noble ones, or cause them to attain dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and patience, or to attain the supreme and wondrous roots of goodness of a bodhisattva; the Buddhas then bestow upon them the prediction of their attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Or those with little wholesome root receive various pleasures among devas and humans; these sentient beings each individually experience the retribution of their own wholesome and unwholesome deeds. O Brahmin!
Among sentient beings, if there were even a single person devoid of roots of goodness, the Tathāgata would be unable to preach the Dharma for severing suffering.
Although the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, is a field of merit, if one lacks roots of goodness, he cannot cause them to sever all dharmas of suffering and affliction.

"Brahmin! I have now resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. When I practice the bodhisattva path, I shall cultivate and gather the Mahāyāna, enter into inconceivable Dharma-gates, and perform the work of a Buddha by teaching and transforming sentient beings; I never wish to resolve upon *bodhicitta* within the defiled lands of the five turbidities."

As I now practice the bodhisattva path, I vow that when I attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), the sentient beings of my world shall be free from all suffering and affliction.
If I obtain such a buddha-field, only then shall I attain unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha immediately entered a samādhi called ‘Beholding Various Adornments.’”

Having entered samādhi, he performed miraculous transformations and emitted great radiance. By the power of samādhi, he manifested within each of the ten directions a thousand Buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-worlds, with their various adornments. In some worlds, the Buddhas had already entered parinirvāṇa;
in some worlds, the Buddhas had just entered parinirvāṇa;
and in some worlds, Bodhisattvas were just sitting at the site of enlightenment, subduing the hosts of Māra beneath the Bodhi tree.
In some worlds, the Buddha turns the wheel of Dharma immediately upon attaining enlightenment;
in some worlds, he turns the wheel of Dharma only after a long time since his enlightenment;
and in some worlds, they are entirely filled with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the like, such that even the names "śrāvaka" and "pratyekabuddha" do not exist.
In some worlds, the Buddha teaches the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
in some worlds, there are no Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas;
and in some worlds, there are the five turbidities and evil conditions.
There are worlds that are pure, subtle, and wondrous, free from all turbidity and evil;
there are worlds that are lowly, base, and impure;
and there are worlds that are adorned, pure, and exquisitely beautiful.
In some worlds, the lifespan is immeasurable;
in some worlds, the lifespan is short;
and in some worlds, there are great conflagrations.
In some worlds there is the calamity of great water;
in some worlds there is the calamity of great wind;
and in some worlds an eon is about to begin its formation.
There are worlds whose formation has been completed;
there are such immeasurable worlds as these, all of which are universally illumined by subtle and wondrous light, causing them to become manifest.
"At that time, the great assembly all beheld such immeasurable, pure Buddha-worlds with their various adornments.
Then, the Brahma-cultivator Ratnasāgara addressed the Wheel-turning King: 'Great King!'"

Now that you have been able to behold these various adornments of the Buddha-worlds, you should therefore now resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, seeking whatever Buddha-land you desire according to your own will.
“Good son! At that time, the Wheel-Turning King joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
By what karma do the bodhisattvas take up pure worlds?
By what karma do they take up impure worlds?
And by what karma is their lifespan immeasurable?
"By what karma is one's lifespan short?
The Buddha told the Holy King:
"Great King, you should know that all Bodhisattvas, by the power of their vows, take up pure lands and remain free from the five turbidities and evils."
"Furthermore, there are bodhisattvas who, by the power of their vows, seek out the five turbidities and evil worlds.
At that time, the Holy King came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I shall now return to the city and, in a secluded place, contemplate with focused mind and make a vow.
Just as I have beheld the characteristics of the Buddha-lands, free from the five turbidities and evils, I pray to seek a world of pure adornment."
The Buddha said to the Holy King:
"You should know that now is the time.
O son of noble family!
At that time, the Wheel-Turning King prostrated his head at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, circumambulated them three times to the right, and then withdrew and departed.

He returned to the city and went to his residence; within his own palace, in a secluded spot, he sat upright with a focused mind, contemplating and cultivating the various adornments for his own buddha-field.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara next addressed Prince Animiṣa: ‘Good son!...’”

You, too, should now resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. All the three bases of merit that you have practiced—namely, giving, self-restraint, and the wholesome governance of body and speech—as well as all other pure and virtuous deeds you have performed, should be combined and dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Prince spoke these words:
"I should now first return to the palace and sit upright in a secluded place to reflect."

"If I am truly able to resolve my mind toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I shall return to the presence of the Buddha; before the Buddha, I shall resolutely resolve my mind, vowing to take up various pure and wondrous Buddha-lands."
At that time, the Prince prostrated himself with his head at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, circumambulated them three times to the right, and then departed.
Upon reaching his own palace, he sat upright in a secluded spot with single-minded concentration, contemplating and cultivating the various adornments for his own buddha-field.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin again addressed the second prince, speaking these words: ‘Good son!’”
"You should now resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In this way, the thousand sons of the noble king were all instructed and led to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, the brahmin further instructed and transformed eighty-four thousand minor kings, as well as ninety-two billion other sentient beings, causing them to resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The entire great assembly spoke these words: "O Brahmin!
We shall now each return to our respective abodes and, sitting upright with single-minded concentration in a quiet place, contemplate and cultivate the various adornments of our own Buddha-worlds."

Thus, for seven years, this great assembly remained with single-minded tranquility; each sat upright in their own respective dwelling place, contemplating and cultivating various adornments for their own Buddha-worlds.
“Good son! At a later time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again thought to himself:
‘I have now taught and transformed immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
"I have now invited the Buddha and the great assembly to provide for all their needs and comforts for seven years.

If I shall surely attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the future and my vow is fulfilled, I shall exhort the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others, causing them to make offerings to such a great assembly."
"Good son! At that time, the brahmin immediately called to mind the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa. Good son!"

At that time, the Heavenly King, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the brahmin, was respectfully surrounded by hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable yakṣas as he went to the brahmin’s location; that very night, he stood before the brahmin and spoke these words: “Brahmin!
"What instructions do you wish to give? The brahmin asked, "Who are you?"
Vaiśravaṇa said: "Brahmin! Have you ever heard of King Vaiśravaṇa?"
"I am that very person.
What do you command?
At that time, the brahmin said:
"Welcome, Great King! I am now making offerings to such a great assembly; you may assist me in making these offerings together.
King Vaiśravaṇa said:
"I shall respectfully follow your instructions and provide whatever you require.
The brahmin spoke again:
"Great King!..."

"If you can comply with my wishes, I shall cause all the yakṣas to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Furthermore, I shall proclaim to the yakṣas: 'Those who desire merit and those who desire *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* should cross the great ocean daily to fetch ox-head sandalwood, aloeswood, various other incenses, and diverse flowers, and bring them here; they should also, as I do, make daily offerings to the Buddha and the Saṅgha.'"
At that time, having heard these words, the Heavenly King returned to his abode, beat the drum to assemble the yakṣas and rākṣasas, and proclaimed these words: "Do you all know?"
In this Jambudvīpa, there is a Wheel-Turning Sage King named Araṇemin, and there is a brahmin named Ratnasāgara, who is the great minister of that sage king.
"For a full seven years, I have invited the Buddha and the Sangha and provided them with all that they require for their comfort.
You all should feel sympathetic joy toward this merit; having felt such joy, by means of these roots of goodness, you should resolve your minds to dedicate them toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“Good son! At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of yakṣas and others who, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words:

‘If the brahmin Ratnasāgara, during the seven years, makes offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, providing them with all necessities for their comfort, we rejoice in his roots of goodness and the resulting merit.’”
"By virtue of these roots of goodness from this act of sympathetic joy, may we attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Heavenly King spoke again, saying:
"Listen attentively, all of you!"

Those who wish to obtain merit and roots of goodness may cross the great ocean every day for the sake of that brahmin, gathering ox-head sandalwood and aloeswood to prepare cooked food for the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.
At that time, ninety-two thousand yakṣas spoke simultaneously:
"O Heavenly King!

For the next seven years, we shall constantly procure this ox-head sandalwood and aloeswood to provide for that brahmin, so that he may prepare cooked food for the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus."
Furthermore, forty-six thousand yakṣas also spoke with one voice, saying:
"We shall take various exquisite incenses and give them to that brahmin, to offer as worship to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."
Furthermore, fifty-two thousand yakṣas likewise spoke with one voice, saying:
"We shall gather various kinds of exquisite flowers and present them to that brahmin, as an offering to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."
Furthermore, twenty thousand yakṣas likewise spoke with one voice:
"We shall take the essence of all flavors and provide it to that brahmin, who shall prepare food and drink to offer as an oblation to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus."
At that time, there were also seventy thousand yakṣas who spoke with one voice, saying:
"We shall go and provide food and drink as an offering for the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin again had this thought:
‘Next, I shall exhort the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa, and the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.’”

Having formed this thought, at that time the three kings immediately perceived his intention and went to the place where the brahmin was, returning eventually to their own abodes. Virūḍhaka, together with hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Kumbhāṇḍas; Virūpākṣa, the Heavenly King, together with hundreds of thousands of immeasurable koṭis of nayutas of nāgas; and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with hundreds of thousands of immeasurable koṭis of nayutas of gandharvas—likewise, they all resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Good son! At that time, the brahmin then further called to mind the Four Great Kings of the second continent. By the power of the Buddha, those four kings came to where the brahmin was and spoke these words: ‘Brahmin!’”
"What do you wish to command me now?
The brahmin replied,
"I now exhort you and your retinue to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
The Four Heavenly Kings replied,
"We shall respectfully follow your instructions.
They immediately returned to their respective abodes and, together with all their retinues, collectively resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In this manner, even up to the ten billion kings of Vaiśravaṇa throughout the trichiliocosm resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Likewise, the ten billion kings of Virūḍhaka, the ten billion Virūpākṣas, and the ten billion Dhṛtarāṣṭras, each together with all their respective retinues, also resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin again thought to himself:

‘If, in the future, I shall certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and if my vows are fulfilled and I obtain my own benefit, I shall cause all the devas to likewise obtain a portion of this merit, and I shall also exhort them to resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
"If, in a future life, I shall surely attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi by means of these roots of goodness, may the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven come here to meet me;
may the Son of Heaven of Yāma, the Son of Heaven of Tuṣita, the Son of Heaven of Nirmāṇarati, and the Son of Heaven of Paranirmita-vaśavartin also come here to meet me."

“Good son! At that time, after the brahmin had formed this thought, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the King of the Yāma Heaven, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven all came to this place. They met with the brahmin and spoke these words: ‘Brahmin!’”
"What do you wish to command now?
The brahmin replied, "Who are you?"
Then the five heavenly kings each announced their names and spoke again to the brahmin:
"What do you command us to do?
Is there no need for us to serve in this great assembly?"
The brahmin replied:

“Great King, you should know that all the wondrous jeweled palaces, towers, and pavilions in your celestial realm, as well as the various jeweled trees, clothing trees, incense trees, flower trees, and fruit-bearing vines; the celestial garments, thrones, cushions, rugs, and mats; the exquisite jeweled vessels and necklaces; the celestial banners, parasols, silken streamers, and other various adornments; and all the diverse musical performances of the devas—[all these are surpassed].”
"You may use such items as these to adorn this Jambūvana Grove in various ways, making offerings to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus.
Then the five heavenly kings spoke thus:
"We respectfully obey your instructions."
Then the various Heavenly Kings each returned to their respective abodes. The King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven addressed the son of heaven Virūḍhaka;

the King of the Yāma Heaven addressed the son of heaven Atapama; the King of the Tuṣita Heaven addressed the son of heaven Rucika; the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven addressed the son of heaven Kautūhalika; and the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven addressed the son of heaven Nanda. Each spoke these words:

"You must now descend to the realm of Jambudvīpa and use all these various things to adorn that Jambuvana Garden. Hang up various necklaces and spread out various seats, just as the various Heavenly Kings have adorned [their realms]. For the sake of the Tathāgata, construct a precious high tower, making it exactly like the precious towers found here in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

Having heard these instructions, those devaputras immediately descended into Jambudvīpa. That very night, they adorned the Jambuvana grove in various ways, embellishing it with all kinds of jewel trees and even celestial banners. For the sake of the Tathāgata, they constructed a pavilion of the seven precious substances, just like the jeweled pavilions found in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven.
These five devaputras, having taken various precious objects and adorned the Jambudvīpa garden in manifold ways, immediately returned to the heavens and each addressed their respective king:

"Great King, you should know that we have already gone to decorate that garden; all its features are exactly as described, without any difference. For the sake of the Tathāgata, we have constructed a pavilion of the seven treasures, which is equal to and indistinguishable from the treasure pavilions found in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven."

“Good son! At that time, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the King of the Yāma Heaven, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven immediately came to Jambudvīpa, went to where the brahmin was, and spoke these words: ‘Brahmin!’”
"I have now, for the sake of the Buddha and the Sangha, adorned this garden; what further instructions do you have?
Please tell me. The brahmin replied:
"Each of you, within your respective domains, possesses the sovereign power to assemble the various devas. Convey my words to them:

'Within Jambudvīpa, there is a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara who, for seven years, has invited the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and an immeasurable assembly of monks to provide them with all necessities.'"

"You all should now give rise to sympathetic joy regarding this merit; having given rise to sympathetic joy, you should resolve your minds to dedicate it toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. For this reason, you should go to where the Buddha is, see the World-Honored One and the assembly of bhikṣus, provide whatever offerings they require, and listen to and receive the sublime Dharma."
At that time, the five heavenly kings, having heard these words from the brahmin, each returned to their respective abodes.
Then Śakra-devānām-indra, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, immediately assembled the devas and addressed them, saying:

"You should know that within Jambudvīpa there is a Cakravartin King named Araṇemin, who has a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara, who is the king’s chief minister. This minister has invited the Buddha, the World-Honored One, along with immeasurable billions of monks, and for a full seven years will provide them with all necessities. I have already, on behalf of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, taken various precious objects to adorn that Jambūvana Garden."

By means of these roots of goodness, you all should give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy; having given rise to sympathetic joy, you should resolve to dedicate this merit toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and thereby cause the brahmin to obtain his wish as he has prayed for it.
"Good son! At that time, hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of Trāyastriṃśa devas joined their palms in reverence and spoke these words:
'We now give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward these roots of goodness; by virtue of this sympathetic joy, may we all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.'"

"The King of the Yāma Heaven, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven—each of these likewise gathered the various devas and addressed them, saying:"

"You should know this: within Jambudvīpa there is a Cakravartin King named Araṇemin, and there is a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara who is that king’s chief minister. He has invited the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and immeasurable billions of monks to provide for all their needs for a full seven years. I have already, on behalf of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, taken various precious objects to adorn that Jambūvana Garden. Because of these roots of goodness and conditions, you should give rise to sympathetic joy; having given rise to sympathetic joy, resolve your minds upon dedication toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, so that the brahmin may obtain his wish."
“Good son! At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of devaputras in each of the four heavens, who, with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words:
‘We now give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward these roots of goodness; by virtue of this sympathetic joy, may we all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
At that time, each of the five kings spoke to them, saying:

"O you! You should now go to Jambudvīpa to see the Buddha Ratnagarbha and his assembly of bhikṣus, and there pay them homage, circumambulate them, revere them, make offerings to them, honor them, and praise them."
“Good son!

At that time, each of the five celestial kings, during the night, led their respective hosts of devaputras, devakanyās, young males, and young females, along with other retinues numbering hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas, surrounding him from front and back as they came to the place where the Buddha was. They prostrated at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, and having listened to the Dharma from the Buddha until dawn, they ascended into the air and remained there. They scattered various celestial flowers—*utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, *puṇḍarīka*, *sumana*, *vārṣika*, *atimuktaka-jambuka*, *māndārava*, and *mahāmāndārava*—over the great assembly like falling rain, while also playing celestial music as an offering.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again had this thought:

‘If in the future I shall certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and if my vows are fulfilled so that I obtain my own benefit, I shall further teach and transform all the asuras, causing them all to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”

"Good son! At that time, after the brahmin had formed this thought, five asura kings came to where the brahmin was. Furthermore, hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of asuras—men, women, boys, and girls—following the brahmin’s instruction, resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and went to the Buddha’s presence to listen to and receive the sublime Dharma."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again had this thought:

‘If in the future I shall certainly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and if my vows are fulfilled so that I obtain my own benefit, I shall further teach and transform the celestial Māra Pāpīyān, causing him to resolve upon the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”

"Good son! At that time, Māra Pāpīyas immediately knew what the brahmin was thinking in his heart. He then brought hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of men, women, boys, and girls to the brahmin’s location, where they paid respect as instructed and resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; even those who merely listened to the Dharma did likewise."
The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Second;
The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Third.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
The Third Chapter on Great Giving, Part Two.
The Buddha again addressed Śāntamati: "Good son!
At that time, the brahmin again had this thought:

"If, in the future, I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and my vows are fulfilled so that I obtain my own benefit, I shall next teach and transform the Great Brahmā Heaven King, causing him to resolve upon the mind of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, the Brahmā King, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the brahmin, went to where the brahmin was and spoke these words:
"What do you wish to command?"
The brahmin asked, "Who are you? The Brahma King replied:
"I am Mahābrahmā. The brahmin replied, "Welcome, Great King!"
"You may now return to the heavens to assemble the devas and convey my words to them:

'In Jambudvīpa there is a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara, who for seven years has invited the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and an immeasurable assembly of monks, providing them with all necessities. You should now rejoice in this merit; having rejoiced, you should resolve your minds upon and dedicate it toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.'"
At that time, having heard these instructions, the Brahma King immediately returned to the heavens, assembled the various Brahmās, and addressed them, saying:

"You all should know that within Jambudvīpa there is a Wheel-Turning Sage King named Araṇemin, who has a great Brahmin named Ratnasāgara, who is the chief minister of that Sage King. He has invited the Buddha, the World-Honored One, along with an immeasurable assembly of monks, and for the duration of seven years, he shall provide for all their needs."

"You all, by means of these roots of goodness, should give rise to sympathetic joy; having given rise to sympathetic joy, you should resolve your minds to dedicate them toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, so that the Jewel Ocean may attain his aspirations as they are."
“Good son! At that time, hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of Brahmā sons joined their palms in reverence and spoke these words:
‘We now give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward these roots of goodness; by virtue of this sympathetic joy, may we all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.’”
He further addressed them, saying:

"You should now go to Jambudvīpa, where you shall see the Buddha Ratnagarbha and the community of bhikṣus; there you must pay homage, circumambulate them, show reverence, make offerings, honor, and praise them."

"Good son! At that time, the Brahma King, surrounded before and behind by hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of Brahma sons, came to the place where the Buddha was. He prostrated his head at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, and listened to and received the sublime Dharma."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmin again had this thought:
‘I shall further convert and teach the kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven in the second continent.’”
By the power of the Buddha, they each came to where the brahmin was and each spoke these words:
"What do you command? The brahmin asked:
"Who are you? they asked. Each replied, "I am [the king of] the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, and so on, up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven."
The brahmin replied, "Each of you should return to your respective dwellings and convey my words to them:

'In Jambudvīpa there is a Wheel-Turning King named Araṇemin, who has a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara, who is the king's chief minister; for a full seven years, he has made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus.'"
You, sirs, should rejoice in these roots of goodness; having rejoiced, you should resolve your minds to dedicate them toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and all the Kings of the Heavens up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven heard these words, they each returned to their respective abodes and immediately assembled the devas, addressing them thus:

"You should know that within Jambudvīpa there is a Wheel-turning Sage King named Araṇemin, and a great brahmin named Ratnasāgara who serves as this Sage King’s chief minister; for a full seven years, he has made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus."

"By virtue of these roots of goodness, you should give rise to sympathetic joy; having given rise to sympathetic joy, you should resolve your minds to dedicate [the merit] toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Good son! At that time, the assembly of devas joined their palms in reverence and spoke these words:
'We now give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward these roots of goodness; by virtue of this sympathetic joy, may we all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.'"
He spoke further, saying:

"You all should now go to the place where the Buddha is; there you shall see the World-Honored Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, and you should prostrate to them, circumambulate them, revere them, make offerings to them, honor them, and praise them."

“Good son! At that time, the kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, up to and including the king of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, each accompanied by hundreds of thousands of immeasurable billions of nayutas of devaputras, devakanyās, devaputrakas, and devakanyakās, as well as their other retinues, came to the place where the Buddha was, surrounding him before and behind. They prostrated at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, and listened to and received the sublime Dharma.”
The five asura kings of the second continent, the celestial Māra Pāpīyān, and Mahābrahmā likewise did so.

Third, fourth, fifth, and so on, up to the Buddha-worlds of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system—ten billion Trāyastriṃśa heavens, ten billion Yāma heavens, ten billion Tuṣita heavens, ten billion Nirmāṇarati heavens, ten billion Paranirmita-vaśavartin heavens, ten billion of the five Asura kings, ten billion Māra Pāpīyas, and ten billion Great Brahmā Kings, along with their immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of retinues—all resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. By the power of the Buddha, they all came together to this four-continent world, arrived at the place where the Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of the Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus, and listened to and received the sublime Dharma.
At that time, the great assembly completely filled this place, such that there was no vacant space throughout the trichiliocosm.
"Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again had this thought:"
"I have now already accomplished the conversion of ten billion Vaiśravaṇa Heavenly Kings, up to ten billion Mahābrahmā Heavenly Kings; thus, all my vows have now attained mastery."
He further thought:

"If in a future life I shall certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and achieve my own benefit as I have vowed, may the Buddha, the World-Honored One, manifest various supernormal transformations for the sake of the great assembly; and by means of his supernatural power, may all beings in this trichiliocosm—beasts, hungry ghosts, those in the hells, and human beings alike—be entirely freed from all suffering and affliction, and experience nothing but pure happiness."
Before each and every sentient being, there appears a manifested Buddha who exhorts that being, causing them to resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, immediately knowing the thoughts in the mind of Ratnasāgara, at once entered the *anupatāpa* samādhi."

At that time, after the World-Honored One had entered this samādhi, he manifested such transformations of supernatural power (*ṛddhi-vikurvaṇā*): from each and every pore, he emitted immeasurable and boundless rays of light. These rays were subtle and wondrous, pervading and illuminating the trichiliocosm as well as the hells. Sentient beings suffering from freezing cold encountered them and became warm; sentient beings tormented by heat encountered them and became cool; sentient beings afflicted by hunger and thirst encountered them and became satiated, experiencing the most sublime bliss.

Before each and every sentient being, there was a manifested Buddha, adorned with the thirty-two marks and encircled by necklaces, further embellished in succession by the eighty minor characteristics.
Having experienced such happiness, those sentient beings reflect thus:
"By what cause have we been freed from suffering and affliction to receive this sublime joy?"

At that time, the sentient beings saw the transformation Buddha, adorned with the thirty-two marks and successively graced by the eighty minor characteristics. Having seen this, they each spoke these words:
"By the grace of this one who has perfected great compassion, we have been enabled to leave behind all suffering and affliction and receive sublime bliss."
At that time, the sentient beings gazed upon the Honored One’s countenance with hearts full of joy.
Then, the transformation Buddha addressed all the sentient beings:

"You should all together recite 'Namo Buddha' and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. From this point forward, you shall no longer undergo suffering, but shall constantly experience the foremost and most wondrous bliss."
Those sentient beings immediately spoke these words:
"Homage to the World-Honored One!
We resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
By these roots of goodness, they sever all evils and, passing away from that state, are reborn among humans.

Sentient beings afflicted by heat and distress, having encountered this light, immediately attain coolness; freed from the sufferings of hunger and thirst, they experience various sublime joys, until they are even reborn among humans.
Just as it is with those in the hells, the animal realm, and the hungry ghost realm, so it is with humans.

After that light has universally illumined all worlds, it returns, circles the Buddha’s body three times, and enters through the crown of his head. At that time, immeasurable and boundless numbers of humans, devas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, nāgas, and rākṣasas attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, there were incalculable sentient beings who attained dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and patience.

At that time, immeasurable devas from among the humans of Jambudvīpa, for the sake of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the community of bhikṣus, used all manner of celestial objects to adorn and decorate the Jambūvana Garden outside the city walls, making it indistinguishable from the celestial realms themselves. These people then thought:
"We should now go to behold this, and to see the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus, so that we may listen to and receive the Dharma."

“Good son! At that time, every day there were hundreds of thousands, immeasurable billions of nayutas of men, women, boys, and girls who came to where the Buddha was, prostrated their heads at the feet of the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, circumambulated him three times to the right, and with reverence, made offerings, paid respect, and offered praise, desiring also to see this Jambūvana Garden.”

The park had twenty thousand gates, all composed entirely of the seven precious gems; before each gate were spread five hundred couches made of the seven precious gems, upon which sat five hundred brahmins, each on his own.

If there are sentient beings who wish to enter this garden, these brahmins will immediately exhort and transform them, causing them to resolutely take refuge in the Triple Gem and resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; only then will they permit them to enter this garden to see the World-Honored One and the assembly of bhikṣus, where they may pay homage, circumambulate, revere, make offerings, honor, and praise them.
“Good son! At that time, during those seven years, the brahmin converted and instructed incalculable devas, causing them to become definitively established in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
Furthermore, he causes countless dragons, asuras, gandharvas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, pretas, animals, hell-beings, and humans to all definitively abide in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

“Good son! At that time, after seven years had passed, the brahmin took eighty-four thousand golden wheels—excluding the divine wheel—and eighty-four thousand white elephants adorned with the seven treasures—excluding the elephant-treasure—up to eighty-four thousand kinds of musical instruments; with such items as these, he desired to offer them to the Buddha and the assembly of monks.”

"At that time, for seven years, the Wheel-Turning Sage King’s mind was free from the desire for sensual pleasures, free from the desire for ill-will, free from the desire for ignorance, free from the desire for pride, free from the desire for territory, free from the desire for children, free from the desire for precious women, free from the desire for food and drink, free from the desire for clothing, free from the desire for flowers and incense, free from the desire for vehicles, free from the desire for sleep, free from the desire for pleasure, free from the desire for self, and free from the desire for others. Throughout these seven years, he did not harbor even a single thought of desire; he sat constantly without reclining, had no perception of day or night, no perception of exhaustion, and likewise no perceptions of sound, fragrance, flavor, or touch."

Within that state, he constantly perceives each of the ten directions as being like ten thousand Buddha-lands, filled with the pure adornments of Buddha-worlds as numerous as the atoms of dust; he does not see Mount Sumeru or the various small mountains, nor the dark and obscure spaces between the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains, nor the sun, moon, stars, or the palaces of the various devas.
What they see is only pure and adorned Buddha-lands.
Having seen these things, they take them up according to their vows.
Just as a Wheel-Turning Sage King enjoys happiness for seven years, so too do they behold various pure and adorned Buddha-worlds and vow to take up a supreme, wondrous, and pure Buddha-land.

The Crown Prince Animiṣa of the Wheel-Turning Sage King, along with his thousand sons, eighty-four thousand minor kings, and ninety-two trillion sentient beings, each for seven years remained free from desire in their hearts; they were even devoid of perceptions of fragrance, taste, or touch. Each entered meditative concentration in a secluded place and contemplated, whereby they beheld, in every direction of the ten worlds, as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in ten thousand Buddha-fields, including all the adornments of those Buddha-worlds. They did not see Mount Sumeru or the various small mountains, nor the Great and Small Iron Ring Mountains, nor the dark spaces between them, nor the sun, moon, stars, or the palaces of the devas.
As for what they saw, they saw only pure and adorned buddha-fields.
According to what they saw, they accordingly took hold of it.
Thus, throughout the seven years, all these great assemblies each attained the practice of various dharma-gates; some vowed for pure buddha-fields, while others vowed for impure buddha-fields.

“Good son! At that time, after seven years had passed, the brahmin took various kinds of the seven treasures and offered them to the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus. Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”

I have already exhorted and converted the Wheel-Turning Sage King, causing him to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; he has returned to his residence to sit in quiet meditation and reflection, even refusing to allow a single person to enter.

I further exhorted and transformed the king’s thousand sons, causing them to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. These princes likewise each returned to their respective dwellings, where they sat in meditation and contemplation, not even permitting a single person to enter.

Eighty-four thousand minor kings and nine hundred twenty billion sentient beings likewise resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; each sat upright in a quiet place, reflecting in meditation, and would not allow even a single person to enter.
“World-Honored One!

Now, please cause this Wheel-Turning King and others to arise from samādhi and come to the Buddha’s presence; and likewise, those whom I have previously taught and inspired to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may they all assemble here at the place of the Buddha, World-Honored One. May they sit upright with single-minded focus and receive the pure Buddha-world, never regressing from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Having received their predictions from the Buddha, they shall then take up their respective lands, as well as their names and clans.”

"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha entered the Samādhirāja-samādhi. Having entered this samādhi, various colored lights—blue, yellow, red, white, and purple—issued from his mouth, like those of a wheel-turning monarch in meditative concentration. Before each of them appeared a manifested Brahmā King, who spoke these words:

'You all should now arise from your concentration and go to where the Buddha is; behold the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the community of bhikṣus, and pay homage, circumambulate, revere, make offerings, honor, and praise him.'"
"You should know that after the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara has completed the dharma assemblies during these seven years, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, shall now travel again to other lands."
When the Wheel-Turning King and his retinue heard these words, they immediately arose from their meditative concentration.

At that time, the various devas in the void performed various musical performances. "In the world-system of Saṃtāraṇa, during the eon called Susthita, when the lifespan of humans is eighty thousand years, a Buddha shall appear in the world named Ratnagarbha. At that time, there will be a universal monarch named Amitaviśuddhi who rules over the four continents; this king’s crown prince shall be named Avalokiteśvara."

Having made offerings for three months to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and the community of bhikṣus, by virtue of these roots of goodness, after the latter half of the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa—as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—he shall attain Buddhahood, with the name Tathāgata Sarvaprakāśaprabhāsaguṇaparvatendrarāja, and his world shall be named Sarvaratnasamudgata.
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses to Avalokiteśvara:
"The merit of great compassion should now arise once more;
the earth shall shake in six ways, as well as all the Buddha-fields."
"The Buddhas of the ten directions have already bestowed upon you the prediction that you shall become a Buddha;
therefore, you should rejoice. "Good son!

At that time, having heard these verses, Prince Avalokiteśvara felt great joy in his heart. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and went forward to prostrate at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the second prince, Nyama, saying: ‘Good son!...’”
The pure karma of merit that you have now performed, for the sake of all sentient beings attaining omniscience, should be dedicated toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Good son! At that time, the prince sat before the Buddha, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
'World-Honored One!'"

Just as I have previously made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus during these three months, together with all my pure conduct of body, speech, and mind—may I now dedicate all such merit toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

I do not wish for an impure or defiled world; rather, may my own land and my bodhi tree be adorned with various jewels and precious bodhi trees, just like those of Avalokiteśvara’s world, and may I attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).

Furthermore, I vow that when the Buddha Universal Radiance of Merit first attains the Way, I shall be the first to request him to turn the wheel of Dharma; throughout the entire duration of his preaching, I shall practice the bodhisattva path in the interim.
After this Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa and the True Dharma has been extinguished, I shall subsequently attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in due order.

When I become a Buddha, the buddha-deeds I perform, all the various adornments of my world, and the duration of the True Dharma remaining in the world after my parinirvāṇa—all such matters shall be exactly equal to those of that Buddha, without any difference.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the second prince: "Good son!
As for the greatest world that you now aspire to, in a future age you shall attain such a great world-realm, exactly as you have vowed."

"Good son! In a future age, you shall attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi) in such a supreme world-system, and your name shall be the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Sthitabhadra-ratnaparvatarāja."
“Good son! Because you have made the vow to take up a great world, for that reason I shall name you Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
At that time, Mahāsthāmaprāpta came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, then as I now pay homage to the Buddha, may all the Buddha-worlds in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, tremble in six ways, and may the *sumanā* flowers rain down; and may the Buddhas currently residing therein each grant me a prediction of enlightenment.”

“Good son! At that time, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, standing before the Buddha, prostrated himself with his head to the ground. Immediately, worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down sumanā flowers; the various Buddhas, World-Honored Ones currently residing therein, each bestowed upon him a prediction of enlightenment.”
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses for the sake of Mahāsthāmaprāpta:
“O you of firm strength and merit, Arise now!
The great earth trembles, And *sumana* flowers rain down.”
"The Buddhas of the ten directions have already bestowed upon you the prediction that in the future you shall attain the status of a venerable one among humans, devas,
and Brahmās. "Good son!"

At that time, having heard these verses, Mahāsthāmaprāpta felt great joy in his heart; he immediately rose, joined his palms, and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the third prince, Rājasaṃgha, saying: ‘Good son!’”
Now, you should dedicate this accumulation of merit and pure karma that you have performed toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, so that all sentient beings may attain all-knowledge.
"Good son! At that time, the third prince sat before the Buddha, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
'World-Honored One!'"

Just as I have previously made offerings to the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus for three months, together with all my pure conduct of body, speech, and mind—may all such merit and virtue now be entirely dedicated toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Regarding my present vow, I cannot attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this impure world, nor do I wish to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi quickly.

When I practice the bodhisattva path, I vow that all sentient beings within the infinite and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions whom I transform shall resolve their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, be firmly established in the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and be exhorted, transformed, and settled in the six *pāramitās*. I further vow that they shall all, before me, attain Buddhahood and preach the Dharma in each of the ten directions within Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in Buddha-fields equal to the sands of the Ganges River; and that at that time, I may see them all clearly and universally with my purified divine eye.

May I, when acting as a bodhisattva, be able to perform such immeasurable buddha-works; may my practice of the bodhisattva path in future ages be without limit; and may all sentient beings whom I transform have minds as pure as the Brahma-heaven. Only after such beings are born into my realm shall they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, thereby purifying and adorning this buddha-field with these qualities.

May the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges within this trichiliocosm, become a single buddha-field. May this world be surrounded by great walls of precious jewels set with the seven treasures, these walls reaching in height up to the Formless Realm. May its ground be made of pure, deep-blue lapis lazuli, free from all dust, stones, soil, sand, filth, and thorns. Furthermore, may there be no harsh textures, nor even the name of "woman. May all sentient beings be born through transformation, not consuming solid food but taking the joy of the Dharma and samādhi as their sustenance. May there be no vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, but only bodhisattvas, who are free from greed, hatred, and delusion, all practicing the holy life and filling the land.

When he was born, his hair and beard fell away of their own accord, and he was clothed in the three dharma-robes. Immediately upon birth, as he desired food, there appeared a precious vessel in his right hand, and naturally, within it, a bowl filled with a hundred kinds of exquisite flavors was provided.
At that time, the bodhisattvas reflected:
"We should not consume this morsel of food; we shall now take it to the ten directions to offer it to the Buddhas and their assemblies of śrāvakas, as well as to the poor.
There are hungry ghosts who suffer the pains of hunger and thirst with their bodies aflame; we shall go to their places and provide for them sufficiently."
"We ourselves should practice the food of the samādhi of Dharma-joy.
Having formed this thought, they attained a bodhisattva samādhi called "Inconceivable Conduct."

Having attained this samādhi, they immediately acquire unimpeded supernormal powers and travel to the presence of the Buddhas currently residing in immeasurable and boundless worlds. There, they make offerings to the Buddhas and their assemblies of bhikṣus, and provide for the poor, even down to the hungry ghosts. Having performed such acts of giving, they preach the Dharma for them; then, at the time of the meal, they travel back and forth and return to their own lands.
They likewise use clothing, precious jewels, and all necessary items to make offerings to the Buddhas, down to the hungry ghosts, in the same manner, before finally using them for themselves.

May my world be free from the eight difficulties and the suffering of unwholesome states; may it be such that even the names of receiving precepts, violating precepts, and repentance do not exist there.

May my world be constantly filled with immeasurable varieties of rare treasures, and with trees of precious garments such as have never before existed or been seen or heard of in the worlds of the ten directions—such that even if one were to speak their names for a hundred million years, one could never exhaust them.

May the bodhisattvas in my world, if they wish to see a golden color, be able to see it at will; if they wish to see a silver color, they shall likewise see it at will. When seeing silver, they shall not lose the appearance of gold; when seeing gold, they shall not lose the appearance of silver. It shall be the same for all kinds of precious jewels—crystal, lapis lazuli, musaragalva, agate, and red pearls—they shall be able to see them at will according to their desire.

If one wishes to see agarwood, tagara, tamāla-pattra sandalwood, aloeswood, and red sandalwood, or wishes to see pure sandalwood, one shall see them according to one's desire. If one wishes to see aloeswood, one shall likewise see it as desired; when seeing the aloeswood, the sandalwood is not lost, and when seeing the sandalwood, the aloeswood is not lost. It is the same for all others; whatever various aspirations one has, they shall all be fulfilled.

May my world be without sun or moon; may the bodhisattvas therein possess great radiance that emerges spontaneously according to their original aspirations, capable of illuminating hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds. Because of this radiance, there shall be no distinction between day and night: when the various flowers bloom, it shall be known as the daytime; when the flowers close, it shall be known as the nighttime. May the world be perfectly harmonious, free from cold and heat, as well as from old age, sickness, and death.

If there is a bodhisattva in their final birth who attains anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in another direction, they do so by passing away from this very body in the Tuṣita heaven of that other direction and becoming a buddha.
If, after I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I do not enter parinirvāṇa within that realm, then at the time of my parinirvāṇa, I shall abide in the midst of space.

Whatever the bodhisattvas desire to obtain arises spontaneously. On the periphery of that world, there are always hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of natural musical instruments. These instruments do not produce sounds associated with sensual desires; rather, they constantly produce the sounds of the six pāramitās, the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha of bhikṣus, the sound of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, and the sound of profound meaning. And the bodhisattvas, according to their respective understandings, comprehend these various sounds.
“‘World-Honored One!

When I practice the bodhisattva path, may all the various adornments, various necklaces, various appearances, and various [features] of hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeyas of Buddha-worlds as I have seen them...’”
May all such adornments as these— the various dwelling places and various aspirations— be fully accomplished in my world;
excepting only the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and likewise excluding the age of the five turbidities,
the three evil realms, Mount Sumeru, and the great and small Iron Ring Mountains.
There are no soils, sands, pebbles, great oceans, or forests; there are only trees made entirely of jewels.
There are no flowers other than those surpassing all that exist in the heavens, save for the celestial *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.
Free from all foul odors and impurities, it is filled everywhere with exquisite fragrances throughout that land.
