All these bodhisattvas are in their final birth; not a single one among them is born in another place, except for those who are destined to attain buddhahood in other directions, who pass away from Tuṣita Heaven and achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

“‘Bhagavān! When I practice the bodhisattva path, there shall be no limit; I must surely attain this subtle and wondrous fruit of a pure buddha-field, filled with bodhisattvas in their final birth. Among these bodhisattvas, there shall not be a single one who was not taught by me, who first resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and established themselves in the six *pāramitās*. All such bodhisattvas were first taught by me to resolve their minds and establish themselves in the six *pāramitās*. In this Saṃdṛśana world-system, if they enter my realm, all sufferings and afflictions shall entirely cease.’”
“‘World-Honored One!
When I practice the bodhisattva path, I must first accomplish such rare and extraordinary deeds as these;
only then shall I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a future age. I pray that the Bodhi...’”
The name of the Bodhi tree was Selection of Excellent Jewels; it was fourteen thousand worlds in length and breadth, and its fragrance and radiance pervaded thirteen thousand great trichiliocosms.
Beneath the Bodhi tree, a diamond throne made of various precious jewels was formed, equal in length and breadth to five or four worlds; such was that throne.
It is named "Fragrance of Wisdom that Skillfully Selects Quiescence. It is fourteen thousand yojanas high;

upon this seat, I sit cross-legged and, within a single thought-moment, attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, remaining thus from my parinirvāṇa until the end, always seated upon the vajra beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment.

Without the seat being dissolved or destroyed, one should further manifest immeasurable Buddhas and assemblies of Bodhisattvas, dispatching them to other Buddha-worlds to teach and transform sentient beings.

Each manifested Buddha, for the duration of a single meal, shall preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma for all sentient beings; within that single meal-time, they shall cause [immeasurable and boundless beings to...]
All sentient beings resolve their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
immediately upon generating that resolve, they become non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
In this manner, these emanation Buddhas and the assembly of bodhisattvas constantly perform such rare and marvelous deeds.

Once I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may all sentient beings in other worlds see my body. If there are sentient beings who behold my body with their eyes—its thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics—may they all become certain of attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and until they reach *nirvāṇa*, may they never be separated from seeing the Buddha.
May all sentient beings within my realm have their six sense faculties complete and free from any deficiency.
If there are bodhisattvas who wish to see me, wherever they may dwell—whether walking, coming, sitting, or lying down—may they all be able to see me.

As soon as these bodhisattvas have resolved their minds [on enlightenment], they immediately see me sitting at the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree. Upon seeing me, all previous points of doubt and obstruction regarding the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*) are severed even before I have spoken, and they also attain a profound understanding of the meaning of the characteristics of phenomena.
May my lifespan in the future be immeasurable and beyond counting, except for that of the All-Knowing One; may the lifespan of the bodhisattvas also be thus.

Once I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a single thought-moment, may there be immeasurable bodhisattvas within that same single thought-moment whose hair and beards fall away naturally and who don the three dharma-robes, continuing so until their parinirvāṇa. During this interval, may not a single person among them grow out their hair and beards or wear secular clothing; rather, let all of them wear the robes of śramaṇas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the third prince: "Good son! Excellent!"
Excellent! You are a truly virtuous great man.
Intelligent and wise, you are well-versed in understanding and are able to make such a most difficult and great vow.
The merit you have performed is most profound and most profound, inconceivable, and the work of subtle wisdom.
O son of good family!
For the sake of sentient beings, you have yourself made such a weighty vow to take up a wondrous land; for this reason, you are now named Mañjuśrī.

In a future age, after the passing of two *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* (Ganges-sand) quantities of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*, and upon entering the third immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*, there will be a Buddha-world in this southern direction named Pure and Stainless Jewel-Array (*Vimala-ratna-vyūha*), and this world-system of Saptarṣi will also be included within it.

That world is adorned with various kinds of splendors; therein you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, receiving the name Prabhūtaratna Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. The assembly of bodhisattvas there will all be pure, and your vows shall be fully accomplished, exactly as you have spoken.

"Good son! When you practiced the bodhisattva path, you planted various roots of goodness in the presence of immeasurable billions of Tathāgatas. Therefore, all sentient beings regard you as medicine; your pure mind can destroy afflictions and increase all roots of goodness."
At that time, Mañjuśrī came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If my vows are fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, I pray that the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds of the ten directions will shake in six ways; that the Buddhas therein, currently preaching the Dharma, will grant me a prophecy; and that all sentient beings will receive joy and bliss, as if a Bodhisattva were freely sporting in the second dhyāna. May the heavens rain down māndārava flowers, filling the entire world, and from within these flowers may there constantly emerge the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṃgha of Bhikṣus, the six pāramitās, the powers, and the fearlessnesses.”
"May such signs as these appear immediately when I pay homage to the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

Having spoken these words, he immediately prostrated before the Buddha, touching his head to the ground. At that very moment, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds in the ten directions shook in six ways; devas rained down *māndārava* flowers from the sky, and all sentient beings experienced joy and bliss, like a bodhisattva entering the second dhyāna and sporting with mastery. At that time, the bodhisattvas heard only the sounds of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha of bhikṣus, as well as the sounds of the six *pāramitās*, the ten powers, and the fearlessnesses.
At that time, the bodhisattvas from other directions, having seen and heard these matters, marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and each addressed their own Buddha, saying:
"By what causes and conditions does this auspicious omen arise?"
The Buddhas of the ten directions each addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"This is a portentous sign because the Buddhas of the ten directions have each extensively bestowed the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi upon Mañjuśrī."
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses for Mañjuśrī:
“O Victorious One of Vast Mind, you may now arise once more;
The Buddhas of the ten directions have already bestowed upon you the prediction of enlightenment.”
In a future age, you shall attain the path of the Honored and Victorious One;
the great earth of this world will tremble in six ways,
and all sentient beings, their needs fulfilled, shall experience happiness.

“Good son! At that time, having heard these verses, Mañjuśrī felt great joy in his heart. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and went forward to prostrate at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.”
The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll Three.
The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll Four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Four, Part Two: The Original Prophecy of All Bodhisattvas. "Good son!
At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara addressed the fourth prince, Nagaṇu, saying: '... [and] even his making of vows was likewise so.'"
At that time, the Buddha addressed Agana, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! When you practice the bodhisattva path, you shall shatter the mountains of afflictions of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings with vajra-wisdom, perform great buddha-work, and only thereafter attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“O son of good family!
For this reason, I shall address you as Vajrajñānaprabhāsaguṇa.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsaguṇa:

“Good son! In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges River has passed and you enter the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges River, there will be a world named Amoghadarśin (Unblinking) located to the east, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten Ganges-river-sands’ worth of worlds.

"Good son! Within this you shall attain Buddhahood, and your name shall be the Tathāgata Samantabhadra, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣa, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
"Whatever adornments exist in that Buddha-world shall all be fully present, exactly as you have vowed. "Good son!

When the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha bestowed the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsa-guṇa, at that time there were immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of devas in the void who praised him, saying:"
"Excellent! Excellent!
he exclaimed, and offered as worship *gośīrṣa-candana*, *agaru*, *tagara*, *tamālapatra*, along with powdered incense, raining them down like rain.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsaguṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, I now pay homage to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."

I only pray that all the subtle and exquisite fragrances of the devas throughout worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions—whether among the various classes of sentient beings in the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, the heavens, or among humans—if they should smell this fragrance, may all ailments of physical and mental suffering be entirely removed.
"Thus, with his head and face touching the ground.
Son of good family!
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsaguṇa had spoken these words, he immediately prostrated himself, bowing his head and face to the Buddha."

At that time, throughout worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there was a pervasive and subtle fragrance; all sentient beings who smelled it were able to distance themselves from the sufferings and afflictions of body and mind.
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses to the Bodhisattva Vajramatiprabhāsaśrī:
“Vajra-wisdom can shatter [all obstacles]; you may now rise up.
Throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, sublime fragrances pervade everywhere.”
"Bestowing peace, happiness, and joy upon immeasurable sentient beings,
they shall in the future attain Buddhahood as the Unsurpassed Knower of the World.
"O son of good family!"

At that time, having heard these verses, the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsaguṇa was filled with joy; he immediately rose, joined his palms, and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the fifth prince, Abhayadatta, and so forth; his generation of the bodhicitta was likewise in this manner.”
At that time, the prince replied to the brahmin, saying:
"The aspiration I now hold is not to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within this impure world."

I vow that when I attain Buddhahood, there shall be no hells, animals, or hungry ghosts within my world; its ground shall consist entirely of deep-blue lapis lazuli, and its detailed adornments shall be exactly like those of the Lotus World.
At that time, Prince Abhaya held a lotus flower and offered it to the Buddha Ratnagarbha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, then by the power of the Buddha, may I now, before the Buddha, obtain the samādhi of seeing all manner of various adornments."

Furthermore, I pray that the heavens will rain down various lotus flowers as large as chariot wheels, filling the Buddha-lands of the ten directions—equal in number to the atoms within worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—and may we all behold them from afar.

“Good son! After Prince Abhayamati had spoken these words, by the power of the Buddha, he immediately attained the Samādhi of Seeing All Various Adornments. Then, from the heavens, there rained down various immeasurable lotus flowers as large as chariot wheels, filling the Buddha-lands of the ten directions as numerous as the atoms within lands equal to the sands of the Ganges River. The entire great assembly was able to see this from afar; having witnessed this event, they attained joy and bliss.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed Prince Abhaya:

"Good son! You have been able to make such a profound and subtle great vow to take up a pure and adorned buddha-field, and you have further been able to swiftly attain the samādhi of seeing all manner of adornments. Because your vow is not in vain, the heavens have rained down such immeasurable lotus flowers."
“World-Honored One!
If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may these flowers all remain suspended in the air and no longer fall.”
Then the Buddha Ratnagarbha said to Prince Abhaya:
"Son of good family!
You have now swiftly sealed the void with various lotus seals; therefore, I name you 'Void Seal' (Gaganamudrā)."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā: "Good son!

In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed, and upon entering the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world named Padma located to the southeast of this buddha-field, at a distance of hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. There, you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and your name shall be Padmottara Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. All the members of your great assembly shall consist solely of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, their number being immeasurable and beyond calculation.
"The lifespan of that Buddha shall be immeasurable and boundless; all his vows shall be fulfilled and entirely accomplished.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā prostrated with his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, then rose and joined his palms. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses for the sake of Gaganamudrā:
“Good son, you should know: There are those who act for their own benefit, Who are able to sever the fetters of affliction, And who constantly cause themselves to attain tranquility.”
The merit you have received and maintained is as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and equal to the atoms of all worlds; it is perfected and never lost.
In a future age, you shall achieve the unsurpassed path.
"Just as with the Buddhas of the past, they are all equal and without distinction. "Good son!
Upon hearing these verses, the Bodhisattva Ākāśamudrā felt great joy in his heart."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara addressed the sixth prince, Ākāśa, and so forth, until his generation of the mind of enlightenment was likewise as described.”
At that time, Prince Āmra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
My present aspiration is not to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in this impure world; in brief, it is as was the aspiration of Gaganamudrā."
"Bhagavān! If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may there spontaneously appear in the worlds of the ten directions—
equal in number to the sands of the Ganges— wondrous canopies made of the seven treasures, arrayed in the void above."
It stands there, covered above by a net of pure gold, adorned with bells made of the seven treasures hanging down;
from the precious bells of that canopy, there constantly issue forth the sounds of the Buddha,
the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus, as well as the sounds of the six pāramitās, the six supernatural powers, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and so forth.
When the sentient beings of the world hear them, they immediately resolve their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;

those who have already resolved their minds shall immediately attain the stage of non-retrogression. The sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, as well as the sounds of the fearlessnesses, which issue from the precious bells, completely fill the void of the worlds of the ten directions; this is all due to the power of the Buddha.
I have now been able to hear it myself.
World-Honored One!

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, I pray that I may now realize the Sun-like Samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, may all roots of goodness be increased. Having attained this samādhi, I further pray that all Buddhas will grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
When the prince had spoken these words, by the power of the Buddha, he immediately attained the Sūryaprabha-samādhi (Sunlight Samādhi).
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the prince, saying: "Excellent!"
Excellent, son of good family!

Your aspiration is most profound, most profound. By virtue of these causes and conditions of profound merit, at that very moment, throughout the worlds of the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there spontaneously appeared wonderful canopies made of the seven treasures, which remained suspended in the void above, arrayed in rows. Nets of pure gold covered them from above, and they were fully adorned with bells made of the seven treasures; those bells constantly emitted the sounds of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, up to the sounds of the fearlessnesses.

At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings who, upon hearing this sound, immediately resolved their minds on anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; for this reason, you are named "Sunlight Radiance of Space."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganasūryaprabha:

"In a future age, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. After one asaṃkhyeya-kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed, and upon entering the second asaṃkhyeya-kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, there will be a world named Candrasūrya located two asaṃkhyeya-kalpas of Buddha-fields to the east of here. Therein, you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your title shall be Dharmeśvarabhadrarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
At that time, having heard this prediction, the Bodhisattva Ākāśasūryaprabha prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
Then, the World-Honored One spoke these verses for the sake of Ākāśasūryaprabha:
“Good man, arise now! Well done, you who have disciplined yourself!”
With pure and gentle great compassion, for the sake of all sentient beings,
he delivers them and causes their suffering to cease; ultimately abiding on the other shore,
with wisdom that skillfully discerns, he leads them to the unsurpassed path.

“Good son! At that time, having heard these verses, the Bodhisattva Ākāśasūryaprabha was filled with joy in his heart. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.”
"At that time, the brahmin Ratnasāgara again addressed the seventh prince, Subāhu, and so forth, until his generation of the mind was likewise as described.
Then, the prince said to the Buddha:"

"My present aspiration is not to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in this impure world. I pray that in all worlds of my future lives, there shall be no names for hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, or women; nor shall there be birth from a womb, Mount Sumeru, the great and small Iron Ring Mountains (*cakravāḍa*), hills, mounds, elevations, stones, sand, filth, thorns, evil winds, trees, forests, great oceans, rivers, suns, moons, days, nights, darkness, or foul-smelling places. Among the various classes of sentient beings, there shall be no excrement, urine, nasal mucus, saliva, or bodily impurities, and their bodies and minds shall never experience any unpleasant things."

The ground is made of agate, free from all dust and soil, and is adorned with hundreds of thousands of immeasurable precious jewels; there are no weeds, but only exquisite and wonderful *mandārava* flowers, and various jeweled trees serve as decorations.

Beneath those jewel trees were exquisite jeweled canopies, as well as various kinds of precious garments and flower garlands, all manner of precious necklaces, fragrant flowers, and musical instruments, along with various precious vessels and wonderful jewels; with these and other such things, the trees were adorned.
In this world there is no distinction between day and night; the seasons are known by the opening and closing of flowers.

The bodhisattvas dwelling therein are born spontaneously within golden flowers. Once born, they all attain the various adorned samādhis, and by the power of these samādhis, they are able to see the Buddhas currently residing in worlds throughout the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust.
Within this samādhi, in the space of a single thought-moment, one is fully endowed with the six supernormal powers:
by means of the divine ear, one hears the sounds of all present Buddhas preaching the Dharma in worlds throughout the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust;
by means of the knowledge of past lives, one knows the events of former existences throughout kalpas as numerous as the motes of dust in a single buddha-field.
By means of the divine eye, they see all the various adornments of the Buddha-worlds in the ten directions;

by means of the knowledge of others' minds, within a single thought-moment, they know the thoughts and intentions of sentient beings in as many worlds as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world, and until they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they never lose this samādhi.

At the time of early dawn, gentle and pure winds arose from the four directions, blowing subtle fragrances and scattering various flowers; by the power of these winds, the bodhisattvas arose from their samādhi, and having arisen from samādhi, they immediately attained such supernormal powers of mastery as they desired.

By this power, in a single moment of thought, they are able to reach as many Buddha-worlds in each of the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-land, making offerings to the present Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and requesting to receive the sublime Dharma; then, within that same single moment, they return to their own original lands without any hindrance.

The various bodhisattvas, seated cross-legged within the calyxes of *mandārava* and *mahāmandārava* flowers, contemplate the Dharma-gate, namely: "If they wish to see me in whichever direction I am located, may they all be able to see me according to where their bodies are directed;
if there are those who have doubts or obstructions regarding the profound Dharma, may these be immediately eliminated upon seeing me;
and if there are those who inquire about the meaning or wish to hear the Dharma, may they immediately attain deep understanding and be free from doubt upon seeing me."

All bodhisattvas have a profound understanding of non-self and that which belongs to the self; therefore, they are able to relinquish the faculty of body and the faculty of life, and all are certain never to regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
In that world, there shall be no mention whatsoever of unwholesome deeds, nor shall there be the names of receiving precepts, breaking precepts, violating precepts, or repenting for transgressions.

All sentient beings shall possess bodies endowed with the thirty-two marks and the strength of Nārāyaṇa; furthermore, until they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, not a single person shall have any of their six sense faculties impaired or incomplete.

As soon as all sentient beings are born, their hair and beards fall off naturally, they don the three Dharma robes, and attain the Samādhi of Skillful Discernment; furthermore, until they reach Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall never lose this state midway.
All sentient beings shall attain the harmony of all roots of goodness, and not a single person shall suffer from old age or illness.

When these bodhisattvas reach the end of their lives, they shall sit in the full lotus posture and enter the fire-samādhi, spontaneously incinerating their own bodies. Once their bodies have been consumed by fire, pure winds shall blow upon them from the four directions, and their relics shall be scattered throughout the worlds of the ten directions where no Buddha resides; immediately, these relics shall transform into maṇi-jewels, just like the precious jewels possessed by a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin).

If there are sentient beings who see or touch [this], may they all be prevented from falling into the three evil realms; until they reach nirvana, may they not undergo any suffering. Immediately upon casting off their bodies, may they be reborn in the presence of a presently living Buddha in another direction, where they may consult and receive the sublime Dharma, resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and never again fall back.

When all sentient beings reach the end of their lives, their minds shall remain in meditative concentration without distraction, and they shall not undergo the sufferings of being separated from those they love.

After passing away, they shall not fall into the eight difficult states or into worlds devoid of Buddhas; rather, until they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they shall always behold the Buddhas, receive and inquire about the sublime Dharma, and make offerings to the Saṅgha.
All sentient beings therein are free from greed, anger, delusion, attachment to loved ones, jealousy, ignorance, and pride.

The world contains no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; the entire great assembly consists solely of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who fill that land. Their minds are supple and free from the turbidity of craving; they are firm and non-regressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, having attained all samādhis.
The world is entirely pure, filled with radiant light; throughout the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust, all shall hear of my world.

All the subtle and wondrous fragrances within my world pervade the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust. The sentient beings in my world constantly experience happiness, and the sound of suffering has never been heard there.

"Bhagavān! When I practice the bodhisattva path, I shall not set a limit; I must now adorn such a pure buddha-field that all classes of sentient beings are made pure and fill its realm, and only then shall I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
“World-Honored One!

When I attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I shall emit immeasurable and boundless light that illuminates the ten directions, reaching as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms in a thousand Buddha-fields, so that all sentient beings therein may see my thirty-two marks from afar. Instantly, they shall sever all afflictions—greed, anger, ignorance, jealousy, delusion, and pride—and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, obtaining dharanis, samadhis, and patience according to their aspirations.”
Because they see me, all sentient beings in the Cold Hells obtain warmth and joy, just as when a Bodhisattva enters the second dhyāna.

Because they see me, their bodies and minds experience the foremost sublime bliss, and they resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; when their lives end, they shall certainly be born in my Buddha-world, and having been born, they immediately attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
It is likewise for those in the Hot Hells and so forth, as well as for animals and hungry ghosts.
The radiance seen by the various devas is ten times greater than that;
may my lifespan be immeasurable, boundless, and beyond counting, except for those with all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvajñā*).
"World-Honored One!..."

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, may the Buddhas currently residing in the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds of the ten directions praise me. May other sentient beings who hear this sound of my praise plant roots of goodness with the aspiration to be swiftly reborn in my land; upon the end of their lives, they shall certainly be born in my land, with the sole exception of those who commit the five heinous crimes, destroy the True Dharma, or slander the sages.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, may all sentient beings in the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds of the ten directions who hear my voice and make a vow to be born in my world, see me surrounded by a great assembly at the time of their death. At that moment, I shall enter the *anāvaraṇa* (unobstructed) samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, I will appear before them and preach the Dharma for them. By hearing the Dharma, they shall immediately sever all suffering and affliction, and their hearts will be filled with great joy. Because their hearts are joyful, they shall attain the *ratnāloka* (jewel-light) samādhi. By the power of this samādhi, their minds shall attain mindfulness and the realization of non-arising (*anutpāda-kṣānti*), and after their lives end, they shall certainly be born in my realm.”
If there are sentient beings in other worlds who lack the seven riches, who do not wish to cultivate and practice the three vehicles,
and who do not wish to be born among humans or devas; who furthermore do not cultivate any roots of goodness or the three bases of merit,
but instead engage in unrighteous conduct, are defiled by it, are attached to evil desires, and are solely devoted to wrong views— just as [in this world]...
"May I, for the sake of these sentient beings, enter the Samādhi of Unafflicted Tranquility. By the power of this samādhi,
when those sentient beings reach the end of their lives, may I stand before them with a great assembly to preach the sublime Dharma,
further manifesting all that exists within the Buddha-lands, and exhorting them to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
When sentient beings hear of this mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they immediately conceive deep faith in me;
filled with joy and peace, they promptly resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
This causes those sentient beings to sever their suffering and affliction; having severed their suffering and affliction, they then obtain the *sūryapradīpa-prabhāsa* (Sun-Lamp Radiance) samādhi.
“...having dispelled the darkness of delusion, after the end of his life, he will immediately be reborn in my realm.
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised him, saying: “Excellent!”
"Excellent!
You are now able to make such a subtle and sublime great vow.
[The Bodhisattva replied: "World-Honored One!"

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may all Buddha-worlds in the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust, be rained upon with *utpala* and *bala* incense, as well as sandalwood incense, gośīrṣa-candana incense, and various kinds of powdered incense.
If there are sentient beings who, wherever they may be, hear this fragrance, may they all resolve their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
May I now attain the Vajra-Vow Samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, may I be able to see from afar all the fragrances being rained down throughout all worlds.

“Good son! At that time, after the prince had spoken these words, he immediately attained samādhi. He personally beheld Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust, wherein there were all kinds of fragrances—such as uḍrāra-bhara incense, gośīrṣa-candana, and various powdered incenses—and he also saw, in every direction, immeasurable sentient beings with palms joined in reverence, giving rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha addressed the prince, saying:
"O son of good family!

Your vow has already been fulfilled. After the heavens rained down various kinds of subtle and wondrous incense, there were immeasurable sentient beings who, with palms joined in reverence, gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. For this reason, I name you Siṃhagandha (Lion Incense)."

In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed and you have entered the second asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, forty-two asaṃkhyeya kalpas worth of Buddha-worlds—measured by the number of atoms in those worlds—will lie above this world in the upward direction. There will be a world named Blue Fragrance Radiance Stainless; in that land, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and you shall be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Prabhāsa-vimala-dṛḍhagandha-śrī-rāja.
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha prostrated himself before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, touching his head to the ground.
Then, the Tathāgata spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha:”
"The Teacher of Gods and Humans has arisen; receiving all offerings,
he delivers beings from birth and death, causing them to leave behind suffering and affliction,
severing all fetters and defilements."
"In a future life, you shall become the Honored One of gods and humans.

"Good son! At that time, having heard this verse, the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha was filled with great joy. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and sat down not far from the Buddha to listen to the Dharma once more."
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the eighth prince, Mṛdu, and so forth; his generation of the aspiration was likewise as described above.”
At that time, the prince came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

My present vow is that I must cultivate the bodhisattva path in this impure world, and furthermore, I shall cultivate and adorn ten thousand impure worlds, making them as pure and adorned as the world-system ‘Stainless Radiance of Blue Fragrance. I shall also teach and transform immeasurable bodhisattvas, causing their minds to be pure and free from defilement, so that they all turn toward the Mahāyāna and completely fill my world; only then shall I attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
"Bhagavān! When I practice the bodhisattva path, may I surely surpass all other bodhisattvas. Bhagavān!"

For seven years, I have sat upright in meditation, contemplating the pure merits of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the merits of the various adornments of Buddha-lands. At that time, I immediately attained the Samādhi of Seeing All Various Adornments and advanced in the practice of eleven thousand Bodhisattva samādhis.
World-Honored One!
We pray that when all bodhisattvas of the future practice the bodhisattva path, they too shall all attain such a samādhi as this.
World-Honored One!

May I attain the Samādhi of the Supreme Banner that Transcends the Three Times; by the power of this samādhi, may I see all the infinite and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, and in every place where the Buddhas of the present dwell, transcending the three times, they preach the True Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

"Bhagavān! May I attain the *avaivartika-samādhi*. By the power of this samādhi, may I, within a single thought-moment, see all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—as numerous as motes of dust—and all Śrāvakas surrounding them with reverence. May I, at each and every such Buddha’s presence, attain the *anāśrita-samādhi*. By the power of this samādhi, may I manifest transformation bodies (*nirmāṇakāya*) that simultaneously reach the abodes of Tathāgatas as numerous as the motes of dust in a single Buddha-field, to offer worship and prostrations. May each of these bodies, adorned with various unsurpassed precious jewels, flowers, incense, ointments, powdered incense, and exquisite music, make offerings to each and every Buddha."
"Bhagavān! May each of my individual bodies practice the bodhisattva path for as many eons as there are drops of water in the great ocean, before each and every Buddha.

May I attain the Samādhi of All-Bodies-Manifestation; by the power of this samādhi, may I, in a single thought-moment, stand before each and every Buddha and know as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms within a single Buddha-land."
World-Honored One!

May I attain the Samādhi of the Power of Merit; by the power of this samādhi, may I reach before each and every Buddha as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a single buddha-land, and with subtle and wondrous praises, extol those Buddhas.
"World-Honored One!
May I attain the Unblinking Samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, may I, within a single thought-moment, see all Buddhas filling the infinite and boundless worlds throughout the ten directions."
World-Honored One!

May I attain the Samādhi of Non-contention; by the power of this samādhi, may I, within a single thought-moment, behold all the pure and wondrous worlds of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

“World-Honored One! May I attain the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. By the power of this samādhi, may I manifest the body of a hell-being and enter into the hells to preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma to the sentient beings therein, exhorting them to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Once those sentient beings have heard this Dharma, they shall immediately resolve upon unsurpassed bodhicitta; they shall then pass away and be reborn among humans. In whatever place they are born, they shall always encounter Buddhas; wherever they encounter Buddhas, they shall hear the Dharma; and having heard and received the Dharma, they shall immediately abide in the stage of non-retrogression.”

The gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, as well as devas, nāgas, ghosts and spirits, yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, butchers, executioners, merchants, courtesans, animals, and hungry ghosts—all such multitudes were likewise caused to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

There are sentient beings who, according to their place of birth, obtain various physical forms; I shall divide my body according to their karma, experiencing suffering and pleasure as well as various crafts and skills. May I manifest such transformed bodies, teaching and transforming them according to their actions.
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings each with different voices, may I, according to their various sounds, preach the Dharma for them so that each may be gladdened; through that gladdening, may I exhort and establish them, causing them not to retreat from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”
“World-Honored One!

I shall instruct all sentient beings throughout ten thousand Buddha-lands to purify their minds, so that they are free from the poisons of karma, conduct, and afflictions, and not even a single person among them shall fall under the sway of the four māras, let alone many.”

"If I were to adorn ten thousand buddha-fields so that they are as pure as the world-system of Blue Fragrance Radiance Stainless, belonging to the Buddha Light Without Stain Honored Fragrance King, with all its various subtle and exquisite adornments, only then would my own body and my retinue fulfill the vows of that Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha."
“‘World-Honored One!

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may all sentient beings in ten thousand Buddha-worlds sever all suffering and affliction, attain a supple mind, and attain a disciplined mind; may each of them, within their own four-continent world-system, see the Buddha, the World-Honored One, currently preaching the Dharma; may all sentient beings spontaneously obtain various kinds of rare treasures, flowers, incense, powdered incense, and unguents, as well as various garments and various banners and streamers, each using these to make offerings to the Buddha; and having made offerings to the Buddha, may they all resolve to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta.’”
“World-Honored One!
Because we have now fully attained the power of the Samādhi of Various Adornments, we are all able to see these various matters from afar.
Having spoken these words, they immediately saw everything exactly as they had wished.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised Amitāyu, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! In this world of yours, the ten thousand Buddha-lands surrounding the four directions are pure and adorned. In future ages, you shall further transform and guide immeasurable sentient beings to purify their minds, and you shall further make offerings to immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones."

"Good son! For this reason, I now change your name to Samantabhadra (Universal Worthy). In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges River has passed, during the final period of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges River, in the northern direction—beyond sixty *Ganges*-sands of Buddha-lands from this world—there shall be a world named Jñānāmbu-suvimala-guṇa (Pure Virtue of the Water of Wisdom). There you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and your title shall be Jñāna-dṛḍha-nāda-vaiśvarya-lakṣaṇa-rāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat."
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra prostrated himself with his head to the ground before the Buddha Ratnagarbha.
Thereupon, the Tathāgata spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra:”
"Arise, O Excellent Guide! You have already attained what you vowed;
you are well able to discipline sentient beings, causing them all to attain one-pointedness of mind, to cross over the river of afflictions, and to be liberated from all evil dharmas."
"In future lives you shall become a lamp of light, a teacher for the gods and the people of the world. "Good son!
At that time, ten thousand people in the assembly conceived indolence in their hearts and, with one voice, spoke these words:"
“World-Honored One!
In a future age, we shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within such a pure and adorned buddha-field—namely, those pure worlds cultivated by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.”
"Bhagavān! We must fully cultivate the six pāramitās; because we have fully cultivated the six pāramitās, each of us shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in our respective Buddha-fields."
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha immediately bestowed upon these ten thousand people the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, saying: 'Good sons!'"

When Samantabhadra Bodhisattva attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you shall all simultaneously attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within the pure lands of ten thousand buddhas cultivated by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; there shall be one thousand buddhas, all sharing the same name: Jñānajvalana-ghoṣarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
Furthermore, there were one thousand Buddhas all sharing the same name, King of Increasing Marks and Honored Sound;
another one thousand Buddhas all sharing the same name, King of Good Stainless Honored Sound; another one thousand Buddhas all sharing the same name, King of Honored Sound Free from Fear;
another one thousand Buddhas all sharing the same name, King of Good Stainless Light Honored Sound; and another fifteen hundred Buddhas all sharing the same name.
Sūryaghoṣarāja, furthermore there were five hundred Buddhas all named Sūryaratnagarbharājarāja;
furthermore there were five Buddhas all named Rativighuṣṭarājarāja; furthermore there were two Buddhas both named Sūryaprabha;
furthermore there were four Buddhas all named Nāgeśvara; furthermore there were eight Buddhas all named Bhayaviśāradaśrīrājamati.
Furthermore, there were ten Buddhas all named Light of Separated Sounds;
eight Buddhas all named Renowned Sound; eleven Buddhas all named Manifesting the Sound of Dharma;
nine Buddhas all named King Renowned for Meritorious Dharma; and twenty Buddhas all named Inconceivable King.
Furthermore, there were forty Buddhas all named Ratnaketu-prabhāsa-guṇarāja;
another Buddha named Vijñapti-saṃjñā-rāja; seven Buddhas all named Acintya-ghoṣa;
three Buddhas all named Jñānagarbha; fifteen Buddhas all named Jñāna-parvata-ketu; and five [Buddhas...]
There were ten Buddhas, all equally named King Ocean of Wisdom; furthermore, there were thirty Buddhas, all equally named King of Great Powerful Resonant Sound;
furthermore, there were two Buddhas, both equally named Mountain Merit Kalpa; furthermore, there were eighty Buddhas, all equally named Pure Wisdom Diligence;
furthermore, there were ninety Buddhas, all equally named King of Noble Marks and Lineage; furthermore, there were one hundred Buddhas.
There were eighty Buddhas all named Honored King of the Sound of Stainless Thunder of Good Wisdom;
furthermore, there were forty Buddhas all named Honored King of Supreme Bodhi;
furthermore, there were two Buddhas both named King of the Flower on the Mountain of Wisdom-Awakening; furthermore, there were two Buddhas... [and so forth].
There was one named Guṇaparvatajñānabodhi; furthermore, there were three Buddhas all named Vajrasimha;
furthermore, there were two Buddhas both named Śīlaprabhāsa; furthermore, there were two Buddhas both named Upadarśanavardhana;
furthermore, there was one Buddha named Amitaprabha; furthermore, there were three Buddhas all named Siṃhavikrīḍita.
Furthermore, there were two Buddhas both named Akṣayajñānagiri; again, two Buddhas both named Ratnaprabha;
again, two Buddhas both named Vimalajñāna; again, nine Buddhas all named Jñānaprabha;
again, two Buddhas both named Siṃhaghoṣa; again, two Buddhas both named...
The Universal King of Merit was followed by two Buddhas both named Rain of the Lotus Sutra;
then one Buddha named Creating Radiance; then one Buddha named Increasing Mountain King;
then one Buddha named Emergence of the Stainless Dharma King; then one Buddha named Fragrant Honored King; then one Buddha named No... [text continues]
Kalmāṣākṣa, furthermore, there was a buddha named Mahāratnagarbha; another buddha named Balāsaṅgavikrāmin;
another buddha named Svayaṃjñātaguṇabala; another buddha named Cīvarasaṃtuṣṭa;
another buddha named Vaśitāprāpta; and another buddha named Anāvaraṇa.

Obstructing benefit; furthermore, there was a Buddha named Wisdom Treasury, another Buddha named Great Mountain King, another Buddha named Power Treasury, another Buddha named Seeking Merit, another Buddha named Flower Banner Branch, and another Buddha named Multitude of Radiance. Furthermore...
One Buddha was named King of Non-delusion Merit; another Buddha was named Vajra-Upper;
another Buddha was named Dharma-Mark; another Buddha was named Honored Sound King;
another Buddha was named Firmly Holding Vajra; another Buddha was named Jewel Sovereign King; and yet another...

The Buddha’s name was Dṛḍhasvayaṃdhvaja; furthermore, there was a Buddha named Parvatakalpa, another named Varṣarati, another named Kuśaladharmavardhana, another named Sālarāja, and two Buddhas who shared the same name, Guṇapūrṇamahāsāgaraguṇarāja. Furthermore...
There was a Buddha named Wisdom-Union; another Buddha named Blazing Wisdom;
another Buddha named Flower-Multitude; another Buddha named Honored One of the World;
another Buddha named Udumbara-Flower Banner; another Buddha named Sovereign King of the Dharma-Banner; and yet another Buddha.
One was named Candanarāja; another Buddha was named Supratiṣṭhita; another Buddha was named Vīryabala;
another Buddha was named Dhvajaprabhasama; another Buddha was named Jñānagati;
another Buddha was named Sāgaradhvaja; another Buddha was named Dharmakīrtinirghoṣa; and yet another...
There was a Buddha named Destroyer of Māra; another Buddha named Multitude of Radiance;
another Buddha named Emanating Wisdom Radiance; another Buddha named Lamp of Wisdom;
another Buddha named King of Tranquility; another Buddha named Sound of Wisdom; and another Buddha named Banner.
Furthermore, there was a buddha named Heavenly Vajra; another buddha named King of Various Adornments;
another buddha named Invincible Wisdom; another buddha named Well-Abiding Mind;
another buddha named Moon King; and another buddha named Sovereign King of Unconquerable Steps.
Furthermore, there was one buddha named King Sālendra; furthermore, there were eighty buddhas all named Lion-Gait King;
furthermore, there were fifty buddhas all named Nārāyaṇa Invincible Treasury;
furthermore, there were seventy buddhas all named Accumulated Jewel Merit; furthermore, there were thirty buddhas all named Radiance.
Furthermore, in that world-system, there were twenty Buddhas all named King of the Distinction of Constellations;
another two Buddhas both named King of the Sāla Tree of Meritorious Power; ninety Buddhas all named Subtle and Wondrous Sound;
one Buddha named Brahmā-increase; and one Buddha named King of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
Furthermore, there were one thousand Buddhas all sharing the name Padmagandhavicitravikrāntagāmin;
furthermore, there were sixty Buddhas all sharing the name Prabhāsa-jvalana-rāja; furthermore, there were thirty Buddhas all sharing the name Padmagandhabalavardhana;
furthermore, there were two Buddhas both named Aparimitaguṇasāgarajñānavardhana; furthermore, there was one Buddha named...
In Jambū-chāyā, there were again one hundred and two Buddhas all sharing the name Guṇa-parvata-dhvaja;
another Buddha named Siṃha-lakṣaṇa; another one hundred and one Buddhas all sharing the name Nāga-ghoṣa-vara-kusuma-prabha-rāja;
and another Buddha named Sukhagati-gotra-nairātmyāmṛta-guṇa-rāja-kalpa. Furthermore—
There are one thousand Buddhas, all sharing the same name, who reside in the world-realm called Dragon King Liberation-Enlightenment Eye Mountain King;
they are all endowed with the ten titles: Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, and Bhagavat.

"Venerable One, these Buddhas likewise, on the same day and at the same time, each attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in their respective worlds; each has a lifespan of ten intermediate kalpas, and your parinirvāṇas shall also occur on the same day. Once you have entered parinirvāṇa, all the True Dharma (*saddharma*) shall perish after seven days."
“Good son! At that time, ten thousand people prostrated themselves with their heads at the feet of the Buddha Ratnagarbha.
Then, the World-Honored One spoke these verses for the ten thousand people:”
“O Dragon King, arise! Firm and sovereign,
with supreme and virtuous vows, pure and harmonious—
apply your minds with the swiftness of a fierce wind!”
"By diligently practicing and studying the six pāramitās,
you will surely become a Honored One among devas and humans in a future life. "Good son!"

At that time, having heard these verses, the ten thousand people felt great joy in their hearts; they immediately rose, joined their palms, and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, they sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the ninth prince, Madhusukha, and his generation of the mind of awakening was likewise as described above.”
At that time, the prince came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

When I practice the bodhisattva path, may all the present Buddhas in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions bear witness for me, as I now resolve my mind toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi before the Buddha."

“World-Honored One! May it be that when I practice the bodhisattva path, until I attain Buddhahood, in the interval between now and then, I shall not give rise to a mind of regret. Until I attain Buddhahood, may I always abide in a single-minded state without regression; may my practice accord with my words and my words accord with my practice. May not even a single person come to disturb my mind. Furthermore, may I seek neither the vehicle of the śrāvaka nor that of the pratyekabuddha. May I not give rise to thoughts of lust or evil intent. May my mind not associate with sleep, arrogance, doubt, or remorse. Moreover, may I not give rise to thoughts of greed, lust, killing, stealing, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous speech, covetousness, anger, wrong views, jealousy, pride regarding the Dharma, or deceitful intentions.”

As I cultivate the bodhisattva path until the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may no such states as these arise in the interim. Furthermore, from the time I practice for the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, in every step and with every thought and mental factor, may I constantly keep all Buddhas in mind; may I behold all Buddhas, receive and uphold the sublime Dharma, and make offerings to the Saṅgha. In all places of birth, may I always aspire to leave the household life. At the moment of leaving home, may I immediately achieve the three robes of discarded rags (*pāṃśukūla*). May I always sit alone beneath trees in contemplation, dwell in forest hermitages (*āraṇya*), and always practice alms-gathering without seeking gain or honor. May I practice contentment, constantly preach the Dharma, achieve immeasurable and unobstructed eloquence, and never commit grave offenses.

One should not preach the Dharma to women while perceiving them as having the mark of a woman; when preaching the Dharma, one should always do so with the mark of emptiness, constantly keeping in mind the dharma of emptiness and non-existence, sitting upright with hands folded, and not even showing one's teeth.

If there are those who study the Mahāyāna and conceive the notion of a World-Honored One toward them, honoring and making offerings to them; if they likewise conceive the notion of a Buddha toward the place where the Dharma is heard; and if they generate reverence, make offerings, and show respect toward all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas—excepting only the Buddha, the World-Honored One.

Among all beings, one should practice giving without generating discrimination as to whether "this is a field of merit" or "this is not a field of merit," and one should vow: "May I never give rise to a mind of envy toward those who bestow the gift of Dharma."
If there are sentient beings who ought to be executed, may I sacrifice my own life to protect them.
If there are sentient beings who have committed various offenses, may I rescue and deliver them through my strength, my speech, and my wealth, so that they may attain liberation.

If there are householders or those who have left the home life who have committed various transgressions, may they not reveal or manifest them to others; and regarding all gain, offerings, fame, and reputation, may they always remain far removed from them, as if avoiding a pit of fire, swords, or poisonous trees.
“World-Honored One!

If this vow of mine shall be fully accomplished until I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, just as it was vowed here before the Buddha now, may my two hands naturally possess the divine wheel with a thousand spokes, and may the light it emits be like the fierce flames of fire.”
"Good son! At that time, as soon as the prince had spoken these words, there immediately appeared upon each of his two hands a thousand-spoked wheel, obtained exactly as described."
“World-Honored One!
If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, realizing unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
may I now dispatch this celestial wheel with its thousand spokes to those worlds of the five turbidities where no Buddha dwells.”
This wheel should produce such a great sound as to pervade the entire buddha-field,
just as the dragon kings Nanda and Upananda produce a great sound that pervades the world; the sound of this wheel shall be likewise,
namely, the sound of the bodhisattva’s prediction of enlightenment and the wisdom of unflagging mindfulness.
the sound of the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas who have cultivated and studied the dharma of emptiness— if there are sentient beings who,
wherever they may be, hear this sound of the Dharma, they shall immediately sever greed,
anger, delusion, arrogance, stinginess, and envy, and attain tranquility as they contemplate the profound [teachings] of the Buddhas.
With profound wisdom, they resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Son of good family!

At that time, the prince immediately dispatched two wheels; their swiftness was like the supernatural power (*ṛddhi*) of the Buddhas, and the speed at which those wheels departed was likewise so. They traveled everywhere throughout the ten directions to the evil worlds where no Buddhas reside, producing for all sentient beings the sound of the prophecy of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas, the sound of unflagging mindfulness and wisdom, and the sound of the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas regarding the cultivation and study of the Dharma of emptiness. Wherever sentient beings heard this Dharma-sound, they were able to sever greed, anger, delusion, pride, stinginess, and envy, and attained tranquil contemplation of the profound wisdom of the Buddhas. They then resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. In an instant, the wheels returned and came to rest before this prince.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised the prince, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
Excellent, son of good family!

The virtuous vows you have made while practicing the bodhisattva path are unsurpassed and most sublime. By dispatching this celestial wheel to the five turbid worlds where no Buddha dwells, you cause immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of sentient beings to abide in hearts free from defilement and free from affliction and harm, and you exhort them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. For this reason, I now change your name to Akṣobhya; in a future age you shall become a World-Honored One. You should now, before the Buddha, according to your own inclinations, vow to take up various adornments for your buddha-field.
At that time, Akṣobhya addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!

My present vow is for such various adornments of a buddha-field as these: may the ground of my world be made of pure gold; may the ground be as level as the palm of a hand; may it be filled everywhere with many kinds of wonderful celestial jewels; may there be no mountains, hills, mounds, earth, sand, gravel, stones, thorns, or the like; may the ground be soft, like celestial raiment, such that when one walks, the feet sink into it four inches, and upon lifting the feet, it returns to its original state.”

There are no hells, animals, or hungry ghosts, nor any impurity, stench, or filth; there is only the subtle and supreme fragrance of the devas, and the land is filled everywhere with *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.

All sentient beings shall be free from old age and illness; each shall abide in their own place without mutual fear or dread, never causing affliction to others, and their lives shall not be cut short prematurely.
At the time of passing away, their minds shall be free from regret; their resolve shall be firm and unconfused as they focus their mindfulness on contemplating all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.

After their lives have ended, they shall not fall into the evil realms, nor be born in a world of the five turbidities where no Buddha dwells; until they attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall always behold the Buddhas, receive and study the sublime Dharma, and make offerings to the Saṅgha.
All sentient beings have diminished lust, anger, and delusion, and all practice the ten wholesome deeds.

In this world, there are no various crafts or skills; there is neither the commission of crimes nor even the names for such offenses. Furthermore, there are no obstacles caused by celestial Māras. When sentient beings receive their physical forms, they possess no unwholesome appearance, nor do they differentiate between the noble and the base or high and low. All sentient beings deeply understand non-self (*anātman*) and the absence of "mine" (*amama*). Śrāvakas and Bodhisattvas do not lose their purity even in dreams. Sentient beings always delight in seeking and hearing the Dharma, and not a single person gives rise to inverted views; moreover, there are no non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*).

Sentient beings experience no physical or mental exhaustion and all attain the five supernormal powers; they are free from hunger, thirst, and all forms of suffering and affliction. Whatever food or drink they desire, by their mere wish, precious vessels spontaneously appear in their hands, filled with various kinds of sustenance, just like those possessed by the devas of the desire realm.

There is no affliction of mucus, saliva, excrement, urine, phlegm, sweat, or tears, nor is there any sensation of cold or heat; rather, a soft and fragrant wind constantly touches their bodies. This wind’s fragrance is subtle and perfect, such that gods and humans have no need for other perfumes. Following these gods and humans, this fragrant wind satisfies all their requests for either coolness or warmth.

Furthermore, there are those who seek the fragrant wind of the *utpala* lotus, those who seek the fragrant wind of *udumbara*, those who seek the fragrant wind of aloeswood (*agaru*), those who seek the fragrant wind of *tagara*, those who seek the fragrant wind of *agaru*, and those who seek various kinds of fragrant winds; at the moment they resolve their minds, all such aspirations are fulfilled, except in the world of the five corruptions (*pañca-kaṣāya*).

May my land possess towers made of the seven treasures; within these towers may be spread couches of the seven treasures, with rugs and crimson pillows that are fine, smooth, and soft like celestial garments, so that all sentient beings dwelling upon these jeweled towers and couches shall be filled with joy.
On the four sides of that tower are excellent ponds, whose waters possess the eight meritorious qualities, which sentient beings may take and use as they please.

In that land there are many *kadamba* trees, fully endowed with various flowers, fruits, and exquisite fragrances, adorned with the most sublime precious garments, various jeweled canopies, and pearl necklaces. According to the inclinations of all sentient beings, they may freely take and wear wonderful precious robes directly from the trees; the same applies to the flowers, fruits, and fragrances.

“‘Bhagavān! May my Bodhi tree be composed entirely of the seven treasures, reaching a height of one thousand yojanas, with its trunk extending for one yojana in circumference and its branches and foliage spanning a thousand yojanas in length and breadth. May a gentle breeze constantly blow upon this Bodhi tree, causing it to emit the subtle sounds of the six pāramitās, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment. Should any sentient beings hear these wondrous sounds, may they all become free from desire.’”

All women therein have accomplished every kind of sublime merit, resembling the celestial maidens of the Tuṣita Heaven. They are free from all impurities associated with women, such as double-tongued speech, stinginess, jealousy, and a concealing mind.

They do not engage in sexual intercourse with men with a defiled mind. If any man gives rise to lustful thoughts and approaches a woman, gazing at her with a heart of attachment, in a mere moment his desire will vanish; he will spontaneously feel weary of and detached from it, and immediately depart, soon attaining the pure and stainless samādhi.
By the power of samādhi, she attains liberation from all demonic bonds and no longer gives rise to thoughts of evil desire.
Thus, if such a woman sees a man with a mind of lustful desire, she may become pregnant, yet she remains free from the conceptualization of sexual passion.

When she is pregnant, whether carrying a male or female child, her body and mind shall be free from all suffering and affliction; she will constantly experience bliss, like the supreme and wondrous happiness experienced by the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

The joy experienced by a woman during the seven days and seven nights of pregnancy is likewise; it is just like a bhikṣu entering the second dhyāna. Whether male or female, the child in the womb is not defiled by any impurities.

Upon completing the seven days, it is immediately born. At the moment of birth, it experiences various forms of bliss and emits a subtle, wondrous sound. When the woman gives birth, she likewise feels no suffering. Thus, mother and child together enter the water to bathe their bodies.

At that time, the woman gave rise to such a thought; by the power of that thought, she immediately attained the pure samādhi of freedom from desire. By the power of that samādhi, her mind remained constantly settled, and she attained liberation from all demonic bonds.

If there are sentient beings whose past karma has matured such that they ought to take the form of a woman for immeasurable lifetimes, by virtue of their power of meditative concentration, they shall be freed from the female body even unto Nirvana; all karmic seeds of being female will be extinguished without remainder, never to be experienced again.

There may be sentient beings whose past karma has ripened such that they ought to suffer in a womb for immeasurable billions of kalpas; may it be that once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, upon hearing my name they immediately experience joy, and having experienced joy, they shall at once pass away and be born in my world from within a womb. Immediately after being born, the portion of suffering pertaining to the womb shall be forever exhausted without remainder, and until they attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall never again undergo birth from a womb.
There may be sentient beings with abundant roots of goodness who, immediately upon arrival, are born within lotuses in my world.

There may be sentient beings with few roots of goodness who must dwell in a womb, or who are born in my realm by taking on a female body; only thereafter do they attain the permanent exhaustion of the state of being in a womb.

All sentient beings experience exclusively and consistently subtle, wondrous bliss. When a gentle breeze blows through these golden tala trees, they produce subtle and wondrous sounds—namely, sounds of suffering, emptiness, non-self, impermanence, and so forth. Those who hear these sounds all attain the Samādhi of Radiance; by the power of this samādhi, they attain the profound samādhis of the various concentrations on emptiness. In this world, there are no sounds or signs of lustful desire.
“‘World-Honored One!

Once I have sat beneath the Bodhi tree and attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a single thought-moment, I vow that in my world there shall be no distinction between day and night by the light of the sun and moon, except for the opening and closing of flowers.’”

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I shall pervade the trichiliocosm with my radiance. By the power of this radiance, I will cause all sentient beings to obtain the divine eye (*divyacakṣus*). By means of the divine eye, they shall see the immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, and the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently preaching the Dharma in every place therein.

"Bhagavān! Once I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I shall proclaim the True Dharma so that this sound pervades the trichiliocosm, and those sentient beings who hear it shall attain the buddhānusmṛti-samādhi."

Whether sentient beings are walking, standing, or turning about, they shall always be able to see me from whichever direction they face; and should they have any doubts or obstructions regarding any phenomena, by virtue of seeing me, those doubts will immediately be severed.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may all sentient beings—whether they are training as *śrāvakas*, training as *pratyekabuddhas*, or training in the Mahāyāna—in every place throughout the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, who hear my name, be reborn in my world at the end of their lives. If *śrāvaka* practitioners hear my Dharma, may they attain the fruit of an Arhat with the eight liberations; if those training in the Mahāyāna hear my Dharma, may they attain the *dhāraṇī* gates and various *samādhis* of profound *dharmanidhyānakṣānti*, never regressing from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. May I have an immeasurable number of *śrāvakas* as my retinue, so numerous that none can count them, save for the Buddhas.”
“World-Honored One!

When I attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, wherever I go, at every place where I set my foot down, there shall arise a thousand-petaled golden lotus flower. These flowers shall be exquisite and possess great radiance; I shall dispatch them to places where there is no Buddha to proclaim my name.”

If there are sentient beings who, within these flowers, hear the praise of my name, they shall immediately give rise to joy and plant various roots of goodness with the desire to be born in my land; I vow that at the time of their death, they shall all come to be born therein.

I and my great assembly of those who have left the household life are far removed from flattery, crookedness, envy, jealousy, deceit, and fraud—the defilements of a śramaṇa. We revere the Dharma; regarding all necessities such as reputation and gain, our minds do not hold them in high esteem. We constantly delight in suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self; we are always diligent and energetic, honoring the Dharma and relying upon the Saṃgha.

If there are bodhisattvas who have attained non-retrogression, they shall all cause them to attain the *yujū* (cloud-rain) samādhi; by the power of this samādhi, they shall preach the *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of sentient beings, causing them to leave behind birth and death until they achieve Buddhahood, such that the Dharma they preach during that interval shall never be forgotten or lost.

"Bhagavān! After I have attained Buddhahood, my lifespan shall remain in the world for ten thousand great kalpas; after my parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full one thousand kalpas."
At that time, the Tathāgata praised Akṣobhya, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! You have now taken up a pure world.

In a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed and you enter the second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, ten Buddha-worlds to the east of here, there shall be a world named *Sukhāvatī*. All its adornments shall be fully complete, exactly as you have vowed. Therein you shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and you shall still be known by the name Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān—namely, Akṣobhya."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may all sentient beings encompassed by the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases of the entire world attain a heart of loving-kindness, free from thoughts of enmity or malice and all defilements, with body and mind as joyful as those of the bodhisattvas of the ten stages, seated cross-legged upon lotus flowers in the meditative absorption of right reception."
By the power of samādhi, I have rendered my mind free from defilement; likewise, all these sentient beings experience such physical and mental bliss.
Now, with my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to the Buddha, praying only that this ground may be suffused with golden light.

“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya prostrated with his head at the feet of the Buddha. Simultaneously, all immeasurable sentient beings experienced great bliss in both body and mind, and the earth was likewise suffused with golden radiance.”
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses for the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya:
“Rise, O Noble One! By you now, the minds of all the assembly have been made free from anger.”
Furthermore, toward all sentient beings, he gives rise to a heart of great compassion;
in both hands he obtains the divine wheel with a thousand spokes;
with a pure mind, in the future, he shall become the Honored One among gods and humans.

“Good son! At that time, having heard these verses, the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya was filled with great joy. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.”
The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll Four;
The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll Five,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Four, Part Three: The Original Prophecy Bestowed upon All Bodhisattvas.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Silent Intent: “Good son!
At that time, the Brahmā-volunteer Ratnasāgara again addressed the tenth prince, Mṛdumati, and so forth; his generation of the resolve was likewise as described above.
The aspirations of the prince were all identical to those of the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya, and he said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One! ”

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, may all sentient beings be able to contemplate the realm of all Buddhas, and may *candana* and *utpala* incense naturally arise in their hands, with which they shall make offerings to all Buddhas.
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised the prince, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! Your aspiration is most extraordinary.

You aspire that sentient beings shall naturally possess *candana* sandalwood and *utpala* incense in their hands, and that they may all contemplate the realm of the Buddhas and fix their mindfulness upon purity."
"For this reason, I now change your name to 'Fragrant Hand' (Gandhahasta).
The Buddha addressed Gandhahasta: "Good son!"

In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed, during the latter part of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges—following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya and after seven days have elapsed since the extinction of the True Dharma—at that time you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. That buddha-world shall be named *Sukhāvatī*, and the Buddha shall be named Suvarṇapuṣpa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta spoke these words again:
"World-Honored One!
If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, then as I now prostrate to the Buddha, let a rain of *campaka* flowers fall all around this Jambūvana Grove."

"Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta prostrated himself before the Buddha Ratnagarbha with his head touching the ground. Then, within the Jambūvana grove, just as he had spoken, a rain of various campaka flowers fell everywhere in all directions."
At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha spoke these verses to the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta:
“O you of noble and wondrous merit, arise toward the good realms!
May it rain down campaka flowers according to your heart’s wish.”
"Deliver immeasurable, all sentient beings;
show them the various wholesome paths and cause them to reach the state of fearlessness. "Good son!"

At that time, having heard these verses, the Bodhisattva Fragrant Hand was filled with great joy. He immediately rose, joined his palms, and stepped forward to prostrate at the Buddha’s feet. Not far from the Buddha, he sat down again to listen to the Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara again addressed the eleventh prince, Maṅgala, and so forth; his generation of the aspiration for enlightenment was likewise as described above.”
The aspirations of the prince were also like those of the Bodhisattva Gandhahasta.
At that time, when Prince Siṃha made offerings of precious jeweled banners to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Buddha immediately praised Prince Siṃha, saying: "Excellent!"
Excellent! Son of good family!
Because you now offer this precious banner as an act of worship, I shall therefore name you Ratnaketu (Precious Banner).
The Buddha told Ratnalakṣaṇa:

"In a future age, after one asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges has passed, during the latter part of a second asaṃkhyeya kalpa as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Suvarṇapuṣpa in the world-system Sukhāvatī, and after the True Dharma has ceased for three intermediate kalpas, the world-system Sukhāvatī will change its name to Candravijaya. Therein, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and your title shall be Nāgeśvaraghoṣarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
"The adornments of that Buddha-world are equal to those of the world Sukhāvatī, without any difference.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnalakṣaṇa came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, I now prostrate with my head at the feet of the Buddha, so that all sentient beings may obtain such mindfulness as that of a bodhisattva dwelling in the Samādhi of Non-deceit; may all sentient beings obtain great benefit, give rise to great compassion, and awaken the bodhicitta.
