If one understands that all dharmas are fundamentally without the nature of arising and are now without cessation, this is called the prajñā-pāramitā.
For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, I have firmly and diligently cultivated and accumulated the *prajñāpāramitā*. Why is this?

There may have been bodhisattvas in past ages who, for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, practiced the bodhisattva path with firm resolve and diligent effort, cultivating and accumulating the prajñā-pāramitā; and there may be bodhisattvas in future ages who, for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, will practice the bodhisattva path with firm resolve and diligent effort, cultivating and accumulating the prajñā-pāramitā. Therefore, I shall now, in this future age, resolve my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, cultivate the bodhisattva path, and ensure that all wholesome dharmas are never severed.
“World-Honored One!
Since I first resolved upon the path, I have revealed great compassion for the sake of future bodhisattvas, up until their entry into nirvana.
Should there be those who hear the name of my great compassion, they will feel wonder and astonishment, exclaiming that it is unprecedented.”

Therefore, regarding giving, I do not praise myself; I do not rely on ethical discipline, nor dwell upon patience, nor depend on diligence, nor savor the various meditative absorptions. All my wisdom is unattached to the three periods of time; though I practice these six pāramitās in this manner, I do not seek their karmic fruition.

There are sentient beings who are devoid of the seven noble riches, cast out by the worlds of the Buddhas, who have committed the five heinous crimes, subverted the True Dharma, slandered the worthy and holy ones, and practiced false views; their grave and evil offenses are like a great mountain, constantly shrouded and obscured by the paths of error.
Therefore, for the sake of these sentient beings, I now single-mindedly adorn myself and diligently cultivate and accumulate the six pāramitās.

For the sake of planting roots of goodness in each and every sentient being, I shall enter the Avīci Hell for ten kalpas to undergo immeasurable suffering; the same applies to the realms of animals, hungry ghosts, the impoverished, spirits, and those among humans who are lowly and base.

If there are sentient beings who lack all roots of goodness, whose mindfulness is lost and whose minds are scorched, I shall gather them all in and subdue them, causing them to plant roots of goodness. Until the end of the Bhadrakalpa, during that entire interval, I do not wish to experience any pleasures among the devas or humans, except for one lifetime in Tuṣita Heaven while awaiting the time to attain Buddhahood.

“World-Honored One! I should dwell thus for a long time in birth and death for as many kalpas as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world, making offerings of all necessities to the Buddhas for the sake of planting roots of goodness in even a single sentient being. With offering requisites as numerous as the atoms in a single Buddha-world, I shall make offerings to each and every one of the infinite and boundless Buddhas of the ten directions. Furthermore, at each and every place where those infinite and boundless Buddhas of the ten directions reside, I shall attain roots of goodness as numerous as the atoms in a single Buddha-world. Before each and every Buddha, I shall again teach and transform as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world, causing them to abide in the path of unsurpassed Bodhi; this shall likewise apply to Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas, teaching according to the vows of all sentient beings.”

If there are worlds where a Buddha has not yet appeared in the world, may I become a rishi to teach all sentient beings, causing them to abide in the ten wholesome actions and the five supernormal powers, and to remain far removed from all false views.
If there are sentient beings who serve the deity Maheśvara, I vow to manifest a transformation body like that of Maheśvara to teach and transform them, causing them to abide in wholesome dharmas.
To those who serve the Eight-Armed One, I also vow to transform into the body of an Eight-Armed Deva to teach and transform them, causing them to abide in wholesome dharmas.
To those who serve the Sun, Moon, and Brahmā, I also vow to transform into the bodies of the Sun, Moon, and Brahmā to teach and transform them, causing them to abide in wholesome dharmas.

Whether there are those who serve the garuḍa, or even those who serve the rabbit, I vow to transform myself into the body of a rabbit to follow and teach them, causing them to abide in wholesome dharmas.
If I see sentient beings suffering from hunger, I shall give my own flesh and blood to them so that they may be fully satisfied.
"If there are sentient beings who have committed various offenses, I shall take their place with my own body and life to undergo their punishment and act as their protection.
"World-Honored One!
In future ages, there will be sentient beings who are devoid of all roots of goodness and who burn away their virtuous minds."
At that time, for the sake of these sentient beings, I shall diligently practice with vigor on the bodhisattva path,
undergoing all manner of sufferings within birth and death, until, after passing through incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) equal to one Ganges River of sands,
I enter the latter part of a second Ganges River of sands of incalculable eons, at the very beginning of the Bhadrakalpa, during the [period of] fire...
When Māṇava Māla attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and was named Tathāgata Krakucchanda,
those whom I had previously taught— who were devoid of all wholesome karma, who practiced unwholesome karma, who scorched their wholesome minds,
who were destitute of the seven noble riches, who committed the five heinous crimes, who subverted the true Dharma, and who slandered the noble ones— [were all led to liberation].
...those who practice wrong views and commit grave, evil offenses— whose sins are like great mountains and who are constantly shrouded by false paths,

and those abandoned in worlds where no Buddha dwells— causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to practice the *dāna-pāramitā*, up to and including the practice of the *prajñā-pāramitā*.
Established securely in the stage of non-retrogression, they shall all attain Buddhahood;
throughout Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms within a single Buddha-field, they shall turn the wheel of the true Dharma,
causing all sentient beings to plant roots of goodness for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to emerge from evil.
"Regarding the Path, which brings peace and stability, and those dharmas that assist toward enlightenment through merit and wisdom—
may I, at that time, behold them all in their entirety.
'World-Honored One!'"

If there are Buddhas in various places who dispatch sentient beings to the presence of those Buddhas to receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and cause them to attain *dhāraṇī*, *samādhi*, and patience, such that they immediately ascend through the stages of the bodhisattva path, obtain various adorned worlds, each attaining whatever they seek according to their wishes, and take hold of pure Buddha-lands—such sentient beings are all those whom I have exhorted and transformed.

When Krakucchanda Buddha appears in the world during this Bhadrakalpa, may these and other such assemblies likewise attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions as numerous as motes of dust; and wherever they dwell in the world preaching the Dharma, may I behold them all.
“‘World-Honored One!

When Krakucchanda Buddha attained enlightenment, I went to his presence and made offerings to him with various requisites. I inquired of him in various ways regarding the Dharma of renunciation, maintained pure precepts, extensively studied and gained great learning, single-mindedly cultivated samādhi, and practiced with diligent vigor, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma; indeed, apart from the Tathāgata, there was no one who could surpass me.’”

At that time, there may be sentient beings of dull faculties who lack all roots of goodness, who fall into false views, practice the unrighteous path, commit the five heinous crimes, destroy the True Dharma, and slander the sages and saints; their grave and evil offenses are like a great mountain. At that time, I shall for the sake of such sentient beings preach the True Dharma to gather them in and subdue them;
after the Buddha-sun has set, I shall spontaneously perform immeasurable Buddha-works thereafter.
It was likewise when Krakucchanda Buddha, Kāśyapa Buddha, and others dwelt in the world preaching the Dharma, even performing the work of a Buddha spontaneously.

This continued until the human lifespan reached one thousand years; at that time, I exhorted all sentient beings toward the three bases of merit, so that after those thousand years had passed, they would be reborn in the heavens, where I would preach the True Dharma to the devas and humans, causing them to attain discipline and subduing.
Even until the human lifespan reaches one hundred and twenty years, at that time sentient beings will be dominated by ignorance;
relying on their own physical beauty, noble lineage, and prestigious clans, they will fall into the dark and evil world of the five turbidities,
characterized by heavy and thick greed, anger, delusion, and arrogance, as well as negligence, stinginess, and jealousy.
They are stingy, envious, engage in unrighteous sexual conduct, seek wealth through unlawful means, practice perverted and erroneous views,
are devoid of the seven noble riches, are unfilial toward their parents, do not show reverence toward śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas,
fail to do what ought to be done, do what ought not to be done, and do not perform meritorious deeds.
Fearing future lives, they do not diligently cultivate the three bases of merit; they take no delight in the Three Vehicles and are unable to practice the three roots of goodness.
They devote themselves exclusively to the three evils, do not cultivate the ten wholesome actions, and instead zealously commit the ten unwholesome deeds.
Their minds are constantly shrouded by the four inversions, and they remain settled securely within the four transgressions of the precepts.
They cause the four Mara-kings to always attain sovereignty, drowning them in the four currents and having their minds covered by the five hindrances.

In future ages, such sentient beings will have their six sense faculties unrestrained, practicing the eightfold wrong path, entering the mountain of great transgressions, and giving rise to all manner of fetters;
they will not seek the fruits of reward in the heavens or among humans, being perverted and deluded.
They follow various views, treading upon false paths; they commit the five heinous crimes, destroy the true Dharma, and slander the sages.

They are severed from all roots of goodness, impoverished and lowly, devoid of fear or restraint, ignorant of gratitude and righteousness, having lost right mindfulness, and they despise the wholesome Dharma, lacking wisdom and being unable—
In their studies, they violate the precepts and act with flattery; with a mind of jealousy, they do not share the gains they have obtained with others;
they treat one another with contempt and lack respect; they are lazy and indolent, their faculties are impaired, and their bodies are weak and deficient in clothing;
they associate with evil friends, lose mindfulness while in the womb, and thus receive their seeds [of existence].

Because they sow the seeds of suffering and affliction, their complexions are foul and withered; looking at one another with eyes devoid of shame or remorse, they dwell in mutual fear for even the duration of a single meal.
The evils committed through their physical, verbal, and mental actions are immeasurable and boundless, yet because they are capable of such evil, they are praised.
At that time, sentient beings collectively and exclusively cultivate and accumulate the two views of annihilationism and eternalism;
they are firmly attached to the fragile and precarious body of the five aggregates; they give rise to deep craving and attachment toward the five desires;

they constantly harbor thoughts of anger, resentment, and enmity, wishing to harm other beings; their minds are perpetually vexed, defiled, turbid, coarse, and vulgar, and have not yet attained subduing.
They are stingy and greedily attached, failing to relinquish what is unrighteous and lacking any sense of resolve;

they harbor mutual fear and give rise to contention, using defiled minds to kill and harm one another. They distance themselves from wholesome dharmas and, with unwholesome intent, commit various evil deeds.
Having no faith in the retribution of good and evil, they give rise to [unwholesome thoughts] toward all wholesome dharmas.
With a mind that has turned away from the heart, they give rise to a mind of delight toward the destruction of wholesome dharmas,

a mind of intent application toward unwholesome dharmas, and a mind of non-rescue toward the quiescence of *nirvāṇa*. They harbor a lack of reverence toward śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas who uphold the precepts,
give rise to a mind of longing for the various fetters and bonds, and [regard] old age, sickness, and death...
They give rise to deep faith; they give rise to a mind of upholding toward all afflictions; they give rise to a mind of grasping toward the five hindrances;
they give rise to a mind of distancing themselves from the banner of the True Dharma; they give rise to a mind of erecting the banners of various views;
they constantly give rise to minds of mutual opposition and contempt; they together give rise to minds of strife and mutual devouring; each...
Each being mutually opposed and encroaching upon one another, they harbor hearts of resentment, malice, and agitation; they give rise to insatiable desire for sensual pleasures;
they give rise to envy toward the wealth and property of others; they give rise to a lack of gratitude for kindness received;
they give rise to a thieving mind toward sentient beings; and they give rise to the intent to violate and harass the wives of others.
Mind. At that time, all sentient beings have no virtuous aspirations within their minds;
therefore, they constantly hear the sounds of hell, the sounds of animals, the sounds of hungry ghosts, the sounds of illness, the sounds of old age and death, and the sounds of affliction and harm.
The sound of [the eight difficulties], the sound of imprisonment and confinement, the sound of shackles, manacles, collars, locks, and fetters;
the sound of plundering others' property and causing affliction; the sound of anger, contempt, and reproach; the sound of destroying the harmony of the assembly;
the sound of foreign armies and weapons of war; and the sound of famine and the theft of grain during times of high prices.
The sounds of sexual misconduct, lying, and madness; the sounds of double-tongued speech, harsh words, and frivolous chatter;
the sounds of stinginess, greed, envy, and grasping; the sounds of attachment to self and what belongs to self, and of strife; the sounds of hatred and love, and of the pleasant and unpleasant;

the sounds of sorrow and lamentation arising from separation from loved ones; the sounds of suffering and affliction arising from the gathering of enemies and those one hates; and the sounds of each [being] toward one another...

At that time, sentient beings will each constantly hear such sounds as: the sound of servants and slaves; the sound of the foul, impure stench of the womb; the sound of cold, heat, hunger, thirst, and extreme exhaustion;
the sound of the urgent toil of plowing and planting; the sound of weariness with various crafts and skills;
and the sound of the emaciation and suffering caused by illness and affliction.

Such sentient beings—having severed all roots of goodness, being separated from virtuous friends, and constantly harboring anger—fill this Sahā world entirely; they have been cast out from the worlds of the Buddhas in other directions because of their heavy karma.

During this Bhadrakalpa, when the lifespan is one hundred and twenty years, sentient beings—due to the causal conditions of their karma—will experience such lowliness and degradation in this Sahā world, being far removed from those who have perfected all roots of goodness.
In this Sahā world, the ground is largely salty and bitter, consisting of salt flats, soil, sand, gravel, mountains, hills, valleys, and ravines;
it is filled with mosquitoes, gadflies, venomous snakes, and various evil birds and beasts.
Harsh and unpleasant winds arise out of season, constantly occurring at improper times.
There will be evil hail and rain; the taste of that rain will be poisonous, sour, salty, and bitter.
Because of this rain, all medicinal herbs, trees, stalks, nodes, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, and the various flavors of the hundred grains will become permeated with poison.
In this way, sentient beings will encounter untimely, coarse, harsh, foul, turbid, and poisonous things.
Having eaten, their anger increased; their complexions became withered and lacked luster.
They felt no compassion for sentient beings, slandered the noble ones, and each lacked a heart of reverence.
Constantly harboring fear, they harmed one another, giving rise to a mind of affliction and turmoil; they devoured flesh and drank blood, and flayed [living beings].
Clad in skins, wielding swords and staves, they diligently commit acts of killing; relying on their noble lineage, possessing handsome features,
reciting non-Buddhist scriptures, training in riding horses, being skilled with the sword and spear, and proficient in archery and charioteering,
they give rise to feelings of jealousy toward their own kinsmen if those sentient beings practice what is heterodox.
The Dharma involves undergoing various kinds of suffering. “World-Honored One!

May I, at that time, descend from Tuṣita Heaven to be born into the womb of the principal first consort of either the most excellent Wheel-Turning King’s family or a Sovereign King’s family, for the sake of taming the minds of all sentient beings and cultivating roots of goodness.”

Upon entering the womb, he emitted a great radiance; that light was subtle and wondrous, illuminating the entire Sahā world from the Diamond Foundation below up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven above. He caused all sentient beings therein—whether in the hells, among animals, among hungry ghosts, in the heavens, or among humans; whether with form or without form, with perception, without perception, with neither perception nor non-perception—to all wish to see his subtle and wondrous light, and if the light touched their bodies, they likewise wished to perceive it.

Because they perceive and know this light, they are able to fully discern the faults and afflictions of birth and death, and diligently seek the unsurpassed, quiescent nirvana; even to the point of severing all afflictions in a single thought-moment—this is called causing all sentient beings to first plant the root of nirvana.

May I, while dwelling in the womb for ten months, attain the discernment of all dharmas and enter into all dharma-gates—namely, the gate of the samādhi of unborn emptiness—and may I, throughout immeasurable kalpas in future ages, preach this samādhi with a well-determined mind that can never be exhausted.

Once I have emerged from the womb and attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I shall pull those sentient beings out and cause them to leave birth and death; I shall cause all such multitudes as these to behold me.
Although he remained in his mother’s womb for a full ten months, he was in fact dwelling in the *Ratna-samādhi* (Jeweled Samādhi), sitting cross-legged in meditative absorption and contemplation.

When the ten months were complete, he emerged from her right side. By the power of the *Sarvaguṇasampad-samādhi* (Samādhi of the Accomplishment of All Virtues), he caused the Sahā world to tremble in six ways, from the adamantine foundation up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven; all sentient beings therein—whether dwelling in the hells, as animals, hungry ghosts, or among gods and humans—attained awakening.
At that time, there was again a subtle and wondrous radiance that shone throughout the Sahā world, awakening immeasurable sentient beings.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet planted roots of goodness, I shall establish them so that they may plant such roots; once they have planted roots of goodness within nirvana, I shall cause all these beings to produce the sprouts of samādhi.

When I emerge from my right side and my foot treads upon the earth, I further vow that the Sahā world, from the adamantine base up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, shall tremble in six ways; and may all sentient beings—whether dwelling in water, on land, or in space; born from wombs, eggs, moisture, or by transformation; and those in any of the five destinies—attain full awakening.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained samādhi, may they all attain it; having attained samādhi, may they be established securely in the stage of non-retrogression within the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.

Once I have been born, I shall cause all the devas of the Sahā world—the Brahma kings, the Māra devas, the Trāyastriṃśa devas, the Sūrya and Candra devas, the Caturmahārājika devas, the great Nāga kings, Gandharvas, Asuras, Garuḍas, Kiṃnaras, Mahoragas, transformation-born immortals, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas—to come together in their entirety to make offerings to me.

Once I was born, I immediately took seven steps; having taken those seven steps, by the power of the Samādhi of Selecting Merit, I preached the True Dharma, causing the hearts of the great assembly to rejoice and leading them to abide in the Three Vehicles.

Within this assembly, if there are sentient beings who study the vehicle of the śrāvakas, may they attain mastery in this very life; if there are those who practice and study the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, may they all attain the "Flower of the Sun" patience (sūryapuṣpa-kṣānti); and those who study the Mahāyāna, may they all attain the "Vajra-Grasping Protection of the Great Ocean" samādhi, and by the power of that samādhi, may they transcend the three stages.

At that time, I longed for a bath and prayed that a most excellent great Dragon King would come to bathe my body; any sentient beings who saw this would immediately abide in the Three Vehicles, and the merit they would obtain would be as described above.
When I was a youth riding a goat-cart, I manifested various arts and skills for the sake of awakening all sentient beings.

While dwelling amidst the palaces, wives, concubines, and the five desires, enjoying their company, I perceived their faults and perils; thus, at midnight, I departed the city, casting off all my necklaces and ornaments, desiring to refute the teachers of the heterodox paths such as the Nirgranthas.

Out of reverence for the robes, I donned the *kāṣāya* and proceeded to the foot of the Bodhi tree; when sentient beings saw me situated beneath the Bodhi tree, they all made vows, desiring that I would swiftly, by the power of the Samādhi of Accomplishment through All Merits, preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
Having heard this Dharma, they shall give rise to profound and earnest aspiration within the Three Vehicles and practice with diligent vigor.
If there are those who have already set out in the Śrāvaka Vehicle, I shall cause them to be liberated from afflictions and attain taming under my guidance within one more lifetime.
If there are those who have already set out in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, I shall cause them all to attain the "Flower of the Sun" patience (*sūryaprabhā-kṣānti*).

If there are those who have already set out upon the Mahāyāna, they shall all attain the Samādhi of Holding the Vajra to Protect the Great Ocean; by the power of this samādhi, they shall transcend the three stages.

I personally received grass beneath the Bodhi tree, spread it upon the site of the Vajrāsana, and sat down cross-legged with body and mind upright. Binding my mindfulness within the Āspharaṇaka-samādhi, by the power of that samādhi, I caused the inhalation and exhalation to cease and become tranquil. While in this meditative concentration for one day and one night, I consumed half a grain of sesame and half a grain of rice daily, and gave the remaining half to others.

Having thus cultivated and accumulated ascetic practices for such a long time, all those from the Sahā world up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven who hear my name shall come to my presence and make offerings to me.
"May all these assemblies serve as witnesses for me in my practice of such asceticism.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who have planted roots of goodness in the Śrāvaka Vehicle,"
I vow that these beings shall attain tranquility of mind regarding all afflictions; if they must come to my presence for their final birth, I shall subdue them.
It is likewise for those of the Pratyekabuddha vehicle and the Mahāyāna.
If there are nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, or ṛṣis possessing the five supernatural powers who come to my presence and make offerings to me.
These sentient beings shall all bear witness to my such ascetic practices;
and it is likewise for those who have already studied the vehicles of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna.

If there are sentient beings throughout the four continents who practice the paths of externalists, subsisting on coarse food and performing ascetic penances, and non-human beings go to their abodes and speak these words to them: "O you all!..."
If one cannot fully practice all these austerities, nor yet attain the great fruit and retribution, that is not considered rare.

For instance, within my own domain there is a *bodhisattva* in his final birth who practices austerities and further enters such subtle and wondrous meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), wherein the actions of body, speech, and mind are entirely stilled, and the inhalation and exhalation of breath are extinguished. For one day and one night, he consumes only half a grain of sesame and half a grain of rice. Through such austerities, he attains a great fruit and retribution, achieves great benefit, and brings many to transformation and enlightenment; this practitioner of austerities will before long realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“If you do not believe my words, you may go to that place yourself to observe what he does.
[The King replied: “World-Honored One!
I pray that these people will abandon their own practices and all come to me to witness my asceticism;”
There may be sentient beings who have already studied the Śrāvaka vehicle up to the Mahāyāna, and it is likewise for them.
Whether there be kings, ministers, or common people—whether lay or ordained—who see me practicing these ascetic practices and come to my presence to make offerings to me;
or those who have already studied the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, or Mahāyāna vehicles—it is likewise for them.
If there are women who, seeing my ascetic practices, come to where I am to make offerings to me, the very physical bodies these women receive shall be their final bodies;
the same applies to those who have already trained in the vehicles of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or the Mahāyāna.

If there are birds or beasts who see my ascetic practices, they shall also come to my presence; when these birds and beasts pass away from this life, they will never again receive a body as an animal.
If there are those who have already set their minds on the Śrāvaka Vehicle, they shall remain for only one more birth before they must come to my presence and attain taming.
If there are those who have already set their minds on the Pratyekabuddha path, it shall be the same for them.
Even down to the most minute insects and hungry ghosts, it is likewise so.

When I sat in a single cross-legged posture after such long-term ascetic practice, hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable sentient beings served as my witnesses; these beings have already planted the seeds of liberation over immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding my practice of such asceticism, no sentient beings of the past have ever been able to perform such deeds; nor have any other outsiders, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or followers of the Mahāyāna ever been able to perform such ascetic practices.”
“World-Honored One!

Such ascetic practices as these cannot be performed by sentient beings of the future, nor can they be performed by others—whether they be followers of external paths, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or those of the Mahāyāna.”
Even before I had attained Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, I was already able to accomplish a great deed, namely, the destruction of Māra and his retinue.

I vow that after destroying the mara of afflictions and attaining *anuttara-samyak-sambodhi*, for as long as it takes to establish even a single sentient being in the supreme and wondrous fruit of arhatship, I shall manifest and undergo the retribution of residual karma;
likewise for a second sentient being established in arhatship, and so too for a third and a fourth.

For the sake of each and every sentient being, I manifest hundreds of thousands of immeasurable supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) to cause them to dwell securely within right view. For the sake of each and every sentient being, I explain the meanings of hundreds of thousands of immeasurable Dharma-gates, enabling them to abide in the fruits of the noble ones according to their capacity. With vajra-like wisdom, I shatter the mountains of afflictions of all sentient beings and preach the teachings of the Three Vehicles for them. For the sake of each and every sentient being, even if they are hundreds of thousands of *yojanas* away, I travel to their location without relying on supernatural power and preach the Dharma for them, causing them to abide securely in fearlessness.

May there be no obstacles for those who wish to go forth in my Dharma—namely, physical weakness, loss of mindfulness, insanity, arrogance, fearlessness, delusion, lack of wisdom, and the proliferation of various fetters that cause the mind to be distracted.
If there are women who wish to leave the household life to study the Path and receive the full precepts within my Dharma, they shall fulfill their great vows.
My fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās shall all provide them with offerings.
May all devas, humans, and spirits realize the Four Noble Truths; may all nāgas, asuras, and other animals observe the eight precepts and cultivate pure brahmacarya.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, if there are sentient beings who give rise to anger toward me, or who seek to harm me with swords, staves, fire-pits, or various other means; or who revile and abuse me with evil words, spreading slander and contempt throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
or who offer me poisoned food to eat—I shall fully endure all such karmic injuries and yet attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.”

In the past, there were sentient beings who were my enemies and adversaries; they gave rise to harmful intentions, uttered various evil words, offered food mixed with poison, and caused blood to flow from my body—all such persons came to me with malicious intent.

I shall, through my precepts, extensive learning, and samādhi, with a mind perfumed by great compassion, preach the Dharma with a sublime Brahma-voice. Having heard it, may their minds become pure and they abide in wholesome dharmas; may they immediately repent of the evil karma they have committed and never do so again. May they all be reborn among gods and humans without hindrance; having been born among gods and humans, may they attain wondrous liberation, dwell securely in the supreme fruit, leave behind all desires and evils, forever sever the torrents [of defilement], and exhaust all obstructing karma. As for those sentient beings who possess residual karma, may it all be completely exhausted without remainder.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, from every one of the pores of my body, emanated Buddhas shall emerge day after day, their bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks and successively embellished by the eighty secondary characteristics.”

I shall dispatch them to Buddhaless worlds, to worlds where Buddhas do exist, and to the realms of the five corruptions. Whether those worlds contain those who commit the five heinous crimes, destroy the true Dharma, slander the noble ones, or even sever all roots of goodness; or whether there be Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or Mahāyāna followers in training who have violated their precepts, fallen into great offenses, scorched their virtuous minds, lost the path of goodness, and fallen into the desolate wilderness of saṃsāra, practicing various heterodox paths and ascending the mountains of transgression.

In this way, hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of sentient beings are each taught the Dharma by a transformed Buddha throughout a single day; some may serve Maheśvara, and [the Buddha] assumes his form to teach them the Dharma accordingly.
At that time, they shall also invoke my name and praise me.
May these sentient beings, upon hearing this praise of me, give rise to joy in their hearts, plant various roots of goodness, and be born in my world.
“World-Honored One!

If, when these sentient beings approach the time of their death, I do not stand before them to expound the Dharma so as to purify their minds, may I never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the future.”

If those beings, after the end of their lives, were to fall into the three evil realms and not be reborn in my land to receive human bodies, then all the immeasurable true dharmas known to me would utterly perish, and all Buddha-works would fail to be accomplished;
the same applies to those who serve Nārāyaṇa.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I vow that all those in other worlds who commit the five heinous crimes, even those who follow various heterodox paths and climb the mountain of transgressions—such sentient beings, when their lives are about to end, shall all come together and be born in my world. According to the physical forms they received in their original states—pale and lusterless, with hideous countenances like those of piśācas, forgetful and broken in precepts, foul-smelling and short-lived, their bodies diminished by these various evils, and their basic necessities for life never sufficiently provided—I vow this shall be so.”

For the sake of these sentient beings, throughout all four continents of the Sahā world, he simultaneously descended from Tuṣita to manifest in a mother’s womb, and proceeded through his stages as a youth, learning various arts and skills; he left the home life, practiced austerities, destroyed the various Māras, attained the Unsurpassed Way, turned the wheel of the True Dharma, and after his parinirvāṇa, caused his relics to be widely distributed.
In this manner, he manifested various Buddha-activities, which completely filled all such ten billion sets of four continents.
*The Sutra of the Compassionate Lotus*, Fascicle Six.
*The Sutra of the Compassionate Lotus*, Fascicle Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Four, Part Five: "The Original Prophecies of All Bodhisattvas.
[The Bodhisattva] said: "World-Honored One!..."

Once I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I shall preach the Dharma with a single voice; yet there may be sentient beings who study the Śrāvaka-yāna, and upon hearing the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, they immediately come to know the treasury of the Śrāvaka teachings;
or there may be those practicing and studying the Pratyekabuddha-yāna, and upon hearing the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain understanding of the Pratyekabuddha teachings;

or there may be those practicing and studying the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, and upon hearing the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain full comprehension of the Mahāyāna teachings as pure and unmixed.

If there are those who cultivate the factors conducive to enlightenment and desire to attain it, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately relinquish their wealth and practice generosity;

if there are sentient beings who are devoid of all meritorious virtues and long for the happiness of the heavens or the human realm, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately maintain the precepts;

if there are sentient beings who fear one another and harbor hearts of attachment and hatred, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately develop hearts of intimacy and affection toward each other.
If there are sentient beings who delight in committing acts of killing, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain a heart of compassion;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are constantly shrouded by stinginess and jealousy, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately cultivate a heart of sympathetic joy;

if there are sentient beings who are handsome and free from illness, yet become attached to physical form and their minds give rise to negligence, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain a heart of equanimity.
If there are sentient beings whose lust is rampant and whose minds are dissolute, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately contemplate impurity;

if there are sentient beings who study the Mahāyāna but are shrouded by the hindrance of restlessness, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the dharma of mindfulness of the body;

if there are sentient beings who constantly praise themselves, claiming they are capable of great debate, their wisdom as brilliant as a flash of lightning, yet upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately understand the profound twelve links of dependent origination.

If there are sentient beings who have heard little and seen little, yet claim to be able to discourse on the Dharma, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain various *dhāraṇīs* that cannot be taken away nor lost;

if there are sentient beings who have entered the mountain of false views, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately understand the profound gate of emptiness of all phenomena;

if there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by discursive thoughts, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain a deep understanding of the signless (*animitta*) dharma-gate.

If there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by various impure vows, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain profound understanding of the dharma-gate of non-action;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are not pure, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, their minds become pure;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are obscured by many conditions, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they attain understanding of the method for not losing the bodhicitta.
If there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by anger, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they understand the mark of reality and receive a prediction of enlightenment;

if there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by attachment to dependence, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they deeply understand that all phenomena are without anything to depend upon;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by passionate defilement, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they swiftly understand that all phenomena are stainless and pure.
If there are sentient beings who have lost their wholesome minds, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they will profoundly understand the *sūryaprabha-samādhi*;
if there are sentient beings who engage in various demonic activities, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they will swiftly attain understanding of the pure Dharma;

if there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by heterodox doctrines, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they will immediately attain profound understanding and increase in the True Dharma.
If there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by afflictions, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain understanding and become free from the dharma of afflictions;
if there are sentient beings who travel the various evil paths, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately turn back;

if there are sentient beings who, regarding the Mahāyāna Dharma, praise and proclaim false teachings as auspicious and sublime, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately give rise to a mind of renunciation toward those false teachings and attain correct understanding.
If there are bodhisattvas who weary of birth and death, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately conceive a heart of love and joy toward birth and death;
if there are sentient beings who do not know the ground of goodness, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain awakening to the dharmas of the ground of goodness;

if there are sentient beings who, seeing others perform good deeds, do not give rise to appreciation but instead harbor envy and jealousy, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain joy in their hearts.
If there are sentient beings whose minds are each mutually antagonistic, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain unobstructed radiance;
if there are sentient beings who practice various evil deeds, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they deeply understand the retributive fruits obtained from those evil deeds;
if there are sentient beings who fear large assemblies, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they deeply attain and comprehend the Lion’s Gaze Samādhi.
If there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by the four māras, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they will swiftly attain the Śūraṅgama Samādhi;

if there are sentient beings who do not see the radiance of the various buddha-lands, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they will immediately attain the profound understanding of the Samādhi of Various Adorned Radiances;
if there are sentient beings who possess hearts of hatred and attachment, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they will immediately attain the mind of equanimity.
If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the radiance of the Buddha-dharma, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Dharma Banner;
if there are sentient beings who are devoid of great wisdom, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Dharma Torch;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Sun Lamp.
If there are sentient beings who lack eloquence in speech, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain various merits and appropriate eloquence;

if there are sentient beings who contemplate that form is a composite and lacks solidity, being like a bubble on water, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Nārāyaṇa Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings whose minds are distracted and unsettled, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the firm and resolute Samādhi.
If there are sentient beings who wish to behold the crown of the Buddha’s head and hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Sumeru-banner Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings who have abandoned their original vows and hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Firm Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings who have regressed from or lost their various supernormal powers and hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Vajra Samādhi.

If there are sentient beings who harbor doubts regarding the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain realization at the Vajra Site of Enlightenment;
if there are sentient beings who lack a sense of weary detachment toward all phenomena, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Vajra Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings who do not know the minds of others, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately come to know the minds of others.
If there are sentient beings who do not know the sharpness or dullness of their own faculties, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately come to know them;

if there are sentient beings of various different kinds who cannot understand one another's speech, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Understanding Sounds;
if there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the Dharma-body, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the understanding that distinguishes all bodies.
If there are sentient beings who do not see the Buddha’s body but hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Unblinking Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings who discriminate among various conditions but hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Non-contention Samādhi;

if there are sentient beings who harbor doubts and suspicions regarding the turning of the wheel of Dharma but hear the Buddha preach the Dharma, they attain mental purity regarding the turning of the wheel of Dharma.

If there are sentient beings who give rise to the wrong practice of causelessness, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the illumination of the Dharma that accords with dependent origination;

if there are sentient beings who give rise to the view of permanence within a single Buddha-world, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the skillful discernment of immeasurable Buddha-lands;

if there are sentient beings who have not yet planted the roots of goodness for the various marks, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of manifold adornments.

If there are sentient beings who cannot skillfully distinguish all forms of speech, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Discerning Various Sounds and Voices;

if there are sentient beings who single-mindedly seek all-encompassing wisdom, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Non-discriminative Dharmadhātu;
if there are sentient beings who regress from the Dharma, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Firmness.
If there are sentient beings who do not know the dharma-realm, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain great wisdom;
if there are sentient beings who have departed from their original vows, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of non-forgetfulness;
if there are sentient beings who differentiate among various paths, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the single path free from all differentiation.
If there are sentient beings who seek wisdom and desire it to be like empty space, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Non-existence;
if there are sentient beings who have not yet fully perfected the various pāramitās, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately abide in the Pure Pāramitā;

if there are sentient beings who have not yet fully perfected the four methods of attraction (saṃgrahavastu), upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Sublime and Wholesome Attraction.

If there are sentient beings who discriminate regarding the four immeasurable minds, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the diligence of an even-minded exertion;

if there are sentient beings who have not yet fully attained the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of non-appearance;
if there are sentient beings whose minds have lost mindfulness and wholesome wisdom, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of the ocean-seal of wisdom.

If there are sentient beings whose minds are filled with doubt and who have not yet given rise to the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Certainty in All Dharmas (*sarvadharma-niścaya-samādhi*) by virtue of the single characteristic of all phenomena;

if there are sentient beings who have forgotten the Dharma they have heard, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Non-forgetfulness of Mindfulness (*asmṛti-lakṣaṇa-samādhi*);

if there are sentient beings who each preach the Dharma but do not find mutual joy in it, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Pure Eye of Wisdom (*viśuddha-prajñā-cakṣus*), free from the net of doubt.
If there are sentient beings who do not give rise to faith within the Triple Gem, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Increase of Merit;
if there are sentient beings parched for the rain of Dharma, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the Rain of Dharma;

if there are sentient beings who give rise to views of annihilationism regarding the Triple Gem, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Adornments of All Jewels.

If there are sentient beings who do not perform the work of wisdom and do not exert diligent effort, yet upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Vajra Wisdom Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings bound by various afflictions, yet upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Space Seal Samādhi;
if there are sentient beings who conceive of a self and what belongs to a self, yet upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Wisdom Seal Samādhi.
If there are sentient beings who do not know that the Tathāgata is fully endowed with merit, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of worldly liberation;

if there are sentient beings who have not made offerings to the Buddha in past lives, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain various transformations of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*);

if there are sentient beings who have not, throughout immeasurable kalpas in future lives, attained the teaching on the single gate of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the explanation that all dharmas are identical within the single dharma-realm.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained discernment regarding any of the sūtras, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of the True Mark of the Equality of All Dharmas;
if there are sentient beings who are separated from the six dharmas of harmony, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Understanding All Dharmas;

if there are sentient beings who do not exert diligent effort in the inconceivable dharma-gate of liberation, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Lion’s Play Samādhi among all the supernormal powers.

If there are sentient beings who wish to analytically enter the Tathāgatagarbha, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma—and not hearing it from another—they immediately attain the analytical entry into the Tathāgatagarbha;

if there are sentient beings who do not diligently apply themselves to the bodhisattva path, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain wisdom and practice with diligent vigor;
if there are sentient beings who have never before seen the Jātaka-sūtras, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the samādhi of being present everywhere.
If there are sentient beings who have not yet completed their practice of the Path, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Receiving Prophecy;
if there are sentient beings who have not yet fully attained the ten powers of a Tathāgata, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Indestructibility;
if there are sentient beings who have not yet fully attained the four fearlessnesses, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Inexhaustible Intention.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the fullness of the Buddha’s unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*), upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the *asādhāraṇa-samādhi*;
if there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the fullness of the vision free from delusion, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the *praṇidhāna-pada-samādhi*;

if there are sentient beings who have not yet awakened to the gateway of all Buddha-dharmas, upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain the *vimala-śukla-viśuddha-mudrā-samādhi*.

If there are sentient beings who have not yet attained the full realization of all-knowledge, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Skillful Comprehension;

if there are sentient beings who have not yet accomplished all Buddha-works, upon hearing the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, they immediately attain the Samādhi of Immeasurable and Inexhaustible Intention.
Sentient beings such as these each attain faith and understanding within the Buddha-Dharma.

“There are bodhisattvas whose minds are upright and free from guile; upon hearing the Buddha preach the Dharma, they immediately attain eighty-four thousand gateways to the dharmas, eighty-four thousand gateways to samādhis, and seventy-five thousand gateways to dhāraṇīs.”

There were immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had cultivated and gathered the Mahāyāna; upon hearing this teaching of the Dharma, they too attained such immeasurable merit and came to abide securely in the stage of non-retrogression.

Therefore, because the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas desire to attain various kinds of firm adornments, they give rise to inconceivable vows and increase inconceivable knowledge and vision to adorn themselves. By adorning themselves with the thirty-two marks, they obtain the eighty secondary characteristics; by adorning themselves with sublime voices, they preach the Dharma according to what sentient beings delight in, causing those who hear the Dharma to fulfill their knowledge and vision;
by adorning themselves with the mind, they attain all samādhis without falling back;
and by adorning themselves with mindfulness, they do not lose any of the dhāraṇīs.
By adorning the mind, one attains the discernment of all phenomena;
by adorning mindfulness, one understands meanings as subtle as atoms;
and by adorning the virtuous mind, one attains firm vows and steadfast diligence, reaching the further shore according to one's aspirations.
Because they are adorned with single-minded concentration, they pass through the stages of dwelling in succession;
because they are adorned with generosity, they are able to relinquish all that is required;
because they are adorned with ethical discipline, they cause the mind to become thoroughly bright, pure, and stainless.
Because they are adorned with patience, their minds are free from obstructions toward all sentient beings;
because they are adorned with diligence, they assist all things and cause them to be fully accomplished;
because they are adorned with meditative concentration, they attain the lion’s play within all samādhis.
Because they are adorned with wisdom, they know the habitual tendencies of all afflictions;
because they are adorned with loving-kindness, they single-mindedly keep all sentient beings in mind;
because they are adorned with compassion, they are able to pull all sentient beings out from their suffering.
Because they are adorned with joy, their minds have no doubt or confusion regarding all phenomena;
because they are adorned with equanimity, they attain freedom from arrogance, and their minds are without highs or lows;
because they are adorned with the various supernormal powers, they attain the lion’s play regarding all phenomena.
Because they are adorned with merit, they obtain the inexhaustible treasure-hand;
because they are adorned with wisdom, they know all the minds of sentient beings;
because they are adorned with intention, they skillfully awaken all sentient beings.
Because of the adornment of radiance, one attains the clarity of the eye of wisdom;
because of the adornment of various eloquences, one enables sentient beings to attain the Dharma, its meaning, and appropriate speech;
because of the adornment of fearlessness, all Māras are unable to create obstacles.
By means of the adornment of merit, one attains all the merits possessed by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
by means of the adornment of the Dharma, one attains unimpeded eloquence and constantly expounds the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
by means of the adornment of radiance, one attains the radiance of all Buddha-dharmas.
Because of the adornment of illumination, they are able to shine universally throughout all Buddha-worlds;
because of the adornment of the knowledge of others' minds, they attain correct wisdom free from confusion;
because of the adornment of instruction, they attain the observance of prohibitive precepts exactly as taught.
Because they are adorned with the supernormal powers (*ṛddhipāda*), they attain the bases of power (*ṛddhipāda*) and reach the further shore;
because they uphold the adornments of all Tathāgatas, they gain entry into the immeasurable Dharma-treasury of the Tathāgatas;
because they are adorned by the veneration of the Dharma, they attain wisdom that does not depend on others.

Because they adorn themselves by practicing all wholesome dharmas accordingly, they act as they have spoken, desiring that all such sentient beings may fully attain these and other merits and benefits.

If there are immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who cultivate and assemble the Mahāyāna, because of my teaching of even a single phrase of Dharma, they shall all be fully endowed with such pure and wholesome dharmas and made complete. For this reason, the wisdom that these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain regarding all phenomena is not heard from another; they achieve the light of the Great Dharma and realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

If sentient beings in other worlds commit the five heinous crimes, or even violate the four grave prohibitions, thereby burning away and extinguishing wholesome dharmas—whether they be students of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, or Mahāyāna vehicles—and by the power of their vows desire to come to be born in my world; once they have been born here, they further take up all manner of unwholesome karma that is coarse, vulgar, and depraved. Their minds delight in seeking out what is violent and difficult to tame, and they are exclusively attached to the four inversions, being stingy and miserly.”
For such sentient beings—eighty-four thousand with diverse natures and distracted minds—I shall, for each of their respective natures, extensively expound eighty-four thousand aggregates of Dharma.

“Blessed One! If there are sentient beings who study the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, I shall fully and extensively expound the six pāramitās for them—namely, from the dānapāramitā up to the prajñāpāramitā.”

If there are sentient beings who study the Śrāvaka vehicle but have not yet planted roots of goodness, and who aspire to take the Buddhas as their teachers, I shall establish them in the three refuges, and thereafter exhort them to abide in the six pāramitās.
If there are sentient beings who delight in killing, I shall establish them in non-killing.
If there are sentient beings who are exclusively intent on evil greed, I shall establish them in non-stealing.
If there are sentient beings who engage in unrighteous and perverse sexual misconduct, I shall establish them in non-perversion of sexual conduct.
If there are sentient beings who each intentionally commit slanderous and false speech, I shall establish them in non-false speech.
If there are sentient beings who delight in being狂癡 (mad and deluded), I shall establish them in the practice of abstaining from intoxicants.
If there are sentient beings who commit these five transgressions, I shall cause them to receive the five precepts of an upāsaka.
If there are sentient beings who do not find joy in various wholesome dharmas, I shall cause them to observe the eight precepts for one day and one night.

If there are sentient beings with few roots of goodness who develop a heart of love and joy toward those roots of goodness, I shall cause them, in a future life, to leave the household life and study the Way within the Buddha-dharma, establishing them securely in the ten pure and clean precepts.

If there are sentient beings who, with a longing mind, seek all dharmas of the roots of goodness, I shall establish them within those dharmas of the roots of goodness, causing them to achieve the fulfillment of pure conduct and the great precepts.

For such beings as these—who have committed the five heinous crimes, up to and including those who are stingy—he manifests supernormal powers through various means and explains the meanings of all phrases. He reveals the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense bases (*āyatana*), as well as suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self, so that they may abide in the sublime, peaceful, and fearless nirvana. For the sake of these fourfold assemblies—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—he preaches the Dharma.

If there are sentient beings who seek to hear discourses on the treatises, I shall expound the treatises of the True Dharma; even for those who seek liberation, I shall expound the treatises on emptiness and non-existence.
If there are sentient beings whose minds do not delight in the true and wholesome Dharma, I shall explain to them the various matters of worldly activity.
If there are sentient beings whose minds love and delight in the true and wholesome Dharma, I shall explain to them the samādhi of emptiness and demonstrate true liberation.
“World-Honored One!

For the sake of each and every such sentient being, even if I must travel beyond hundreds of thousands of yojanas without employing supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), I shall nonetheless employ immeasurable and boundless various skillful means (*upāya*) to explain the meaning of the phrases, manifesting supernatural powers until their final nirvāṇa, without my mind ever giving rise to weariness.”
“World-Honored One!

By the power of samādhi, I shall relinquish five-sixths of the lifespan obtained and enter parinirvāṇa. At that time, out of compassion for sentient beings, I shall divide my own body into parts as small as half a mustard seed and seek parinirvāṇa.”
After my parinirvāṇa, all the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a thousand years, and the Semblance Dharma shall remain for a full five hundred years.

After my nirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who offer precious jewels and music to my relics, or even those who perform prostrations, circumambulate to the right once, join their palms in praise, or scatter a single flower—by these causes and conditions, according to their respective aspirations, they shall each attain non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles.
“World-Honored One!

After my parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings within my Dharma who can firmly uphold even a single precept as I have taught it, or even recite a single four-line verse for others and cause those listeners to give rise to joy, or make offerings to the Dharma teacher—even with a single flower or a single prostration—by virtue of these causes and conditions, may they each attain non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles according to their aspirations, until the torch of the Dharma is extinguished and the banner of the Dharma has fallen.”

When the True Dharma has ceased, my relics shall immediately sink into the earth down to the adamantine base. At that time, the Sahā world will be empty and devoid of precious jewels; my relics shall transform into wish-fulfilling *vaidūrya* gems. Their brilliant flames will surge forth from the adamantine base into the world, reaching upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven. They will rain down various flowers—*māndārava*, *mahāmāndārava*, *pāriyātra*, *mañjūṣaka*, and *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers. There will be pure radiance as large as a chariot wheel, with a hundred petals, a thousand petals, or even a hundred thousand petals, their light illuminating everywhere.
Furthermore, there are exquisite and subtle fragrances that are constantly diffused, such that those who behold them never grow weary.
Their brilliant flames are so intense as to be beyond measure, and their subtle, wondrous fragrance is infinite and boundless; they rain down exclusively such immeasurable varieties of flowers.
When it rains, various subtle and wondrous sounds emerge: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma,
the sound of the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus, the sound of the three refuges, the sound of the lay follower’s precepts, the sound of the accomplishment of the eight precepts,
the sound of the ten precepts for those who have left the household life, the sound of giving, the sound of maintaining the precepts, and the sound of pure brahmacarya.
The sound of possessing the great precepts; the sound of assisting in communal affairs; the sound of reciting the sūtras; the sound of meditative contemplation;

the sound of contemplating impurity; the sound of mindfulness of inhalation and exhalation; the sound of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; the sound of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;
the sound of the sphere of infinite consciousness; the sound of the sphere of infinite space; the sound of the eight bases of mastery; and the sound of the ten totalities.

From within those flowers, there issued forth such sounds as the sound of entry [into the path], the sound of concentration and wisdom, the sound of emptiness, the sound of signlessness, the sound of wishlessness,
the sound of the twelve links of dependent origination, the sound of the complete collection of the Śrāvaka-piṭaka, the sound of training in the Pratyekabuddha path,
and the sound of the fulfillment of the six pāramitās of the Mahāyāna; these were the sounds produced for the devas of the form realm.
Having heard all of this, they each recalled the roots of goodness they had cultivated in the past;
immediately repenting and reproaching themselves for all their unwholesome deeds, they descended to the Sahā world to teach and transform immeasurable sentient beings,
causing them all to abide securely within the ten wholesome paths of action.

The devas of the desire realm also hear and receive [this teaching]; all their fetters of craving, greed, and delight in the five desires, as well as all mental factors, become entirely tranquil. They each remember the roots of goodness they previously cultivated, and immediately repent and reproach themselves for all unwholesome deeds. Thereupon, they descend to the Sahā world to transform immeasurable sentient beings, causing them all to abide securely within the ten wholesome paths of action.
“World-Honored One!

These flowers in the void shall further manifest as various kinds of precious treasures—gold, silver, mani-jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, jade, genuine gems, counterfeit gems, agate, coral, celestial crowns, and jeweled ornaments—falling like rain until they completely fill the Sahā world.”

At that time, the hearts of the people were harmonious and joyful; there was no strife, hunger, or disease. Hostile enemies from other regions, harsh speech, and all manner of poisons were entirely extinguished, and all attained tranquility.
At that time, there was such bliss in the world that if any sentient beings saw, touched, or made use of various precious jewels, they would never regress from the Three Vehicles.
"These precious jewels have performed this benefit; having performed the benefit, they have vanished back into the earth, returning to their original place upon the vajra-limit.
"World-Honored One!"

When the kalpa of warfare arises in this Sahā world, my bodily relics shall again manifest as sapphire-blue beryl beads emerging from the earth, ascending as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven. There they shall rain down various flowers—Mandārava flowers, Mahāmāndārava flowers, and Pāriyātraka flowers—and continue in this manner until they sink back into the earth, reaching their original dwelling place at the Vajra-limit, where it shall be exactly the same.
“World-Honored One!
Just as it is during the kalpa of weapons, so it is also during the kalpas of famine and pestilence.
“World-Honored One! [he continued.]

Thus, within this Great Bhadrakalpa, after my parinirvāṇa, these various relics shall perform such Buddha-works as to subdue immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, causing them to attain non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles. In this manner, throughout great kalpas as numerous as the atoms in five Buddha-worlds, they shall subdue immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, causing them to attain non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles.
“World-Honored One!

If, after a full thousand *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there are those who attain Buddhahood and appear in the world within the immeasurable and boundless *asaṃkhyeya* remaining worlds of the ten directions, they are all those whom I taught and transformed when I was practicing for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, causing them to first resolve their minds on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and establishing them firmly in the six *pāramitās*.
“‘World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, those whom I have exhorted and transformed to resolve upon the mind of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and whom I have established and caused to dwell in the six pāramitās; as well as those sentient beings who are transformed by the manifestations of my śarīra-relics after my parinirvāṇa—all such beings shall, after more than a thousand *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, attain Buddhahood and appear in the world throughout immeasurable and boundless *asaṃkhyeya* worlds in the ten directions, and they shall all utter my name and speak in praise of me:’”

"In the distant past, there was an eon named Bhadra. At the beginning of that eon, there was a fourth World-Honored One named [Name]. That Buddha, the World-Honored One, exhorted and transformed us, causing us for the first time to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, we had burned away our wholesome minds, accumulated roots of unwholesomeness, and committed the five heinous crimes up to the point of holding false views. At that moment, that Buddha exhorted and transformed us, causing us to dwell securely in the six *pāramitās*. Because of this, we immediately attained the understanding of all *dhāraṇī* gates, turned the wheel of the true Dharma, and were freed from the bonds of birth and death. We caused immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to dwell in the supreme fruit, and further enabled immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to settle in the fruits of gods and humans, up to the fruit of liberation.
"If there are sentient beings seeking the path to bodhi who, having heard this praise of me, each ask the Buddha:
'For what purpose and benefit did that World-Honored Buddha attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi amidst the heavy five turbidities of this evil world?'"

Then those World-Honored Ones immediately spoke to these sons and daughters of good family who seek the path to bodhi, explaining the great compassion they had accomplished in the past, their initial aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and the causal origins of their adornment of worlds and their wondrous, virtuous vows.

Having heard this, that person was struck with awe and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence. Immediately, they made a sublime vow, conceiving a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings no different from their own, and spoke these words of aspiration:

"In whatever world of the five heavy turbidities there may be, where sentient beings commit the five heinous crimes and even cultivate all roots of unwholesomeness, I shall therein bring them to subdual."

Those World-Honored Ones, because these people have accomplished great compassion and made various virtuous vows in this world of five turbidities, bestow upon them predictions of enlightenment according to their respective requests.
“‘World-Honored One!
That Buddha, the World-Honored One, further explained for those who study the Mahāyāna the causal conditions for the manifestations produced by my relics:

“In the distant past, there was a Buddha, the World-Honored One, named [so-and-so]. After his parinirvāṇa, an age of swords, pestilence, and famine arose. At that time, we underwent various sufferings within that kalpa. For our sake, the relics of that Buddha performed various miraculous feats and lion-like displays. Consequently, we were able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, plant various roots of goodness, and diligently cultivate and accumulate the six *pāramitās*, as described at length above.’”
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Śāntamati: "Good son!

At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara was in the presence of the Buddha Ratnagarbha, before a great assembly of devas, humans, and non-humans. He immediately attained the accomplishment of the mind of great compassion, vast and immeasurable. Having made five hundred vows, he again addressed the Buddha, saying:"
“World-Honored One!

If my vow is not fulfilled and I do not obtain my own benefit, then I shall not, within the future Bhadrakalpa—during the fivefold turbidities of the evil age, amidst mutual strife and contention, in this final era of blindness and folly, where there is no teacher to consult and no instruction to follow, having fallen into various views and the great darkness—perform the five heinous acts as described above, nor shall I fulfill my vow or carry out the work of a Buddha.”
I now renounce the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*) and do not wish to plant various roots of goodness in the Buddha-fields of other directions.

World-Honored One! With such single-minded resolve as I have now, I shall not attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* through these roots of goodness; nor do I wish to seek the vehicle of the *pratyekabuddha*, nor do I wish to become one of the vehicles of the *śrāvaka*, nor a king of gods or a king of men. Greedily delighting in the five desires, I would take birth among gods or humans; I do not seek to become a *gandharva*, *asura*, *garuḍa*, *kiṃnara*, *mahoraga*, *yakṣa*, *rākṣasa*, or any of the dragon kings (*nāgarāja*). By means of these roots of goodness, I do not seek any such states.

World-Honored One! If one attains great wealth, it is caused by giving; if one is born in the heavens, it is caused by precepts; if one attains great wisdom, it is caused by extensive study; and if one cuts off afflictions, it is caused by contemplation.
As the Buddha has said: "In matters such as these, those who possess the merit of their own benefit will be able to obtain whatever they seek."
“World-Honored One!

If my roots of goodness are fulfilled so that I may attain my own benefit, may all my acts of giving, observance of precepts, extensive learning, and contemplation be fully accomplished. By means of this karmic fruit, I dedicate it for the sake of all sentient beings in the hells. If there are sentient beings who have fallen into the Avīci Hell, by these roots of goodness, may they be rescued and brought to birth among humans; upon hearing the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, may they immediately attain understanding, become Arhats, and swiftly enter Nirvāṇa.”
If the karmic retributions of these sentient beings have not yet been exhausted, I shall relinquish my life-span and enter the Avīci Hell to undergo suffering and affliction on their behalf.
I vow that my body shall become as numerous as the atoms within a single Buddha-world, each individual body equal in size to Mount Sumeru;
and that each and every one of these bodies shall perceive all forms of suffering and joy, just as the suffering and joy perceived by my present body.

In each and every body, they shall receive retributions for various grave evils and afflictions equal in number to the atoms within a single Buddha-world; as many as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world today,

so shall it be for all sentient beings in the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions who commit the five heinous crimes and give rise to unwholesome karma, even unto their eventual fall into the Avīci Hell.
If, for as many great eons as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world,

all sentient beings throughout as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms in the ten directions were to commit the five heinous crimes and give rise to unwholesome karma such that they would fall into the Avīci Hell, I shall, for the sake of all these sentient beings, [remain] in the Avīci...
They shall undergo all sufferings on behalf of those in hell, ensuring that beings do not fall into hell;
they shall encounter the Buddhas, receive and study the sublime Dharma, emerge from birth and death, and enter the city of Nirvana.
I must now, on behalf of these sentient beings, dwell perpetually in the Avīci Hell for a very long time.
