Furthermore, if all the sentient beings in as many worlds in the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world were to fully ripen their evil karma and inevitably undergo its fruit—falling into the Fire-Scorching Hell, such as the Avīci Hell, the aforementioned Scorching Hell, the Mahāraurava Hell, the Samghāta Hell, the Kālasūtra Hell, and the Saṃjīva Hell—and likewise into various forms of animals, hungry ghosts, the impoverished, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, asuras, garuḍas, and so forth—all would be exactly like this.
“World-Honored One!

If there were as many sentient beings in all the worlds of the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world, who have accomplished evil karma and must inevitably undergo its retribution—being born among humans yet deaf, blind, mute, handless, footless, with disordered minds and lost mindfulness, eating impure things—I would also take upon myself the various sins of such sentient beings, as described above.”

Furthermore, if there are sentient beings who fall into the Avīci Hell and undergo various sufferings and afflictions, I shall for a long time take upon myself these sufferings and afflictions on their behalf; this applies likewise to the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense-bases (*āyatana*) experienced by sentient beings in the cycle of birth and death, as well as those in the realms of animals, hungry ghosts, the poor, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, asuras, garuḍas, and so forth.
“World-Honored One!

If my vow is fulfilled and I attain my own benefit, achieving Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi as I have vowed above, may all the present Buddhas throughout the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable worlds of the ten directions—who are currently preaching the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings—bear witness for me; this is also that which those Buddhas know and see.”
“World-Honored One!

I pray that you will now grant me the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi: that during this Bhadrakalpa, when the human lifespan is one hundred and twenty years, I shall appear in the world as a Buddha—a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.”

"Bhagavān! If I am certain to accomplish such Buddha-work as I have vowed, may this great assembly, along with the devas, nāgas, asuras, and others—whether they dwell on the earth or in the void—with the sole exception of the Tathāgata, all shed tears and, before me, prostrate themselves with their heads at my feet and say in praise: 'Excellent!'"
Excellent! Your accomplishment of great compassion is beyond compare.
Having attained profound mindfulness, you have given rise to this deep compassion for the sake of all sentient beings and made firm and resolute vows.

What you have now accomplished was not through the instruction of another; rather, with a single-minded great compassion, you have protected all beings and gathered in those who commit the five heinous crimes and other unwholesome acts.

I now fully know your virtuous vows: when you first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, you already acted as a great panacea for sentient beings, serving as their refuge, protection, and dwelling place, making this vow so that sentient beings might attain liberation.
"Since you have now obtained your own benefit through this aspiration, the Tathāgata bestows upon you the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Having spoken these words, the Cakravartin King Ananta-viśuddha immediately rose from his seat, weeping with tears falling; with palms joined in reverence, he bowed his head to the ground in salutation toward the brahmin and spoke in verse:
"The aspiration you have now made Is firm and profoundly deep."
Relinquishing his own happiness, he gave rise to great compassion for all sentient beings; for our sake,
he has manifested the true reality of all phenomena, their wondrous and supreme characteristics.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke these verses in praise:
“Sentient beings are attached to many things, But you now have no attachments.
Regarding the various faculties, both superior and inferior, You have long since attained mastery.”
"Therefore, in accordance with sentient beings, I shall fully grant them their faculties and aspirations;
In future worlds, they shall attain The treasury of wisdom of dhāraṇīs.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta spoke these verses in praise:
“‘Billions of sentient beings have gathered for the sake of virtue;
seeing you, the Great Compassionate One, they all weep.
The various ascetic practices you have performed are such as have never occurred before.’”
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva again spoke in verse as praise:
“Vigor and samādhi are exceedingly firm and solid;
Sublime and supreme wisdom is well able to discern.”
"If one offers you flowers and incense,
you shall today be able to accept them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Gaganamudrā again spoke a verse of praise, saying:
"For the sake of sentient beings, you have perfected great compassion;
renouncing wealth to practice giving, in this turbid and evil world,
you maintain all the marks with supreme, subtle excellence."
"For the sake of all devas and humans, You act as their Teacher and Tamer.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsa again spoke in verse as praise:
"Your present heart of great compassion Is as vast as empty space;
"Desiring to be a kinsman to all sentient beings, you thus manifest the practice of bodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ākāśasūrya again spoke in verse as praise:
"The great compassion and merit that you have accomplished—"
"His supreme and wondrous wisdom skillfully discerns the characteristics of phenomena;
with the exception of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, none others can equal him.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha again spoke in verse as praise:
"In a future age, during this Bhadrakalpa, amidst a world of manifold afflictions,
you shall attain great renown and cause immeasurable sentient beings to likewise [attain it]."
"Having severed all suffering and affliction, One attains wondrous liberation.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva again spoke in verse as praise:
"All sentient beings, Diligently cultivate and accumulate [merit];"
Starved by the cycle of birth and death, you traverse the mountains of false views,
devouring one another without a single virtuous thought;
yet, through your great compassion, you are able to gather them in.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya further spoke in verse, praising him:
"Having burned away the virtuous mind, One is intent on committing rebellious evils;
Falling into the great ignorance, Into the midst of black darkness."
"Having no means of escape from the mire of afflictions,
you have already taken such sentient beings under your care.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Fragrant Hand again spoke in verse as praise:
"You now clearly see that in future ages there will be many terrors;
observe them as if looking at reflections in a mirror—
among those sentient beings, the True Dharma will be destroyed."
"All wholesome states of mind are utterly incinerated.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ratnākara further spoke in verse of praise:
"You now possess, through pure wisdom and the observance of precepts,"
With samādhi and compassion adorning their minds,
they are able to gather in such sentient beings who have burned away wholesome dharmas and slandered the sages.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Free from Fear Adornment again spoke in verse of praise, saying:
"The immeasurable ascetic practices you now cultivate are all for the purpose of gathering in sentient beings of the future."
"You burn away the virtuous mind, relying instead on false views.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpahasta again spoke in verse as praise:
"You now possess great compassion, wisdom, and diligence."
Within this great assembly, there is none who can equal him;
therefore, he gathers in those with minds of wrong views who are oppressed by old age, sickness, death, and suffering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jñānakīrti again spoke in verse as praise:
“Countless sentient beings, Afflicted by manifold sufferings of illness,
Are constantly buffeted by afflictions, Like being driven by a malignant wind.”
"You are now able, with the water of great wisdom,
to extinguish all Māras and shatter their power and influence.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharanimudrā again spoke a verse of praise, saying:
“You have now attained firm and steadfast diligence,
whereby you are able to exhaust all afflictions and achieve liberation;
our aspirations are meager, and we cannot reach such a state.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Candraprabhā again spoke in verse,
praising him: "Steadfast in cultivation, Exerting effort with focused intent,
Relying upon merit, He gives rise to a heart of compassion;
"Therefore, in future ages, you shall be able to sever for all sentient beings the fetters of the three realms of existence throughout the three periods of time.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimalacandra again spoke in verse as praise:
“The path practiced by Bodhisattvas takes great compassion as supreme;
what is taught is not established through signs. Therefore, I prostrate to you.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīśvara again spoke in verse as praise:
"In this world of the five turbidities, There are many afflictions and diseases;
You rely upon Bodhi And have made firm and steadfast vows."
"For the sake of all sentient beings, you sever the roots of affliction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Fire-Topknot again spoke in verse as praise:
"Your wisdom is like a treasury of jewels,"
The vows he has made are pure and stainless;
the practice he performs is for unsurpassed bodhi,
solely to act as a great king of physicians for all sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Manifest Power wept with tears of compassion; standing before the brahmin, he prostrated himself, joining his palms and hands together, and spoke these verses of praise:
“By means of this great torch of wisdom, you now sever the disease of afflictions for the sake of all sentient beings.”
"Furthermore, for the sake of those who are impoverished and destitute sentient beings,
I shall sever and eliminate all their immeasurable sufferings. "Good son!"

At that time, the entire great assembly—including devas, nāgas, spirits, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans—prostrated themselves before the brahmin with their heads at his feet. Having paid homage, they stood up, joined their palms in reverence, and praised him with various methods of eulogy.
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Silent Mind:

"Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara knelt with his right knee upon the ground before the Tathāgata. At that moment, the great earth shook in six ways; likewise, all the Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions—equal in number to the atoms within a single Buddha-world—also shook in six ways. A great radiance shone everywhere throughout the world, and various kinds of flowers rained down."

Mandārava flowers, mahā-mandārava flowers, pāriyātra flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, and mahā-mañjūṣaka flowers—even those with immeasurable radiance that shines throughout the ten directions—[appeared] in as many pure and impure worlds as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world. In every place where the present Buddhas were teaching the True Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, and where each of those Buddhas had bodhisattvas seated before them listening to the Dharma, those bodhisattvas saw this great earth shake in six ways, [the Buddhas] emitting great light and raining down various kinds of flowers. Having seen these things, they came forward and addressed the Buddhas, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"For what cause and condition does this great earth tremble in six ways, with a great radiance appearing and various flowers raining down?

At that time, to the east of this world, at a distance of as many worlds as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a Buddha-world named Selection of Precious Jewels. In it dwells a Buddha named Ratnacandra Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. He currently resides there, surrounded by and reverently attended by immeasurable, boundless, asaṃkhyeya great bodhisattvas, preaching the Mahāyāna Dharma.
There were two bodhisattvas, one named Ratnalakṣaṇa and the other named Candralakṣaṇa, who, facing the Buddha Ratnacandra, joined their palms in reverent salutation and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"For what cause and condition do the six kinds of earth tremors occur, why is there great radiance, and why does it rain down various flowers?
At that time, that Buddha addressed the two Bodhisattvas: "Virtuous sons!"

To the west, at a distance from here equal to the sands of one Ganges River, there is a world named Santirana. There dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Ratnagarbha Tathāgata. This Buddha, the World-Honored One, currently resides there together with immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas, bestowing upon them the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and preaching such sutras as those that describe various lands, reveal the adornments of all buddha-worlds, and explain the samādhi-borders and dharani-gates of excellent vows.
Within that great assembly, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of Great Compassion who made this vow:
"I shall now perfume my mind with great compassion and receive the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; for the sake of all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, I shall manifest these excellent vows."

For this reason, he first commanded immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas to make great vows to take up various adorned worlds to subdue sentient beings. This is the Great Compassion achieved by these bodhisattvas, which none among the great assemblies can equal; it subdues those who are corrupt, evil, and full of afflictions in the five turbidities, and gathers in all those who have committed the five heinous crimes, even those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness and burned away their wholesome minds. Among that great assembly of devas, nāgas, spirits, humans, and non-humans, those who did not make offerings to the Buddha shall all together make offerings to this final bodhisattva who has achieved Great Compassion.
Having prostrated with his head at [the Buddha’s] feet, he rose and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke verses of praise.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika stood before the Buddha, his right knee touching the ground, listening for the Buddha’s prophecy. Thereupon, the World-Honored One smiled; by this cause and condition, the earth in worlds throughout the ten directions—as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field—trembled in six ways, emitting great radiance and raining down various flowers. This awakened all the bodhisattvas and likewise manifested the path of the bodhisattvas.

That Buddha, the World-Honored One, caused all the bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions—equal in number to the atoms within a single buddha-field—to assemble together. For the sake of these great bodhisattvas, he preached various gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, as well as the dharma-gates of fearlessness; it is for this reason that that Buddha manifested such various transformations.
“Good son! At that time, having heard these words, the two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
How much time has elapsed since this Great Compassionate Bodhisattva first resolved his mind [for enlightenment]?
Furthermore, for how long has he practiced the bodhisattva path?

And at what time will he, within the five turbidities of this evil world, tame and gather those sentient beings who possess thick and heavy afflictions, who engage in mutual strife and contention, who frequently commit the five heinous crimes, who have brought to fruition all roots of non-virtue, and whose virtuous minds have been incinerated?
At that time, the Buddha said to the two bodhisattvas:
"Sons of good family!
This Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā has today for the first time resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"Good son! You should now go to see the Buddha Ratnagarbha; pay him homage, make offerings, prostrate, and circumambulate him. Listen to such sūtras as the *Samādhi-dhāraṇī-mukha* and the *Abhayadharma-mukha*. Furthermore, visit the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika and speak these words in my voice:
'The Tathāgata Ratnacandra sends his greetings and presents this Moonlight Pure Flower as a token of trust to you.'"
Furthermore, they praised you, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! Since you first resolved your mind on enlightenment, you have already been able to accomplish such great compassion. You now possess immeasurable renown that pervades as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-field; all say, 'The Bodhisattva of Great Compassion—since he first resolved his mind on enlightenment, he has already been able to accomplish such great compassion.'"
Therefore, son of good family!
I now praise you; excellent, excellent!
Furthermore, son of good family!

For the sake of future bodhisattvas so that they may accomplish great compassion, you have spoken of this uninterrupted great compassion and virtuous vow, and have erected the banner of the Dharma; therefore, I praise you once more, saying, "Excellent!"

Excellent! Furthermore, son of good family, your name shall endure in future ages for as many asaṃkhyeya kalpas as there are atoms in a single buddha-field. You shall teach hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable, boundless, and asaṃkhyeya sentient beings, establishing them in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi so that they reach the stage of non-retrogression upon attaining Buddhahood. Whether they make virtuous vows or take up pure lands, you shall gather in sentient beings and tame them accordingly, further causing them to receive the prediction of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the future.

Thus, these sentient beings, after passing through as many eons as there are atoms in a single buddha-field in future ages, shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in as many Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions as there are atoms in a single buddha-field, turn the wheel of the true Dharma, and further praise the Bodhisattvas of Great Compassion.
"Therefore, I praise you with these three methods of praise:
'Excellent! Excellent! " 'Good son!'"
At that time, there were twelve billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in that land who, with one voice and in unison, spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!..."

"We wish to go to the realm of Santirana to see the Buddha Ratnagarbha, to pay homage, make offerings, show respect, and circumambulate him; we wish to hear such sutras as the various gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, and the gates of the dharma of fearlessness, and we also wish to see the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika."
At that time, that Buddha, by means of these three methods of praise and the Moonlight Pure Flower, addressed the two bodhisattvas, saying:
"You should know that now is the time."

At that time, the Bodhisattvas Ratnalakṣaṇa and Candralakṣaṇa, taking moonlight-pure flowers from that Buddha’s presence, set out from that world together with nine billion two hundred million bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Like a flash of lightning appearing and vanishing, they arrived at the presence of the Buddha Ratnagarbha within the Jambūvana Grove in the land of Santiraṇa.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated with their heads at his feet. Having made offerings to the Buddha by means of the various lion-like playful displays attained by the bodhisattvas, they saw the brahmin Ratnasāgara being respectfully saluted and praised with palms joined by this great assembly. Seeing this, they immediately reflected:
"This Great Being must surely be a Bodhisattva of Great Compassion; it is for this reason that the Tathāgata Ratnacandra has sent these precious flowers."
Those two bodhisattvas immediately turned toward the brahmin before the Buddha and gave him the flowers, speaking these words:
"The Tathāgata Ratnacandra gives you these exquisite flowers as a token of faith, along with the three praises of the Dharma as previously described."

"In this way, from the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddha-worlds of the eastern direction, immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were also dispatched to the realm of Santīraṇa; they all used the Dharma of the Threefold Praise with the Pure Moonlight Flower, as described above."

“Good son! At that time, seventy-seven thousand times ten million billion Buddha-worlds to the south of here, there was a Buddha-world named Jewel-Pavilion Lion’s Roar. There dwelt a Buddha named Lion-Aspect Honored King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat, who currently resides there, preaching the Mahāyāna Dharma for the sake of all bodhisattvas.”
There were two bodhisattva-mahāsattvas: the first was named Vajrajñānalakṣaṇa and the second was named Siṃhavajralakṣaṇa. These two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what cause and condition does the earth quake in six ways, a great radiance appear, and various flowers rain down?
All these matters were just as they had been with the bodhisattvas in the eastern direction.
Furthermore, the Buddhas of the south, immeasurable and boundless in number, likewise dispatched immeasurable Bodhisattvas to the realm of Santirana.

At that time, eighty-nine thousand times ten million billion worlds away from here to the west, there was a world named Sukhāvatī. There dwells a Buddha named Sarvendriyasaṃgrahaśuddhanetra Tathāgata, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to the fourfold assembly.

There were two bodhisattvas: the first was named Bhadra-sūrya-prabhāsa (Virtuous Sun Radiance), and the second was named Siṃha-nāda-kāya (Lion’s Roar Body). These two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"For what cause and condition does the earth quake in six ways, great radiance appear, and various flowers rain down?
The rest is as explained above.
Thus it was likewise in immeasurable worlds in the western direction.

"At that time, ninety thousand billion worlds away to the north, there was a world named Supreme True Jewel. There dwelt a Buddha named World-Honored King Tathāgata, who currently resides there, preaching the Mahāyāna Dharma for the sake of all bodhisattvas."
There were two bodhisattvas, one named Acaladhara and the other named Jñānalabdhalokendra-rāja; these two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
“For what cause and condition does the earth shake in six ways?
The rest is as explained above.
It is likewise in immeasurable worlds in the northern direction.

“At that time, nine hundred and eighty thousand billion nayutas of worlds below this world-system, there was a world named Free from Darkness and Fog. There dwelt a Buddha named Sound Free from the Encirclement of Fear, who currently resides there, preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to the fourfold assembly.”
There were two bodhisattvas, one named Sūryaguru and the other named Gaganasūrya. These two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
By what causes and conditions does the earth tremble in six ways?"
The remainder is as explained above.
It is likewise for the worlds of the nadir.
*Beihua jing*, Scroll Seven.
The Sutra of the Compassionate Flower, Scroll Eight, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmakṣema of India during the Northern Liang Dynasty.
Chapter Four, Part Six: The Original Prophecies of the Bodhisattvas.

"At that time, above this world, passing through two million hundred thousand worlds, there was a world named Wondrous Flower. In it dwelt a Buddha named Flower-Blossoming Sun-King Tathāgata, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to the fourfold assembly."

There were two bodhisattvas: the first was named Selecting One’s Own Dharma to Gather in a Land, and the second was named Wondrous Sound of Dhāraṇī. These two bodhisattvas together addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"For what cause and condition does this great earth quake in six ways, with great radiance appearing and various flowers raining down?
At that time, that Buddha addressed the two bodhisattvas: "Good sons!"

Twenty million hundred thousand worlds below, there is a world named Santirana. There dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, titled Ratnagarbha Tathāgata. This Buddha, the World-Honored One, currently resides together with immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas, bestowing upon them the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. He expounds upon various lands and reveals the adornments, virtuous vows, samādhi realms, and dharani gates of all the Buddha-worlds, as well as other such sutras.
Within that great assembly, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of Great Compassion who made this vow:
"I shall now perfume my mind with great compassion and receive the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; for the sake of all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, I shall manifest these excellent vows."

For this reason, he first commanded immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas to make great vows to take up various adorned worlds to subdue sentient beings. The great compassion achieved by these bodhisattvas is such that none among the great assembly can equal it; they subdue those who are corrupt, evil, and full of afflictions in the five turbidities, and they gather in all those who have committed the five heinous crimes, even those who have accumulated roots of unwholesomeness and burned away their virtuous minds. All the members of that great assembly—devas, nāgas, spirits, humans, and non-humans—who did not previously make offerings to the Buddha, now all together make offerings to them.
Finally, the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet. Having paid homage, he rose and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke verses of praise.

Standing before the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā knelt with his right knee on the ground to hear the Buddha bestow a prophecy. Thereupon, that World-Honored One smiled. For this reason, the earth in these worlds of the ten directions—equal in number to the atoms within a single buddha-field—trembled in six ways; a great radiance was emitted, various flowers rained down, and all bodhisattvas were awakened, while the path of the bodhisattvas was likewise revealed.

That Buddha, the World-Honored One, caused all the assemblies of bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions—equal in number to the atoms within a single buddha-field—to gather together. For the sake of such great bodhisattvas as these, he expounded various gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, as well as the Dharma-gates of fearlessness; it is for this reason that that Buddha manifested such various transformations.
“Good son! At that time, having heard these words, the two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
Since this Great Compassionate Bodhisattva first resolved his mind [on enlightenment], how long has he practiced the bodhisattva path?
Until what point will it continue?

And at what time will he, within the five turbidities of this evil world, tame and gather in those sentient beings who possess heavy and dense afflictions, who engage in mutual strife and contention, who frequently commit the five heinous crimes, who have perfected all roots of non-virtue, and whose virtuous minds have been incinerated?
At that time, the Buddha said to the two bodhisattvas:
"Sons of good family!
This Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā has today for the first time resolved his mind toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

"Good son! You should now go to see the Buddha Ratnagarbha, to make offerings to him, revere him, prostrate before him, and circumambulate him. Listen to such sūtras as the *Samādhi-dhāraṇī-mukha* and the *Abhaya-dharma-mukha*. Furthermore, you shall see the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika, and on my behalf, speak these words:
'Buddha Puṣpadhvajarāja sends his greetings and inquires after your well-being; he gives you this Moonlight Pure Flower as a token of his trust.'"
Furthermore, they praised you, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"

"Good son! From the moment you first resolved your mind [on enlightenment], you were already able to accomplish such great compassion. Now, immeasurable fame has spread throughout the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a single Buddha-field, all saying:
'The Bodhisattva of Great Compassion, from his very first resolution, was already able to accomplish such great compassion.'"
"Therefore, son of good family!
I now praise you; excellent, excellent!"
Furthermore, son of good family!

For the sake of enabling future bodhisattvas to achieve great compassion, you have spoken of this uninterrupted great compassion and its virtuous vows, thereby erecting the banner of the Dharma; for this reason, I again praise you, saying: "Excellent!"
Excellent! Furthermore, son of good family,
your name shall endure in future ages, equal in number to the atoms within as many buddha-fields as there are asaṃkhyeyas.
Throughout *kalpas* as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, he taught hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings,
establishing them securely in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* until they attained the stage of non-retrogression upon reaching Buddhahood;
or else they made virtuous vows, or took up pure lands, gathering in sentient beings and taming them according to their aspirations.
Furthermore, may they be granted the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the future; thus,
after as many eons as there are atoms in a single Buddha-field have passed in a future age,
these sentient beings shall attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within as many worlds throughout the ten directions as there are atoms in a single Buddha-field.
Having turned the wheel of the true Dharma through *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, I shall further praise you.
Therefore, with these three modes of praise, I extol you: "Excellent!"
"Excellent! "Good son!
At that time, there were immeasurable billions of bodhisattvas in that land who, with one voice and in unison, spoke these words:"
“World-Honored One!

We wish to go to the realm of Santirana to see the Buddha Ratnagarbha, to pay homage, make offerings, show respect, and circumambulate him; we wish to hear the various gates of samādhi and dhāraṇī, as well as the gates of the dharma of fearlessness, and we also wish to see the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika.”
At that time, the Buddha, with these three methods of praise and the pure moonlight flower, addressed the two bodhisattvas, saying:
"You should know that now is the time."

Then those two bodhisattvas, together with an assembly of immeasurable billions of bodhisattvas, took these precious flowers from that Buddha’s presence; in the space of a single thought-moment, they vanished from that world and suddenly arrived within the Jambūvana grove in the realm of Santirana, where they beheld the Buddha Ratnagarbha and prostrated themselves before him in homage.

At that time, there were in that world immeasurable and incalculable numbers of great bodhisattvas who practiced the Mahāyāna, as well as those who had set their minds on the vehicles of the pratyekabuddhas and śrāvakas, along with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, mahoragas, and other such beings. They were as numerous as the sugarcane, bamboo, reeds, rice, hemp, and forests covering the entire land, and they honored the Buddha with various kinds of lion-like playful displays (siṃhavikrīḍita) attained by these bodhisattvas.

Having made offerings to the Buddha, he saw that the brahmin Ratnasāgara was being honored by this great assembly, who joined their palms and praised him. Having witnessed this, he immediately reflected:
"This Great Being must surely be a Bodhisattva of Great Compassion; it is for this reason that the Tathāgata Puṣpadantādityarāja has sent these precious flowers."
These two bodhisattvas, turning back toward the brahmin before the Buddha, immediately gave him the flowers and spoke these words:
"The Tathāgata Puṣpadantādityarāja gives you these exquisite flowers as a token of faith, along with the three praises of the Dharma as previously described."

“Good son! At that time, the various kinds of flowers that rained down also reached worlds where no Buddha was present, and they further produced all manner of wondrous and virtuous sounds. These sounds filled everywhere, namely: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Bhikṣu-saṃgha, the sound of cessation, the sound of non-existence, the sound of the various pāramitās, the sound of the powers and fearlessnesses, the sound of the six supernormal knowledges, the sound of non-action, the sound of neither arising nor ceasing, the sound of tranquility, the sound of great kindness, the sound of great compassion, the sound of the patience of non-arising, the sound of receiving predictions, and the sound of preaching the Mahāyāna.”

In that world there was a bodhisattva who, by virtue of his original vow, possessed great supernormal power; having cultivated profound dharmas, he had attained mastery. For the sake of sentient beings, he resided in that world, and upon hearing this sound, through the power of the Buddha, the power of his vows, and the power of samādhi, he traveled from that world by means of his supernormal powers. In the time it takes a strong man to bend and extend his arm, he arrived at the presence of the Buddha Ratnagarbha in the Jambūvana Grove of the land of Saṃtīrṇa. Bowing his head to the Buddha’s feet, he made offerings to the Buddha and the great assembly with various kinds of "lion-play" displays attained by bodhisattvas, and sat down in order to listen to and receive the sublime Dharma.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara, having taken these Moonlight-Pure Flowers and offered them to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!...’”
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will grant me the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha entered into a samādhi called 'Lightning Lamp.'"
By the power of samādhi, he caused all the mountains, trees, grasses, shrubs, and soil of the Cāmaras realm to transform into the seven treasures.
He enabled the entire great assembly to see this for themselves, and they all listened to and received the sublime Dharma before the Buddha;
according to their reflections, some saw their own bodies as blue, yellow, or white.

...purple, red, or black; or appearing like wind, or appearing like fire, or appearing like space, or appearing like a mirage in the heat, or appearing like water, or like water bubbles, or like a great mountain, or like Brahmā, or like Śakra; or one sees...
Some resemble flowers, or resemble garuḍas; some see themselves resembling dragons, or lions, or the sun and moon, or the lunar mansions;

others see themselves resembling elephants or wild foxes, sitting before the Buddha to listen to and receive the sublime Dharma, reflecting upon it according to the occasion, each seeing their own body in this way.
Regarding their physical appearance: "Good son!

Thus, according to what these sentient beings contemplate, they again see themselves as being identical to the body of the Buddha Ratnagarbha, without any distinction. While this great assembly is before the Buddha, they immediately see the brahmin sitting upon a thousand-petaled lotus flower made of the seven treasures. Whether the entire great assembly is on the ground or in the air, whether sitting or standing, each and every sentient being sees the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha sitting alone before them, preaching the Dharma to them alone, thinking: 'I alone am seeing him.'"
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha praised the brahmin Ratnasāgara, saying: ‘Excellent!’”

Excellent! O Great Compassionate One of Pure Conduct, for the sake of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, you have given rise to this great compassion; it is able to bring great benefit and acts as a great light within the world.

Brahmin! It is like a perfected flower field, possessing various colors, various fragrances, various textures, various leaves, various stalks, various roots, and various virtues; everything required for medicinal herbs is fully present therein.

There are some lotus flowers that span a full hundred thousand yojanas, with radiance and exquisite fragrance equal to the size of the flower itself; some are one hundred yojanas in length and breadth, some two hundred, and some three hundred yojanas, with radiance and exquisite fragrance likewise equal to the flower; there are even flowers as large as an entire world-system, with radiance and exquisite fragrance equally matchless and without distinction.

Among the various classes of sentient beings, there may be those who are blind; upon smelling this flower fragrance, they immediately regain the ability to see forms. Those who are deaf hear sounds, and even all those with impaired faculties immediately attain their full restoration.
If there are sentient beings suffering from the four hundred and four ailments, when these afflictions arise, upon hearing the fragrance of this flower, their illnesses will be immediately cured.
If there are those who are deranged, dissolute, insane, drowsy, mentally distracted, or have lost mindfulness, upon hearing the fragrance of this flower, they shall all attain single-mindedness.

Within these flower fields, there also grow *puṇḍarīka* flowers. These flowers are as firm and solid as diamond; their stalks are made of lapis lazuli, their calyxes have a hundred buds, their petals are of pure gold, their anthers are of agate, and their filaments are of red pearls. These flowers are eighty-four billion *yojana*s in height, with a circumference and breadth of one hundred thousand *yojana*s. Their color, fragrance, and tactile qualities pervade the ten directions throughout as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms in a single Buddha-field.

Among those sentient beings, there were some whose four great elements were out of harmony, who were afflicted by severe illnesses, whose faculties were weakened and impaired, or who were deranged, dissolute, insane, dazed, drowsy, mentally distracted, or forgetful; upon seeing the radiance of the flowers and smelling their fragrance, all their ailments were individually cured, and they all attained single-mindedness.

If those sentient beings have just passed away and their bodies have not yet decayed, when the light touches them and the fragrance permeates them, they immediately regain their life-faculty and arise as before, wandering together with their kinsmen through gardens and groves, enjoying themselves with the five sensory pleasures.
If he were to inevitably reach the end of his life, he would not be reborn elsewhere, but would be born in the Brahma Heaven, dwelling there for a long time with an immeasurable lifespan. O Brahmin!

This lotus field is none other than this great assembly; it is like the rising of the sun causing all flowers to bloom, and like the appearance of the Buddha-sun, which increases and nurtures wondrous fragrances and radiance to sever the sufferings of all sentient beings.

“Good son! I am now like the sun appearing in the world, causing the flowers of the roots of goodness in all sentient beings to bloom, with subtle and wondrous fragrances and radiance shining everywhere, able to eliminate the various illnesses of sentient beings. This is the Tathāgata’s appearance in the world, whereby the radiance of great compassion covers all things, causing the roots of goodness in all sentient beings to open and flourish, increasing their merit and establishing them securely in the three bases of happiness.”
"O son of good family!

As for the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable number of sentient beings whom you have transformed and established in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, those who have come to me—each of these sentient beings has individually made various kinds of virtuous vows to take up a Buddha-world, whether pure or impure; I have accordingly bestowed upon them their predictions of enlightenment."

"Good son! If there is a bodhisattva who, standing before me, vows to take up a pure land, and with a pure mind, having well-disciplined himself, plants various roots of goodness to gather in sentient beings—even such a one is called a bodhisattva, yet he is not a valiant and heroic great man, nor does he possess the profound and weighty great compassion of a bodhisattva."

For the sake of sentient beings, one seeks *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. If there is anyone who grasps at a pure Buddha-field, that person is a bodhisattva who has abandoned great compassion; furthermore, if they do not wish for the two vehicles to be intermingled, such a bodhisattva lacks skillful means and wisdom, and does not possess a mind of true equanimity.

If there is a bodhisattva who makes this vow: “May my world be far removed from the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; may the unwholesome roots be extinguished, and may there be no women nor the three evil realms. Having attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, may I have as my great retinue exclusively bodhisattvas mahāsattvas and the like; may I preach exclusively the unsurpassed Mahāyāna Dharma; may my lifespan be immeasurable, and may I abide long in the world for incalculable kalpas, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma solely for those whose minds are well-tamed by goodness, who are pure, and who have perfected their wholesome roots.”
Such a person, though called a bodhisattva, is not a mahāsattva.
Why is this? Because they lack skillful means and the wisdom of equality.
“Good son!

At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha extended his golden arm, and from the tips of his five fingers he emitted a great radiance. This light, possessing hundreds of thousands of various and immeasurable colors, shone throughout the western direction, passing beyond immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) worlds. There was a world named Mahāṅguṣṭha; the people of that land had a lifespan of thirty years, their complexions were ugly and their appearances loathsome, and they were possessed of all roots of unwholesomeness. They were six feet tall. In that land there was a Buddha named Mahāprabha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, who currently resides there, preaching the Dharma of the Three Vehicles to the fourfold assembly.
"Good son! At that time, the great assembly was all able to see from afar that Buddha, the World-Honored One, and his multitude.
Then, the Buddha Ratnagarbha addressed the great assembly:"

That Buddha Mahāprabha, in the past, during immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, first resolved his mind toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the presence of the Buddha Ratnacchatraprabha.

At that time, he also exhorted immeasurable, boundless billions of nayutas of sentient beings to settle securely in the unsurpassed path, causing them to take up various adorned worlds according to their own aspirations—whether pure or impure, or even the five-turbid evil world.
That Great Radiance Buddha also exhorted me to resolve my mind and dwell securely in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, in the presence of the Buddha Jewel Canopy Radiance, I was inspired by his exhortation and made a vow to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in this world of five turbidities.
At that time, that Buddha praised me, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"
He then immediately bestowed upon me the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Because I had such a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) at that time, he exhorted me toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. That spiritual friend, a supreme and wondrous man, took up this heavy and evil world of the five turbidities—a land of impurity with manifold afflictions—where all sentient beings practice perversity and even cultivate various unwholesome roots, burning away their virtuous minds and wandering through the vast wilderness of birth and death; it was there that he resolved to tame such sentient beings.

At that time, all the Buddhas throughout the infinite and boundless Buddha-worlds of the ten directions each dispatched a messenger to this good man’s location to proclaim his praises, and they conferred upon him the title "Great Compassionate One, Radiance of the Sun and Moon."

That Great Compassionate One, the Radiance of Sun and Moon, is my very own spiritual friend; he has brought great benefit and, not long after attaining Buddhahood in the world of Mahāṅguli, has turned the wheel of the True Dharma for the sake of these short-lived and evil people.

When that Buddha first attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the Buddhas of the ten directions, immeasurable and boundless in number, each dispatched messengers to the place where that Buddha was, in order to offer him worship, reverence, respect, and praise.

All these World-Honored Ones were originally exhorted and transformed by the Buddha Great Radiance, who first caused them to dwell securely in the *dānapāramitā*, and so on, up to the *prajñāpāramitā*.
"These World-Honored Ones, out of gratitude, have dispatched these bodhisattvas to present this offering.
'O Brahmin! Do you see now?'"

Each of these World-Honored Ones dwells in their respective pure worlds; their lifespans are immeasurable, and they perform the buddha-work solely for those who possess virtuous minds, are disciplined, pure, and have perfected their roots of goodness.

This Great Radiance Buddha, dwelling in this defiled and impure world, the evil age of the five turbidities, has attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Among all sentient beings there, many commit the grave offenses of immediate retribution and even cultivate various unwholesome roots; their lifespans are short. Yet, within such a place, he increases their longevity and performs immeasurable Buddha-works. Without abandoning the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, he preaches the Dharma of the three vehicles for the sake of all sentient beings.

"You are a great man, beyond the reach of all this assembly. What you have accomplished is most excellent and exceedingly difficult: you have vowed to take up an impure land in an age of the five turbidities, where many commit acts of rebellion and even cultivate all manner of unwholesome roots, yet you have tamed and gathered such sentient beings."

"Good son! If there is a bodhisattva who takes up a pure buddha-field, free from the three evil realms as well as śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and gathers and subdues those sentient beings whose minds are virtuous, pure, and who have accomplished roots of goodness—this is called a 'bodhisattva like other flowers. This is not what is meant by a 'great bodhisattva' like the *puṇḍarīka* flower, because [the latter] subdues sentient beings with a virtuous mind, plants all roots of goodness, and performs the work of a Buddha."
“Brahmin! Listen now to the four dharmas of indolence in a bodhisattva.
What are the four?
First, the vow to take up a pure world;
second, the vow to perform buddha-work among a community of beings who are well-tamed and pure through their virtuous minds;
third, the vow that after attaining buddhahood, one shall not preach the teachings of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Fourth, the aspiration that after attaining Buddhahood one’s lifespan shall be immeasurable.
These are called the four dharmas of indolence in a bodhisattva; such a bodhisattva is said to be like other flowers, not like the *puṇḍarīka*.

“Brahmin! In this great assembly, with the sole exception of one person, Pāyāsi, who takes up an impure world to discipline and protect those with many afflictions, there may be some bodhisattvas within this Bhadrakalpa who likewise take up impure lands.”
“Brahmin! There are four qualities of diligence for a bodhisattva.
What are the four?
First, the vow to take up impure worlds;
second, to perform the work of a Buddha among impure people;
third, after attaining Buddhahood, to preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
Fourth, having attained Buddhahood, one obtains a moderate lifespan that is neither too long nor too short.
These are called the four dharmas of bodhisattva diligence; this is what is meant by a bodhisattva being like a *puṇḍarīka* lotus and not like other flowers. This is called a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

“Brahmin! Now, within this flower-field of an immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) assembly of bodhisattvas, you have made your vow and received your prediction. Because you have already produced the great compassion *puṇḍarīka* in the presence of the Buddha, you shall gather those who commit many transgressions and achieve [the salvation of] all those with unwholesome roots in the evil world of the five turbidities (*pañca-kaṣāya*), and therein tame them according to their needs.”

Because of your voice of great compassion, you have been able to cause the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, throughout the ten directions—as numerous as the atoms within a single Buddha-field—to dispatch messengers to praise you. Having praised you, they have designated you as "One Who Has Accomplished Great Compassion," and have further caused this great assembly to make offerings to you.

Furthermore, Great Compassionate One, in a future age, after one *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed, during the latter part of a second *asaṃkhyeya* kalpa equal to the sands of the Ganges, in the Sahā world during the Bhadrakalpa when the human lifespan is one hundred and twenty years, beings will be bound by old age, illness, and death. In this dark age, they will have no teacher to consult; they will accumulate all roots of unwholesomeness, practice false paths, enter the river of afflictions, and be solely intent on committing the five heinous crimes. They will destroy the True Dharma, slander the sages, violate the four grave prohibitions, and so forth, as described above.

In such an era of afflictions and turmoil, you shall become a Buddha, a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, a Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, a Sugata, a Lokavid, an Anuttara, a Puruṣadamyasārathi, a Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, a Buddha, and a Bhagavān; you shall leave the wheel of birth and death behind, turn the true Wheel of Dharma, and destroy the four Māras.

At that time, you shall possess great renown, filling the immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions. You shall have an assembly of twelve hundred and fifty śrāvakas, and over the course of forty-five years, you shall accomplish such immeasurable Buddha-works as you have vowed, fulfilling them completely and without deficiency.

When this King Immeasurable Purity attains Buddhahood, his lifespan shall be immeasurable; even throughout immeasurable and boundless kalpas, he will likewise be able to accomplish such Buddha-works, equal and without distinction.
"O virtuous man!

After your parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full thousand years. Once the True Dharma has vanished, your various relics shall perform the work of a Buddha according to your vows, remaining in the world for a long time to benefit sentient beings, as previously described."
“Good son! At that time, there was a brahmin in the assembly named Lakṣaṇasampanna, who spoke these words: ‘O Great Being!’”

If, in future ages throughout immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, while you are a bodhisattva, in whatever place you may be born, I shall always serve as your attendant; with a heart of constant compassion, I will provide all that you require, and until the time of your final birth, I shall further become your father.
"When you have attained Buddhahood, you shall become a great donor; you must also grant me the prediction of unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, there was a sea deity named Tiao-yi (Subduing Mind) who spoke again, saying: "O Great Being!..."
From this day forward, in every place throughout my entire life, may I always be your mother.
Once you have attained Buddhahood, you shall also grant me the prediction of unsurpassed enlightenment.
At that time, a water deity spoke again, saying:
"From this day forward, wherever you may be, even for the duration of a single lifetime, I vow to always serve as your wet nurse."
"When you have attained Buddhahood, you should likewise bestow upon me the prediction of unsurpassed enlightenment.
Two Śakras were there—one named Sunetra and the other named Ratnamati—who further spoke these words: "O Great Being!..."
"Once you have attained Buddhahood, we shall become your śrāvaka disciples, endowed with wisdom and supernormal powers.
Furthermore, there was a Śakra named Sudarśanapāda who spoke these words:
"O Great Compassionate One!..."
"From this day forward, wherever you may be, until the end of this life, I shall always be your son.
Then the Sumeru spirit named Sukhapuṣpa spoke again: "O Great Compassionate One!..."
"From this life until the end of my existence, I shall always be your wife.
Once you have attained the Way of the Buddha, you must also grant me the prediction of unsurpassed enlightenment.
Furthermore, there was an asura king named Vakṣa-cara who spoke these words:

"O Mahākāruṇika! Throughout immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas while you were practicing as a bodhisattva, and even until your final birth—during all that time—I shall serve as your servant and attendant, providing for all your needs."

Once you have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and turned the wheel of the true Dharma, I shall first understand the Dharma, attain the fruit of reality, partake of the flavor of the nectar of immortality, and even reach the severance of all afflictions to become an arhat.

“At that time, there were again gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, humans, non-humans, and others, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, who made this vow toward the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika: ‘O Great Being!’”
"You must surely tame and transform us.
At that time, there was a naked ascetic brahmin named Vikṣiptamati-bhairava who spoke again, saying: "O Great Man!

While you practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, I shall follow after you and seek from you whatever you require; I will constantly go to your presence to beg for clothing, beds, bedding, dwellings, houses, elephants, horses, carriages, kingdoms, cities, wives, children, head, eyes, marrow, brain, skin, flesh, hands, feet, ears, nose, tongue, and body.
"O virtuous great man!
I shall act as a supportive cause for you, enabling you to fulfill the dānapāramitā, up to and including the prajñāpāramitā."
"O Great Compassionate Brahmin, when you practice the Bodhisattva path in such ways as these, I shall exhort you so that you may fully perfect the six pāramitās.

Once you have attained Buddhahood, I pray to become your disciple; I shall hear from you the eighty thousand aggregates of Dharma, and having heard them, I shall immediately be able to discern and explain their characteristics. Having explained these characteristics, you shall then grant me the prediction of unsurpassed enlightenment."
“Good son! At that time, having heard these words, the brahmin immediately prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the naked ascetic brahmin, saying: ‘Excellent!’”

Excellent! You are truly my peerless companion on the path. For immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, you have constantly come to me to beg for whatever you required—be it clothing, or even my tongue and body. At those times, with a pure mind, I gave away all that I possessed as alms to you; yet at those times, you incurred no share of transgression.
“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā again spoke these words:
‘World-Honored One!’”

Throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, in every place where I was born as a bodhisattva, there were beggars who stood before me—whether they sought food and drink, or used gentle words, or harsh speech, or spoke with contempt and derision, or spoke the truth.
World-Honored One!
At that time, I did not give rise to even a single thought of an evil mind.

If I had given rise to anger for even as long as a finger-snap, seeking a future reward through the causes and conditions of giving, I would have been deceiving the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently dwelling in the worlds of the ten directions; furthermore, in future ages, I would certainly not have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“World-Honored One!

I shall now, with a heart of joy, bestow gifts upon those who beg. I vow that the recipients shall suffer no harm nor gain any benefit [from me], and that there shall be no hindrance to their roots of goodness, even for so much as a single hair’s breadth. If I were to cause even a hair’s breadth of harm or benefit to those recipients, or any hindrance to their roots of goodness, I would then be deceiving the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently dwelling throughout the worlds of the ten directions. If I were to deceive these Buddhas, I would surely fall into the Avīci Hell and would be unable to joyfully give away clothing, food, or drink.”
If those beggars should seek such things as his head, eyes, marrow, and brain, whether using gentle words, harsh speech, insults and disparagement, or even truthful statements.
World-Honored One!

If at that time my heart were not joyful, or if I were to give rise to even a single thought of anger, seeking a karmic reward on account of this gift, I would be deceiving the immeasurable and boundless Buddhas currently residing throughout the worlds of the ten directions; by reason of this, I would certainly fall into the Avīci Hell.
"As it was taught regarding the dāna-pāramitā, so it is for each up to the prajñā-pāramitā.
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha immediately praised the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara:"
"Excellent! Excellent!
It is well that you have been able to establish a mind of great compassion and thus make such a vow."
"Good son! At that time, the entire great assembly—devas, nāgas, spirits, humans, and non-humans—joined their palms and praised him, saying: 'Excellent!'"

Excellent! Because you are well able to settle in the mind of great compassion, you have made this vow and attained great renown; you steadfastly practice the six dharmas of harmony, bringing abundant benefit to all sentient beings.
“Good son! When the naked Brahmin made his vow, there were also eighty-four thousand people who likewise made the same vow as the Brahmin.”

“Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā, together with these eighty-four thousand people, made a vow and their hearts were filled with joy. Joining his palms and looking around at the great assembly, he spoke these words:
‘It is unprecedented!’”

In future ages, at the time when the True Dharma is extinguished, amidst the many afflictions of the five turbidities and evil worlds, I shall emit great radiance therein and act as a Teacher who Tames, kindling the lamp of the True Dharma in this world of darkness.

If there are sentient beings who have no protector, no power, and no Buddha to guide them, at the very moment I first resolve upon Bodhicitta, I have already obtained such supreme companions for the Path. May these people follow me from lifetime to lifetime, and may they receive from me their heads, eyes, marrow, brains, skin, flesh, bones, blood, hands, feet, ears, noses, tongues, bodies, and even their clothing and food.
“Good son! At that time, the brahmacārin Ratnasāgara addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”

If, in future ages, throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of asaṃkhyeya kalpas, such sentient beings come to me and receive from me gifts of my head, eyes, marrow, and brain, even down to as much as a single hair’s breadth of food and drink, yet after I have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they are not liberated from birth and death and do not receive the prediction of the three vehicles, then I would be deceiving the immeasurable and boundless Buddhas currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions, and I shall certainly not attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha again praised the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā: ‘Excellent!’”
Excellent! Excellent, O Great Being!

That you are able to practice the bodhisattva path in this way is like the Bodhisattva Sumerugarbharatna in the past, who before the Buddha Lokaprabhāsa first gave rise to such a mind of enlightenment, made this vow, and likewise practiced the bodhisattva path for as many incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River.

To the east, beyond hundreds of thousands of billions of Buddha-worlds, there is a world named Radiant Blazing Wisdom. There, the human lifespan is one hundred years, and he attained Buddhahood therein, being known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Jñānakusuma-vimala-dṛḍha-bodhi-rāja. He remained in the world preaching the Dharma for forty-five years, performing the work of a Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā:

"After that Buddha enters parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full thousand years; once the True Dharma has ceased, the Semblance Dharma shall likewise remain in the world for a thousand years."
O Great Compassionate One!

Whether that Buddha, the World-Honored One, remains in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa, during the interval between the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma, there will be bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs who act contrary to the Dharma and violate the precepts, following deviant paths. They will sever the offerings to the Dharma, lacking shame and remorse; they may misappropriate the property of the Saṃgha of the Four Quarters, or seize the robes, food, drink, bedding, and medicine belonging to the present Saṃgha. Taking the property of the Saṃgha as their own, they will use it for themselves, give it to others, or bestow it upon householders.
"Good son! Such persons as these, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, has bestowed upon all of them the prediction of enlightenment within the Three Vehicles.
O Great Compassionate One!"

In that Tathāgata’s presence, if there are those who have left the household life and donned the *kāṣāya*, they shall all receive the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) that they will not regress from the three vehicles (*triyāna*).

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who have committed the four grave prohibitions (*caturmahāpatti*), that Buddha regards them as the World-Honored One; because they have planted various roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*), he likewise grants them the prediction that they will not regress from the three vehicles.
"Good son! At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā again spoke these words:
'World-Honored One!'"

Regarding the vow I now make: while practicing the bodhisattva path, if there are sentient beings whom I must exhort and transform so that they are established in the *dānapāramitā*, up to and including the *prajñāpāramitā*; or even if I exhort them to establish them in roots of goodness as small as a single hair-tip, up to their attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—if I do not so establish them, or if I cause even a single sentient being to regress from the Three Vehicles, then I would be deceiving the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently residing throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and I shall certainly not attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

After I have attained Buddhahood, if there are sentient beings who enter my Dharma and leave the household life to don the *kāṣāya*, even if they violate the grave precepts, practice wrong views, or harbor contempt and lack faith toward the Triple Gem—accumulating various heavy offenses—whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—if for even a single thought-moment they give rise to a mind of reverence and respect for the World-Honored One, or for the Dharma and the Saṃgha...”
World-Honored One!

If even a single such sentient being were to regress without receiving the prediction of enlightenment within the Three Vehicles, they would be deceiving the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently residing throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and they would certainly never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“World-Honored One!

Once I have attained Buddhahood, if any gods, nāgas, spirits, humans, or non-humans can respectfully revere, make offerings to, honor, and praise those who wear this kashaya robe, and if such persons should even see a small portion of this robe, they shall immediately attain non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles.”

If there are sentient beings oppressed by hunger and thirst—whether they be impoverished spirits, those of lowly birth, or even hungry ghosts—if they obtain even a small portion of this *kāṣāya*, as little as four inches, they shall immediately obtain sufficient food and drink, and their wishes shall be swiftly fulfilled according to their desires.

If there are sentient beings who oppose one another, giving rise to thoughts of enmity and banditry, engaging in mutual strife and contention—whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, humans, or non-humans—and when they are thus contending together, if they bring this *kāṣāya* robe to mind, they will immediately give rise to a heart of compassion, a gentle heart, a heart free from enmity and banditry, a heart of quiescence, and a well-disciplined, virtuous heart.

If there are those who find themselves amidst the fray of weapons, combat, litigation, or judicial proceedings, and they take even a small portion of this *kāṣāya* robe into the midst of such people for their own protection—honoring, revering, and respecting it—then none among these people will be able to invade, destroy, harass, or mock them; they shall always prevail over others and overcome these various difficulties.
World-Honored One!

If my *kāṣāya* cannot accomplish these five kinds of noble merits, then I would be deceiving the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Buddhas currently residing throughout the worlds of the ten directions; I shall not attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the future to perform the Buddha-work, I shall lose the wholesome Dharma, and I will certainly be unable to destroy the followers of external paths.
“Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha extended his golden right arm, rubbed the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika, and praised him, saying: ‘Excellent!’”
Excellent! Great man! What you have spoken is a great treasure; it is most noble and virtuous.
Once you have attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, this monastic robe will be able to accomplish these five noble merits and bring about great benefit.

"Good son! At that time, having heard the Buddha’s praise, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahākaruṇā felt great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight. Because the Buddha extended this golden arm—with long fingers joined by webbing and hands as soft as celestial raiment—and stroked his head, his body immediately transformed, appearing like a youth of twenty years."

"Good son! The great assembly in that gathering—gods, nāgas, spirits, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans—joined their palms in reverence toward the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika, making offerings by scattering various flowers and even providing musical performances as an act of worship."
He further offered various kinds of praise; having finished praising, he remained silent. Chapter Five:
The Perfection of Giving (Dānapāramitā), Part One. "O son of good family! The Sutra of the Compassionate Lotus, Chapter Five: The Perfection of Giving, Part One. "O son of good family!"

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika prostrated with his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha; having paid homage to the Buddha’s feet, he stood before the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Regarding what is called the *Sūtra on the Gateways of All Samādhis, the Aids to the Dharma for Awakening, and the Gateways of Purification*, to what extent does it refer to the *Sūtra on the Gateways of All Samādhis, the Aids to the Dharma for Awakening, and the Gateways of Purification*?
"How does a bodhisattva become fully endowed with the armor of fearlessness through patience? "Good son!
At that time, that Buddha praised the Bodhisattva Mahākaruṇā, saying:"
"Excellent! Excellent! O Great Compassionate One!"
The question you have now asked is most extraordinary and sublime; it is itself a precious jewel, capable of bringing great benefit to immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas. Why is this so?
O Great Compassionate One!
You are able to ask the Buddha about such a great matter.
O Great Compassionate One!
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
If there are sons or daughters of good family who practice the Mahāyāna and possess the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, by entering this samādhi they are able to enter into all other samādhis.
There is the Ratnamudrā-samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to seal all samādhis.
There is the Siṃhavikrīḍita-samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to perform the lion’s play among all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of the Good Moon; entering this samādhi, one is able to illumine all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of the Banner Mark; entering this samādhi, one is able to uphold the banners of all samādhis.
There is the samādhi called "Emergence from the Nature of All Dharmas"; entering this samādhi, one is able to emerge from all samādhis.
There is the samādhi called "Contemplation of the Seal"; entering this samādhi, one is able to contemplate the summit of all samādhis.
There is the samādhi called "Detached from the Dharma-realm"; entering this samādhi, one is able to discern all samādhis.
There is the samādhi called "Detached from the Banner-Mark"; entering this samādhi, one is able to uphold the banners of all samādhis.
There is the Vajra Samādhi; entering this samādhi enables one to make all samādhis indestructible.
There is the Dharmamudrā Samādhi; entering this samādhi enables one to seal all dharmas.
There is the Samādhirāja-sustained samādhi; entering this samādhi, one dwells securely among all samādhis like a king.
There is the Radiating Light samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to emit light that illuminates all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of powerful progress; entering this samādhi, one attains sovereign advancement among all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of correct emergence; entering this samādhi, one is able to correctly emerge from all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of eloquent speech; entering this samādhi, one fully understands all immeasurable sounds.
There is the samādhi of language; entering this samādhi, one is able to enter into all forms of language.
There is the samādhi of observing directions; entering this samādhi, one is able to universally observe the directions of all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of all dharmas; entering this samādhi, one is able to shatter all dharmas.
There is the samādhi of Holding the Seal; entering this samādhi, one holds the seals of all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of Entering the Quiescence of All Dharmas; entering this samādhi, one causes all samādhis to enter into quiescence.
There is the samādhi of non-forgetting; entering this samādhi, one does not forget any samādhi.
There is the samādhi of the immovability of all dharmas; entering this samādhi, one causes all samādhis to become immovable.
There is the Samādhi of Approaching the Ocean-Seal of All Dharmas; entering this samādhi, one gathers and approaches all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Universal Selflessness; entering this samādhi, one causes all samādhis to be without arising or cessation.
There is the samādhi called "Pervading the Void"; entering this samādhi, one pervades all samādhis.
There is the samādhi called "Non-interruption of All Dharmas"; entering this samādhi, one sustains all samādhis so that they are never severed.
There is the Vajramaṇḍala Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to purify the maṇḍalas of all samādhis.
There is the Sarvadharmānekarasa Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to maintain the single flavor of all dharmas.
There is the samādhi of detachment from the craving for pleasure; entering this samādhi, one is detached from all afflictions and secondary afflictions.
There is the samādhi of the non-arising of all phenomena; entering this samādhi, one demonstrates that all samādhis are without arising and without cessation.
There is the Samādhi of Radiance; entering this samādhi, one is able to illuminate all samādhis, causing them to blaze with brilliance.
There is the Samādhi of the Non-extinction of All Dharmas; entering this samādhi, one does not seek even a single analytical samādhi.
There is the samādhi of non-seeking; entering this samādhi, one does not seek any phenomena.
There is the samādhi of non-abiding; entering this samādhi, one does not abide in the dharma-realm among all phenomena.
There is the *ākāśa-saṃjñā-samādhi*; entering this samādhi, one causes all samādhis to become like space and perceives their true reality. There is the *acitta-samādhi*;
entering this samādhi, one is able to extinguish the mind and its mental factors (*citta-caitasika-dharma*) within all samādhis.
There is the formless infinite samādhi; entering this samādhi, one possesses the infinite radiance of form within all samādhis.
There is the pure lamp samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to act as a lamp and light within all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of the boundlessness of all dharmas; entering this samādhi, one is able to manifest immeasurable wisdom within all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of the boundlessness of lightning; entering this samādhi, one manifests wisdom within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of All Radiance; entering this samādhi, one manifests the radiance of the gates of samādhi within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of the Boundlessness of All Realms; entering this samādhi, one manifests immeasurable and boundless wisdom within all samādhis.
There is the pure and firm samādhi; entering this samādhi, one attains the concentration on emptiness within all samādhis.
There is the Sumeru-emptiness samādhi; entering this samādhi, one manifests space within all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of stainless radiance; entering this samādhi, one removes all defilements from among all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of fearlessness regarding all dharmas; entering this samādhi, one manifests fearlessness within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Joyful Joy; entering this samādhi, one attains joyful joy within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Right Play in All Dharmas; entering this samādhi, one manifests that no forms whatsoever exist within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Emitting Radiant Light; entering this samādhi, one manifests the emission of light within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of the Stainless Abiding in All Dharmas; entering this samādhi, one manifests stainless wisdom within all samādhis.
There is the inexhaustible samādhi; entering this samādhi, one manifests within all samādhis that they are neither exhausted nor inexhaustible.
There is the inconceivable purity of all dharmas samādhi; entering this samādhi, one manifests within all samādhis as being inconceivable, like reflections in a mirror.
There is the Samādhi of Great Radiance; entering this samādhi, one causes wisdom to blaze forth within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Transcending Exhaustion; entering this samādhi, one manifests inexhaustibility within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Immovability; entering this samādhi, one remains unmoved among all phenomena, does not grasp at them, and is free from frivolity.
There is the Samādhi of Augmentation; entering this samādhi, one perceives the augmentation of all samādhis.
There is the Sun-Lamp Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one emits the gate of radiant light upon all samādhis.
There is the Moon-Stainless Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one produces the moonlight within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Pure White Radiance; entering this samādhi, one attains four kinds of eloquence regarding all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Action and Non-action; entering this samādhi, one manifests the marks of knowledge regarding what is done and what is not done among all samādhis.
There is the Vajra Samādhi; by entering this samādhi, one attains complete penetration of all dharmas, such that not even an obstacle as small as a mote of dust is perceived.

There is the samādhi of abiding mind; entering this samādhi, one’s mind is unmoving, neither experiencing suffering nor pleasure, not perceiving light, and free from anger. Within this state of mind, one likewise does not perceive that "this is the thought of mind."
There is the Samādhi of Universal Illumination; entering this samādhi, one perceives all light within all samādhis.
There is the Samādhi of Skillful Abiding; entering this samādhi, one is able to abide skillfully within all samādhis.
There is the Jewel Mountain Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one sees all samādhis as being like a mountain of jewels.
There is the Supreme Dharma Seal Samādhi; entering this samādhi, one is able to seal all samādhis.
There is the samādhi of conforming to the nature of phenomena; entering this samādhi, one sees that all phenomena are entirely in accord with it.
There is the samādhi of detachment from pleasure; entering this samādhi, one attains detachment from attachment to all phenomena.
There is the samādhi called Dharma-torch; entering this samādhi, one dispels the darkness of all dharmas.
There is the samādhi called Dharma-rain; entering this samādhi, one is able to rain down the rain of Dharma upon all samādhis, thereby destroying attachment to signs.
There is the samādhi of equal speech; entering this samādhi, one obtains the eye of insight regarding all phenomena.
There is the samādhi of transcending speech; entering this samādhi, there is not even a single word among all phenomena.
There is the samādhi of severing conditions; entering this samādhi, one severs the conditions of all phenomena.
There is the samādhi of non-action; entering this samādhi, one perceives no agent among all phenomena.
There is the samādhi of pure nature; entering this samādhi, one perceives that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure.
