That Buddha was also one whom I previously exhorted to first resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, leading him to practice the *dāna-pāramitā* and so forth, up to the *prajñā-pāramitā*.
Furthermore, in the eastern direction there is the world of Wondrous Joy; therein dwells a Buddha named Akṣobhya Tathāgata.
Again, there is the Jambudvīpa world; therein dwells a Buddha named Sūryagarbha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Sukhavaśitā; therein dwells a Buddha named Sukhavaśitāghoṣaprabha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Sukhāvatī; therein dwells a Buddha named Jñānasūrya Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Victorious Merit; therein dwells a Buddha named Nāgeśvara Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Auspicious Appearance; therein dwells a Buddha named Vajrasaṃbhava Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named King of Rivers and Seas; therein dwells a Buddha named Light Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Without Attachment; therein dwells a Buddha named Sun-Treasury Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Vimalaprabhā; therein dwells a Buddha named Vaśitābhirūpa Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Girisprabhā; therein dwells a Buddha named Acintyarāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Saṃcita; in it dwells a Buddha named Mahāguṇakośa Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Puṣpābhāsa; in it dwells a Buddha named Prabhāsvaramati-lakṣaṇa Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Harmony and Blazing Prosperity; in it dwells a Buddha named Peaceful and Harmonious Sovereign Mountain King Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Good Ground; in it dwells a Buddha named Knowing the Image Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Flower Day (*Puṣpadina*), wherein resides a Buddha named Eye-Pure and Stainless Tathāgata (*Vimalanetra-viśuddha-tathāgata*). Good son!

Such are the present Buddhas in the east, as numerous as immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, who turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings. Before they had yet resolved upon unsurpassed bodhicitta, I first exhorted them to generate the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Furthermore, I guided them to the presence of the World-Honored Buddhas wherever they might be throughout the ten directions; in each place they reached, they practiced and dwelt securely in the *dāna-pāramitā*, up to and including the *prajñā-pāramitā*, thereby attaining the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, in the eastern world-realm of Supuṣpa, the Buddha Vimalaguṇaprabhāsa-rāja, his lion throne and the great earth, shook in six ways; a great radiance appeared, and various wondrous jewel lotuses rained down.
When those bodhisattvas saw this occurrence, they were struck with wonder, doubt, and amazement at such an unprecedented event. They immediately addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
For what cause and condition does the seat of the Tathāgata tremble in this manner?"
"We have never before seen such a thing.
The Buddha then addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!..."

To the west, eighty-nine billion Buddha-worlds from here, there is a land named Sahā; therein dwells a Buddha titled Śākyamuni Tathāgata, who is currently present, preaching the Dharma of original causes for the fourfold assembly.

When that Buddha, the World-Honored One, was a bodhisattva, he first exhorted and transformed me, causing me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; furthermore, he led me to the presence of various Buddhas and first caused me to practice the *dāna-pāramitā*, up to and including the *prajñā-pāramitā*.
At that time, wherever I went, I immediately received my first prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

That World-Honored Buddha, Śākyamuni, is my true and virtuous kalyāṇamitra; he is currently in the west, dwelling among the great assembly, preaching the Sūtra of Past Causes for the fourfold congregation.
"It is by the power of that Tathāgata’s supernormal feats (ṛddhi-bala) that the lion throne upon which I sit has been moved.
Sons of good family!
Who among you now can go to that Sahā world to inquire after that Buddha’s well-being and ease?"
At that time, the bodhisattvas each addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One!

The bodhisattvas of this world of Fine Flowers have all attained supernatural powers and possess mastery over the merits of all bodhisattvas. This morning, they beheld this great radiance; that light came from all the buddha-worlds and reached here. At times, the great earth shook in six ways, and various kinds of flowers rained down. Having witnessed these events, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas desire to travel by means of their supernormal powers to the Sahā world to see Śākyamuni Buddha, to make offerings, pay respect, honor, and praise him, and furthermore, to inquire about and receive the instruction on how to understand and master all dharani-doors.”
However, none of them knew in which direction Śākyamuni of the Sahā world was located.

That Buddha then extended his golden right arm and emitted various kinds of subtle and wondrous light from the tips of his five fingers; that light immediately illuminated eighty-nine billion buddha-lands, reaching as far as the Sahā world.

At that time, by means of the light, the bodhisattvas were able to see the Sahā world, which was filled to overflowing with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others; furthermore, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, filled the void of space.
Having seen this, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

I have now already seen that world and know its direction; I also see the great assembly of bodhisattvas and devas filling that land with no empty space between them. Śākyamuni Tathāgata does not look upon us as he preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma."
That Buddha addressed the bodhisattva mahāsattvas: "Good sons!
Śākyamuni Tathāgata constantly surveys all things with his pure, unsurpassed Buddha-eye; there is nothing he does not see."
"Good son! All sentient beings in the Sahā world, whether on the ground or in the air, each and every one says:
'The Tathāgata Śākyamuni alone perceives my mind and preaches the Dharma for me.'"

"Good son! That Śākyamuni Tathāgata, with a single voice, preaches the Dharma for all various and diverse classes of beings; each sentient being attains understanding according to their own kind, yet he does not preach to many people using different voices."
The sentient beings of that land may serve Brahmā; seeing the Tathāgata’s body in the form of Brahmā, they hear the Dharma.

Or they may serve Māra, Śakra, the Sun and Moon, Vaiśravaṇa, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, or Maheśvara—among these eighty-four thousand types of deities, according to whom each serves, they each see his image and hear the Dharma, giving rise to the thought that [the Buddha] is uniquely for them alone.
At that time, there were two bodhisattvas in the assembly: the first was named Rāhuvidyut and the second was named Tejaprabha.
Then, the Buddha Vimalaguṇaprabhāsa-rāja addressed the two bodhisattvas:
"O sons of good family!
"You should now go to the Sahā world and, carrying my words, inquire after the World-Honored One Śākyamuni:
'Are you light and at ease in your daily life? Is your physical strength secure and well?'"
Then the two bodhisattvas addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

We see that in all the worlds of that Buddha, great assemblies have gathered like clouds, filling and crowding both the earth and the void, such that there is not a single space left empty between them.”
"If we go there, where should we dwell?
Then the Buddha told them:
"O sons of good family!
Do not speak such words, claiming that world has no place of abode. Why is this? The place where he dwells is vast and boundless;

the immeasurable merits of that Buddha are inconceivable. By virtue of his original vows, his compassionate heart is so expansive that he causes immeasurable classes of sentient beings to enter the Buddha-dharma and receive the Three Refuges. Thereafter, he preaches the Dharma of the Three Vehicles for them, further teaches the Three Precepts, reveals the Three Gates of Liberation, and rescues immeasurable and boundless sentient beings from the three evil realms, establishing them securely within the three good realms.

"Good son! Furthermore, at another time, not long after Śākyamuni Tathāgata had attained the Unsurpassed Way, for the sake of taming all sentient beings, he stayed in the Indrasailaguha Sāla Cave on Mount Vidyutprabha. For seven days and seven nights, he sat cross-legged, entering samādhi and receiving right concentration to dwell in the bliss of liberation. At that time, the Buddha’s body pervaded the entire cave, leaving no empty space even as small as four inches."

After seven days had passed, twelve nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas from the worlds of the ten directions arrived at the edge of that mountain in the Sahā world. They came desiring to see the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, to make offerings to him, to revere, respect, and praise him, and to receive and accept his sublime Dharma.

“Good son! At that time, by means of his great supernormal power, the Tathāgata caused the cave-dwelling where he resided to become immeasurably vast and spacious, so that it could accommodate twelve nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”

Once the bodhisattvas had entered, they saw that the cave-dwelling was vast and magnificently adorned. There were bodhisattvas who, through the sovereign supernormal power of the lion’s play, made offerings to the Buddha; each bodhisattva sat upon a transformed jeweled throne to listen to the Dharma.
"Good son! Such was the manifestation of that Buddha’s supernormal power.

Having heard the Dharma, these bodhisattvas immediately rose from their seats, prostrated themselves with their heads at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and each returned to his own buddha-world."
Not long after he had departed, the cave returned to its former state.

Śakra Devānām Indra, named Kauśika—the second lord of the four continents—was nearing the end of his life and was certain to fall into the realm of animals. Because of this matter, his heart was filled with fear; together with eighty-four thousand gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, he descended and went to the Indrasāla Cave, desiring to see the Tathāgata.
At that time, there was a yakṣa named Rājākṣa, who was the guardian deity of that cave and was staying outside.
Then, by the power of the Buddha, Śakra thought to himself:

"Now I shall send the gandharva son Pañcaśikha to go first to the Buddha's dwelling, to praise and extol the Tathāgata with exquisite melodies, so as to cause the World-Honored One to arise from his samādhi."

"Good son! Having reflected thus, Śakra-devānām-indra immediately commanded the gandharva youth Pañcaśikha to play a lapis lazuli lute with a subtle and wondrous sound; that sound possessed five hundred distinct varieties as he praised the Tathāgata."

“Good son! When Pañcaśikha was thus praising the Buddha, at that time the Tathāgata again entered the Samādhi of Characteristics. By the power of this samādhi, he manifested great supernormal powers in this world, causing all the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and the devas of the desire and form realms to gather together therein.”
If there are those who delight in hearing sublime sounds, they shall hear them at will and their hearts will be filled with great joy;

or if there are those who delight in hearing praises of the Buddha, upon hearing such praise, their hearts will give rise to joy, and toward the Tathāgata, they will further conceive a mind of reverence and respect;
or if there are sentient beings who delight in hearing the sound of music, they shall immediately hear it, and having heard it, they will rejoice.
"At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni arose from his meditative concentration and showed the door of the Sāla Cave to the great assembly.
Śakra Devānām Indra immediately went to where the Buddha was, prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet, withdrew to stand to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
'World-Honored One!'"
"Where shall I sit now? Then the Buddha replied, "Kauśika!"

"Your retinue shall simply assemble; I will now expand this Śāla cave until it is exceedingly vast and wide, so that it may fully accommodate this great assembly of followers, as numerous as the sands of twelve Ganges Rivers, allowing all of them to sit."

"At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, amidst the great assembly, expounded the True Dharma with a single wondrous voice, enabling eighty-four thousand sentient beings of various faculties to hear according to what they delighted in. Among them, those who were training as śrāvakas heard the Dharma of the śrāvakas; immediately, nine hundred and ninety million sentient beings attained the fruit of srotāpanna.
Those who were training in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas immediately heard the Dharma of the pratyekabuddhas;
and those who were training in the Mahāyāna heard exclusively the Mahāyāna."
Eighteen nayutas of the assembly, headed by the gandharva son Pañcaśikha and others, attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Those who had not yet resolved their minds either generated the aspiration for unsurpassed bodhi, or for pratyekabuddhahood, or for śrāvakahood.
At that moment, Śakra Devendra’s fear was immediately dispelled; his lifespan increased by a thousand years, and he attained the fruit of srotāpanna.

“Good son! By means of his supernatural powers, Śākyamuni Tathāgata is able to produce such vast and boundless sounds of Dharma teaching; it is likewise so that not a single person can fathom the limits of that Buddha’s voice. That Buddha’s skillful means are immeasurable and boundless, and among the sentient beings he transforms, there is none who can fully know such skillful means.”
"Good son! That Buddha’s form-body is likewise immeasurable and boundless; no one is able to determine the dimensions of his body, nor can anyone see the crown of his head. Good son!"

In this way, if this great assembly should wish to enter into that Buddha’s belly, they would all be accommodated; yet once they have entered his belly, it would be impossible for anyone else to reach its edge, and even so, the Tathāgata’s belly neither increases nor decreases.

If all classes of sentient beings were to gather together and wish to pass through and come forth from a single pore, they would encounter no obstruction whatsoever; even with the divine eye, one could not find the edge of a single pore, yet that pore neither increases nor decreases. Such is the body of that Buddha, the World-Honored One—immeasurable and boundless.
“Good son! That Buddha-world is likewise immeasurable and boundless. Good son!”
Even if all sentient beings from worlds as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges Rivers were to enter such a world, they would still be able to find accommodation there. Why is this?
When that Buddha first resolved his mind upon Bodhi, the vows he made were immeasurable and boundless. Good son!

Setting aside the sentient beings of worlds as numerous as the sands of one Ganges River, even the sentient beings of worlds as numerous as the sands of a thousand Ganges Rivers throughout the ten directions could enter that world and be accommodated, without its original characteristics being increased or diminished.

"Good son! When Śākyamuni Tathāgata first resolved upon unsurpassed bodhicitta, he made a great vow because he desired to attain the perfection of all-knowledge; therefore, the world he has now attained is immeasurable and boundless."
“Good son! By means of these four dharmas, Śākyamuni is beyond the reach of all other Buddha-Bhagavāns. Good son!”
"Now, taking these Moonlight-Stainless-Pure Flowers, go to the western direction to the Sahā world as it appears before your eyes, and carrying my voice, inquire after that Buddha:
'Are you light in your movements and at ease? Are your physical strength and vitality secure?'"
At that time, the Buddha Vimalaguṇaprabhāsa-rāja took the moonlight-like stainless pure flower and, giving it to the two bodhisattvas, addressed them, saying:
"Now, by means of my great supernormal power, you shall go to that world."
At that time, twenty thousand bodhisattvas in the assembly addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is so! It is thus!”
"So be it! We shall now, by means of the Buddha’s spiritual power, go to that world to see Śākyamuni Tathāgata, and there offer him worship, reverence, respect, and praise."
That Buddha said to them:
"Sons of good family!
You should know that now is the time."

Then the two bodhisattvas, together with twenty thousand great beings, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, departed from the realm of Good Flowers; in the space of a single thought-moment, they suddenly arrived at Vulture Peak in this Sahā world and, kneeling before the Tathāgata with palms joined, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

To the east, eighty-nine billion Buddha-worlds away from here, there is a world named Good Flower (*Sukusuma*). In that world dwells a Buddha named King of Stainless Merit Radiance (*Vimalaguṇaprabhāsarāja*).
Now, currently surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others, he praises the immeasurable merits of the World-Honored One, speaking these words:
"In the Sahā world there is the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who now, for the sake of the great assembly, turns the wheel of the true Dharma."

When that Buddha, the World-Honored One, was a bodhisattva, he first exhorted and transformed me, causing me to resolve upon the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*). By virtue of these causes and conditions, I immediately thereafter attained the aspiration for the unsurpassed path. Once I had resolved my mind, he further exhorted me to cultivate and accumulate the six *pāramitās*. It was through these four dharmas that the Tathāgata acted—dharmas which no other Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, can equal.
"Therefore, that Buddha, with these moonlight-like, stainless, pure flowers, made an offering to the World-Honored One and inquired after the Tathāgata:
'Are you light and at ease in your daily life? Is your physical strength and vigor secure?'"

“Good son! At the lion throne where the Tathāgata Akṣobhya sits in the world-system of Wonderful Joy in the eastern direction, the earth likewise shook in six ways. When immeasurable great bodhisattvas saw this occurrence, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘World-Honored One!’”
"For what cause and condition does the place where the Tathāgata sits upon the lion throne tremble in this way?
As was said above, it was likewise so throughout the entire eastern direction.

At that time, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) great bodhisattvas from the eastern direction all arrived here in this Sahā world, each carrying moonlight-like, stainless, pure flowers; they beheld the Buddha, making offerings, paying homage, showing respect, and offering praise.
"Good son! In this way, immeasurable Buddhas in the eastern direction have all dispatched their bodhisattvas to praise me: 'Good son!'"

I now see that to the south of this world, passing through as many Buddha-lands as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world named Free from All Sorrow. In it dwells a Buddha named Aśokaguṇa Tathāgata, who is currently preaching the Dharma.
Furthermore, there is a world named Jambūprabha; in it dwells a Buddha named Dharmeśvarasiṃhavikrīḍita Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Anusumera; in it dwells a Buddha named Mārgaiśvarasālarāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named King of Merit Towers; therein dwells a Buddha named Lion’s Roar King Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Adorned with Jewels; therein dwells a Buddha named Eight-Armed Victorious Thunder Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named True Pearl Radiance Pervading Illumination; in it dwells a Buddha named Jewel-Treasury Merit Roar Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Celestial Moon; in it dwells a Buddha named Fire-Treasury Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Candanāmūla; therein dwells a Buddha named Jyotiṣprabha Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Gandhābhyudgata.
In that world there is a Buddha named Guṇabala-sālarāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Suśakha; in it there is a Buddha named Svaraviśeṣa-vaśavartin Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Śīrṣāranya; in it dwells a Buddha named Sāravijitvibhūrarāja Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Candrasvaramati; in it dwells a Buddha named Prabhāsasvaramati Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Good Thunder Sound; in it dwells a Buddha titled Wondrous Sound Sovereign Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Jewel Union; in it dwells a Buddha titled Jewel-Palm Dragon King Tathāgata.
Furthermore, there is a world named Hanging Jewel Trees; in it dwells a Buddha named Rain-Sound Sovereign Dharma-Moon Radiance Tathāgata.

In this same way, all the present Buddhas of the south—immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (asaṃkhyeya)—were all those whom I first inspired to resolve for bodhicitta when I was formerly a bodhisattva. The lion thrones of these World-Honored Ones also trembled, and those Buddhas likewise each praised my merits. They also dispatched immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable great bodhisattvas, who, carrying moonlight-like stainless pure flowers, have all come here to this Sahā world to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa. There they see the Buddha, prostrate, make offerings, pay homage, revere, and praise him, then sit to one side to listen to the Dharma in succession.

“Good son! I now further see, seventy-seven thousand times ten thousand *yojanas* to the west from here, a Buddha-world. There is a world there named ‘Tranquil,’ and within it is a Buddha named ‘Jewel Mountain,’ who currently dwells there preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the fourfold assembly.”
Furthermore, there were the Buddhas Prabhāsa-vimala, Ghoṣajñānagarbha, Yaśasviprabha, Samantagarbha,
Brahmakusuma-tejovikrama, Dharmapradīpa-vīra, Jayaghoṣaparvata, Yaśasvirāja, and Brahmaghoṣarāja;
such were the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable [Buddhas] of the western direction.
"O Buddha, World-Honored One, you were also the first among those whom I, while formerly a bodhisattva,
was able to inspire to resolve upon Bodhicitta. The lion-thrones of all those World-Honored Ones also shook,
and those Buddhas likewise each praised my merits and dispatched immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable [great beings]..."
The Bodhisattvas, holding moonlight-like stainless jewel-flowers, all came to this Sahā world to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa;
there they beheld the Buddha, prostrated, made offerings, paid homage, revered, honored, and praised him,
then withdrew to sit on one side to listen to the Dharma in succession.

"To the northeast, beyond a hundred thousand nayutas of Buddha-worlds from here, there is a world named Vimalā. In it dwells a Buddha named Vigatajvarapramardana-Vaiśravaṇasārarāja Tathāgata, who has two bodhisattvas: the first is named Ratnagiri, and the second is named Prabhādarśana."
Furthermore, there were the Buddhas Bhagnasarvamāra, Śālarāja, Mahābalaprabha, Padmottara, Candana, Merurāja, Sthirasāra, and Tejajñānamahābala.
"In this same way, there are immeasurable Buddhas, Tathāgatas, even in the north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—all are likewise.

At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, by means of his great supernormal power and desiring to accommodate such a multitude, immediately transformed the bodies of each and every person gathered there, making them extremely minute like *ting-li* seeds. The space and the earth of the Sahā world became completely filled and packed, with no empty space remaining even for a single hair.

At that time, all sentient beings could not see one another; nor did they see the great and small mountains, Sumeru, the king of mountains, or the dark and gloomy regions between the great and small Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa). They could not see the palaces of the various heavens above, nor the diamond foundation (vajra-maṇḍala) below, with the sole exception of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.

At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata again entered the samādhi of the "Universal Pervasion of Space and Severance of All Dharmas," causing these immeasurable pure moonlight flowers to enter all the pores of every body, such that the entire great assembly saw it for themselves.

At that time, sentient beings did not at all recollect the marks of the Buddha’s physical body; they saw only the pores, wherein there were wondrous gardens and groves. Within these gardens and groves were various jewel-trees, each with diverse trunks and leaves, and abounding with flowers and fruits. There were various precious robes, celestial banners, standards, canopies, heavenly crowns, jeweled ornaments, pearls, and necklaces—all such adornments were like those in the Western World of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
When this great assembly had witnessed these events, they further reflected:
"We should now go to visit and observe that garden.

At that time, with the exception of sentient beings in the three evil realms and the gods of the formless realm, all other members of the great assembly entered the body of the Tathāgata through his pores and sat within the garden.
At that time, the Tathāgata withdrew his supernormal power (*ṛddhi*), whereupon the great assembly each regained their original forms and beheld one another.
They said to one another: "Where is the Tathāgata now?"
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the great assembly:
"You should know this: I and all of you are now entirely within the body of the Tathāgata."

At that time, the great assembly immediately beheld the interior and exterior of the Tathāgata’s body; they then realized for themselves that they were gathered together with an immeasurable multitude within the body of the Tathāgata, and they said to one another: "From where did we enter?"
"Who will guide me and cause me to enter into this?
Maitreya Bodhisattva again addressed him, saying:
"Listen attentively!"
Listen attentively!

The Tathāgata now manifests the power of great supernormal transformations; furthermore, for the benefit of us, the great assembly, he is about to preach the Dharma. You, virtuous ones, should now focus your minds with single-minded devotion.
At that time, having heard these words, the great assembly knelt with palms joined and listened as they received the instruction.
Then, the World-Honored One expounded the Dharma through the gateway of all practices:
"What is called the gateway of all practices?
Emerging from the mire of birth and death, one enters the Eightfold Noble Path and fully accomplishes the attainment of all-knowledge.
Son of good family!
There are ten ways of single-mindedly aspiring to bodhi by which one can enter this gate.
What are these ten?
First, desiring that all sentient beings attain liberation through the dedication and sympathetic joy [of their merit];
second, giving rise to the mind of great compassion to gather in sentient beings;...
Third, desiring to deliver those not yet delivered, he diligently cultivates and repairs the unsurpassed Dharma-ship;
fourth, desiring to liberate those not yet liberated, he adorns himself by contemplating liberation from false and inverted views;
fifth, desiring the adornment of the fearless lion’s roar, he contemplates that the nature of all phenomena is selfless.
Sixth, they desire that their minds remain free from discrimination regarding all worlds they may reach, having skillfully studied all dharmas as being identical to the ten similes;
seventh, they desire to attain worlds adorned with radiance by cultivating and purifying the aggregate of ethical discipline;
eighth, they desire to accomplish the adornments of the Tathāgata’s ten powers by fulfilling all the pāramitās.
Ninth, they achieve the adornment of the four fearlessnesses by acting in accordance with what they have taught;
tenth, they adorn themselves with the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, for they attain all teachings they hear without exception, remaining ever heedful.

This is called the ten dharmas of single-minded devotion; by giving rise to unsurpassed bodhicitta, one is able to enter all these gates of practice. One then attains the non-regressive stage of unsurpassed bodhi, the gate of signless practice, and the gate of practice on the path of wisdom. Regarding all phenomena, there is no self and no conceptualization; they are neither arising nor ceasing. This is called the Bodhisattva’s stage of non-retrogression.
"For this reason, it is neither regressive nor non-regressive, neither annihilated nor eternal, neither fixed nor distracted.

When this Dharma was spoken, eighty billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, within the Tathāgata’s abdomen attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Furthermore, incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attained various *samādhis* and the profound *dharmanidhyāna-kṣānti*. They all emerged from the pores of the Tathāgata’s body, their hearts filled with great wonder and marveling at such an unprecedented occurrence.

Thereupon, before the Buddha, they prostrated themselves with their heads touching the ground in homage to the Buddha; having risen, they suddenly each returned to their own original Buddha-worlds in the ten directions. Furthermore, they heard the sound of the teachings expounded by Śākyamuni Tathāgata passing through the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddha-worlds of the ten directions without any obstruction.

Although these bodhisattvas have returned to their respective realms, they continue to hear the sounds and teachings expounded by the Tathāgata; the phrasing, meaning, and flavor are not diminished in the least, being no different from when they were listening closely in the presence of the Buddha.
The body is likewise so, pervading the immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions.
There are also immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) bodhisattvas and śrāvakas who likewise see [the Buddha] entering and exiting his pores without obstruction.
In this manner, the second [pore], and so on up to every single pore, allowed him to enter and exit without obstruction; it was likewise for all the worlds of the ten directions.

At that time, the great assembly emerged from the pores of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, prostrated with their heads at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood before the Buddha, praising him with various sounds and voices.

At that time, the devas of the desire realm and the form realm rained down various kinds of flowers, ointments, powdered incense, banners, streamers, and necklaces, and offered exquisite music as an offering to the Tathāgata.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Fearless Grounds (Abhayabhūmi). Kneeling with palms joined, he stepped forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, what should this great sūtra be called?”
"How should it be upheld?
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Fearless Ground:

"This sutra shall be named 'The Door of Dharanis for Understanding All,' and also named 'Immeasurable Buddhas,' and also named 'The Great Assembly,' and also named 'Bestowing Predictions upon Bodhisattvas,' and also named 'The Manifestation of the Four Fearlessnesses in the World,' and also named 'All Gateways to Samadhi,' and also named 'Manifesting the Worlds of All Buddhas,' and also named 'Like the Great Ocean,' and also named 'Immeasurable,' and also named 'The Lotus of Great Compassion.'"
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Abhayābhūmi again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are good sons or good daughters who receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this sutra, and explain it to others—even if only a single verse—how much merit will they obtain?”
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Fearless Ground:
"I have already previously explained the merit obtained; now I shall further explain it to you in brief.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, upholds, reads, recites, and masters this sutra, and explains it to others—even if only a single verse—and if, during the final five hundred years, there is anyone capable of writing down even a single verse, the merit they obtain will surpass that of all Bodhisattvas practicing the six *pāramitās* for ten great eons."

Why is this? Because all gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, nāgas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, humans, and non-humans who possess minds of anger, upon hearing this sutra, immediately attain purity, gentleness, and joy; they are freed from all illnesses, wrath, enmity, and strife, and all violent winds and evil rains are extinguished. Those who are ill are healed, those who are hungry and thirsty are satisfied, and they experience all manner of happiness, living in harmony and mutual accord.
It can cause those who harbor anger to practice patience;
it enables those who are fearful to be free from fear and to experience all manner of joy.

It causes those with afflictions to be free from them, and it can cause all roots of goodness to increase. It can uproot sentient beings from the evil realms, show the path of deliverance for the three vehicles, and enable the attainment of the profound dharma-patience, samādhi, and dhāraṇī gates. It can bring great benefit to sentient beings, lead one to sit upon the vajra-seat at the site of enlightenment, destroy the four māras, demonstrate all factors conducive to bodhi, and turn the wheel of Dharma.
Those who lack the noble wealth shall be brought to its full possession; they shall lead immeasurable and boundless sentient beings into the city of fearlessness.

By these causes and conditions, one who can uphold this sutra, read and recite it with mastery, and explain it to others—even if only a single verse—should they do so during the final age of five hundred years, or even if they can merely transcribe a single verse, shall obtain such an immeasurable and boundless accumulation of merit.
Therefore, as I now preach such a sutra, to whom should this great scripture be entrusted?
Who will be able to protect and uphold this Dharma during the final fifty years?
Who is able to proclaim and cause those non-regressing bodhisattvas, wherever they may be, to hear this?

And who else is able to disseminate this teaching for those who practice what is contrary to the Dharma, who desire evil, who are greedy and hold wrong views, and who do not believe in the existence of karmic retribution for good and evil?
At that time, the great assembly all knew the Buddha’s mind.
Then there was a great seer-yakṣa named Aśoka-tiṣya, who sat among the assembly.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya rose from his seat and led the yakṣa to the place where the Buddha was.
Then the Tathāgata addressed the yakṣa, the great seer:

"You should now receive this sutra and, until the final fifty years of the age, propagate this teaching for the sake of non-retrogressive bodhisattvas, and even for those who do not believe in the retribution of good and evil."
At that time, the yakṣa addressed the Buddha, saying:

“During eighty-four great kalpas in the past, by virtue of my original vow, I became a rishi-yakṣa and practiced for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. At that time, I taught and transformed immeasurable, boundless, asaṃkhyeya persons, establishing them in the four immeasurable minds (catur-apramāṇa), and further caused immeasurable, boundless sentient beings not to regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
World-Honored One!

For the sake of providing protection for all sentient beings in future ages, during the final fifty years of the latter dharma period, I shall receive and uphold this sutra; even if I hear only a four-line verse from another, I shall certainly read and recite it until I have mastered it thoroughly, and I shall disseminate it to others so that it shall never be interrupted.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Bodhisattva Silent Mind (Śāntamati), the great assembly of devas, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans, were all greatly rejoiced. They prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet in homage, withdrew, and departed.

The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Scroll Ten: The King of Mountains of the Merit of Radiant Light, the Mountain King’s Servant, the Virtuous Moon Adornment, the Asura Naṅga-hūṃ, the Sovereign Appearance, and the Classic on Affliction.
